  • Oligo - Read 1: R2:1-10,R2:17-26,R2:33-42

docs.title: Library Structure
docs.text:
DNBelab C4 series single-cell technology encompasses three major omics platforms: scRNA-seq (transcriptome), scATAC-seq (chromatin accessibility), and scVDJ (immune repertoire). Each library features specialized physical architectures, adapter compositions, cell barcodes (CB), and unique molecular identifiers (UMI).

This document provides a comprehensive reference for physical library architectures, base coordinate intervals, invariant linker sequences, and --customize parameter configurations across all modalities.

docs.title: 1. scRNA-seq Library Structure
docs.text: DNBelab C4 single-cell RNA sequencing consists of two complementary libraries: the cDNA library and the Oligo library. The cDNA library captures transcript expression profiles, while the Oligo library records bead barcodes within droplets for cell calling and doublet discrimination.

docs.title: cDNA Library
docs.text:
The cDNA library quantifies gene expression profiles across single cells.

  • Read 1 (58 bp):
  • Linker 1 (Fixed linker 1, 6 bp): TCTGCG (1–6 bp, present in non-dark sequencing only)
  • Cell Barcode 1 (CB1, 10 bp): First cell barcode segment (Non-dark: 7–16 bp; Dark reaction: 1–10 bp)
  • Linker 2 (Fixed linker 2, 6 bp): CCTTCC (17–22 bp, present in non-dark sequencing only)
  • Cell Barcode 2 (CB2, 10 bp): Second cell barcode segment (Non-dark: 23–32 bp; Dark reaction: 11–20 bp)
  • Linker 3 (Fixed linker 3, 5 bp): CGATG (33–37 bp, present in non-dark sequencing only)
  • UMI (10 bp): Unique Molecular Identifier (Non-dark: 38–47 bp; Dark reaction: 21–30 bp)
  • PolyT capture region (11 bp): Anneals to the mRNA 3' poly(A) tail
  • Read 2 (100 bp): cDNA insert (transcript sequence, mapped to the reference genome)

docs.title: Oligo Library
docs.text: The Oligo library resolves bead barcodes co-encapsulated in droplets, distinguishing true single cells from multi-bead background droplets.

docs.title: Read 1 Structure (20–32 bp)
docs.text:
• Non-Dark Mode (32 bp):
  • Linker 1 (6 bp): TCTGCG (1–6 bp, fixed adapter skipped)
  • Cell Barcode 1 (CB1, 10 bp): First cell barcode segment (7–16 bp, extracted as cb,R1:7-16)
  • Linker 2 (6 bp): CCTTCC (17–22 bp, fixed adapter skipped)
  • Cell Barcode 2 (CB2, 10 bp): Second cell barcode segment (23–32 bp, extracted as cb,R1:23-32)
  • Dark Reaction Mode (20 bp):
  • The sequencer hardware skips fixed Linker 1 and Linker 2:
  • Cell Barcode 1 (CB1, 10 bp): 1–10 bp, extracted as cb,R1:1-10
  • Cell Barcode 2 (CB2, 10 bp): 11–20 bp, extracted as cb,R1:11-20

docs.title: Read 2 Structure (30–42 bp)
docs.text:
• Non-Dark Mode (42 bp):
  • UMI (10 bp): Molecular unique identifier (1–10 bp, extracted as R1,R2:1-10)
  • Linker 1 (6 bp): TCTGCG (11–16 bp, fixed adapter skipped)
  • Tag 1 (10 bp): First bead carrier tag (17–26 bp, extracted as R1,R2:17-26)
  • Linker 2 (6 bp): CCTTCC (27–32 bp, fixed adapter skipped)
  • Tag 2 (10 bp): Second bead carrier tag (33–42 bp, extracted as R1,R2:33-42)
  • Dark Reaction Mode (30 bp):
  • The sequencer hardware skips fixed Linker 1 and Linker 2:
  • UMI (10 bp): 1–10 bp, extracted as R1,R2:1-10
  • Tag 1 (10 bp): 11–20 bp, extracted as R1,R2:11-20
  • Tag 2 (10 bp): 21–30 bp, extracted as R1,R2:21-30

For detailed scRNA command arguments, see scRNA Parameters: Custom Read Structure.

docs.title: 2. scATAC-seq Library Structure
docs.text: DNBelab C4 single-cell ATAC sequencing profiles accessible chromatin landscapes. ATAC libraries do not contain UMIs; fragment deduplication and quantification rely on mapped genomic coordinates (cut sites) together with cell barcodes.

docs.title: Read 1 Structure (50–115 bp)
docs.text:
• Non-dark reaction mode (115 bp):
  • Linker 1 (6 bp): TCTGCG (1–6 bp, fixed linker skipped)
  • Cell Barcode 1 (CB1, 10 bp): First barcode segment (7–16 bp, extracted as cb,R1:7-16)
  • Linker 2 (6 bp): CCTTCC (17–22 bp, fixed linker skipped)
  • Cell Barcode 2 (CB2, 10 bp): Second barcode segment (23–32 bp, extracted as cb,R1:23-32)
  • Adapter extension (33 bp): 33–65 bp, invariant adapter extension (skipped)
  • Chromatin DNA insert 1 (50 bp): 66–115 bp, genomic DNA insert (extracted as R1,R1:66-115)
  • Dark reaction mode (70 bp):
  • Sequencer hardware skips Linker 1, Linker 2, and the adapter extension:
  • Cell Barcode 1 (CB1, 10 bp): 1–10 bp, extracted as cb,R1:1-10
  • Cell Barcode 2 (CB2, 10 bp): 11–20 bp, extracted as cb,R1:11-20
  • Chromatin DNA insert 1 (50 bp): 21–70 bp, extracted as R1,R1:21-70

docs.title: Read 2 Structure (50–69 bp)
docs.text:
• Non-dark reaction mode (69 bp):
  • Fixed adapter (19 bp): 1–19 bp (invariant adapter skipped)
  • Chromatin DNA insert 2 (50 bp): 20–69 bp, genomic DNA insert (extracted as R2,R2:20-69)
  • Dark reaction mode (50 bp):
  • Sequencer hardware skips the 19 bp fixed adapter:
  • Chromatin DNA insert 2 (50 bp): 1–50 bp, pure genomic DNA sequence (extracted as R2,R2:1-50)

For scATAC parameter configurations and dark reaction options, see scATAC Parameters: Dark Reaction & Customization.

docs.title: 3. scVDJ Immune Repertoire Library Structure
docs.text: DNBelab C4 single-cell V(D)J sequencing utilizes 5' transcript barcoding combined with nested PCR target enrichment for TCR (TRA/TRB/TRD/TRG) and BCR (IGH/IGK/IGL) transcripts, enabling high-fidelity full-length contig assembly and clonotype identification.

docs.title: Read 1 Structure (100–150 bp)
docs.text:
• Non-dark reaction mode (120–150 bp):
  • Linker 1 (6 bp): TCTGCG (1–6 bp, fixed linker skipped)
  • Cell Barcode 1 (CB1, 10 bp): First barcode segment (7–16 bp, extracted as cb,R1:7-16)
  • Linker 2 (6 bp): CCTTCC (17–22 bp, fixed linker skipped)
  • Cell Barcode 2 (CB2, 10 bp): Second barcode segment (23–32 bp, extracted as cb,R1:23-32)
  • Linker 3 (5 bp): CGATG (33–37 bp, fixed linker skipped)
  • UMI (10 bp): Unique Molecular Identifier (38–47 bp, extracted as umi,R1:38-47)
  • TSO / Extension (13 bp): 48–60 bp, Template Switch Oligo sequence (skipped)
  • V(D)J 5' transcript sequence (60+ bp): 61–120+ bp, extracted as R1,R1:61-120
  • Dark reaction mode (120 bp):
  • Sequencer hardware skips fixed linkers and TSO:
  • Cell Barcode 1 (CB1, 10 bp): 1–10 bp, extracted as cb,R1:1-10
  • Cell Barcode 2 (CB2, 10 bp): 11–20 bp, extracted as cb,R1:11-20
  • UMI (10 bp): 21–30 bp, extracted as umi,R1:21-30
  • V(D)J 5' transcript sequence (90+ bp): 31–120+ bp, extracted as R1,R1:31-120

docs.title: Read 2 Structure (100–150 bp)
docs.text:
• Standard reverse transcript sequencing (1–150 bp):
  • Read 2 always reads target transcript sequence starting from base 1 (derived from C-region specific primer extension, covering CDR3 and rearranged V/D/J elements), extracted as R2,R2:1-150.
  • Note: scVDJ sequencing supports R1 dark reaction or non-dark mode only. Read 2 dark reaction is neither supported nor required.

For scVDJ parameter options and custom structure syntax, see scVDJ Parameters: Dark Reaction & Custom Read Structure.

docs.title: Upgrading from 3.1 to 3.2
docs.text: This document summarizes the major new features, algorithmic optimizations, and output file changes in DNBelab C Series™ HT Single-Cell Analysis Software (dnbc4tools) between versions 3.1 and 3.2. Use the version switcher in the header to view the archived 3.1 documentation.

docs.title: Major New Feature: C6 Multiplexed scRNA Analysis
docs.text:
Version 3.2 introduces native support for C6 Multiplexed scRNA Analysis, enabling pooled multiplexed sequencing and Sample Barcode demultiplexing within a single library:

  • Configuration and Execution: Declare sample names and associated Sample Barcodes in the [samples] section of the multi run configuration. The software automatically detects and runs the C6 multiplexed pipeline without requiring manual chemistry flags.
  • Pooled and Per-Sample Expression Matrices:
    • Complete gene expression matrices are generated for both the pooled library (in the root output directory) and for each demultiplexed sample (under per_sample_outs/<sample>/), provided concurrently in MEX directory, standard H5, and H5AD formats;
    • Each sample delivers a sample-specific interactive HTML QC and analysis report (per_sample_outs/<sample>/<sample>_scRNA_report.html).
  • Sample-Specific BAM Outputs:
    • By default, generates aligned BAM files for each individual sample (per_sample_outs/<sample>/<sample>_alignments.bam with index), facilitating sample-specific IGV visualization and variant detection;
    • When [rna] no_bam is false (the default), reads not uniquely assignable to any sample barcode are collected in unassigned_alignments.bam. Setting no_bam,true omits all BAM files and their indexes, including per-sample, unassigned, and oligo BAM outputs.
  • Independent Dual-UMI Correction: Independently corrects and deduplicates both UMI segments for C6 dual-UMI architectures, for subsequent molecule counting.

docs.title: 1. Single-Cell RNA (scRNA)
docs.text:
• Optimized Intra-Cell Multi-Gene Duplicate UMI Resolution:
    • Version 3.1 already supported this filtering mechanism, but had boundary condition defects. Version 3.2 resolves these defects and optimizes conflict resolution: when a UMI within a cell maps to multiple genes, it is assigned to the dominant gene with strictly higher read counts; if read counts tie, the ambiguous molecule is removed and excluded from gene expression counts.
  • Bound Safeguards for Automatic Cell Calling:
    • Version 3.1 lacked explicit upper and lower bounds for automatic cell number prediction. Version 3.2 introduces automatic prediction bound constraints, to constrain the estimated cell count; assess the resulting cell calls alongside sample QC metrics.
  • Oligo Read 2 Filtering Optimization to Minimize Data Discard:
    • Updates quality control, barcode correction, and filtering rules for barcode and structural sequences in Oligo Read 2.

docs.title: 2. Dual-Species Mixed Classification Algorithm Upgrade
docs.text:
• Bidirectional Background Prediction Bands:
    • Updates the mixed-species classification model (e.g. human-mouse), replacing legacy rigid cutoffs (such as fixed 1,000 UMI / 90% purity rules and empirical quantiles) with empirical bidirectional continuous prediction band models;
    • Employs two-stage robust Huber regression to independently model cross-species background leakage and observation variance between host and secondary species, to assess cell species assignments;
    • Incorporates bead-aware modeling for ATAC species assignment, jointly modeling merged bead counts (N1, N2...) alongside chromatin accessibility depth to distinguish cross-species multiplets from deeply sequenced single cells.

docs.title: 3. Single-Cell ATAC (scATAC)
docs.text:
• Cutsite-Based Quantification for Peaks and Matrices:
    • What is a cutsite? In ATAC-seq, Tn5 transposase binds open chromatin and cleaves the DNA double helix while inserting sequencing adapters, introducing a characteristic 9-bp staggered cut. Cutsite mode counts the actual Tn5 insertion cleavage endpoints after 9-bp offset adjustment. Cutsite mode counts cleavage endpoints, whereas fragment mode counts sequencing fragments; the counting units differ.
    • Metric Semantics: Peak calling and matrix counts default to cutsite quantification; key QC metrics—including FRIP (Fraction of Reads in Peaks), TSS enrichment fraction, and Cell Calling—remain strictly evaluated on deduplicated unique fragments.

docs.title: 4. Single-Cell V(D)J (scVDJ)
docs.text:
• Updates chain pairing and full-length contig assembly logic.
  • Updates deterministic handling of multi-threaded sampling. Keep inputs, parameters, and the software environment consistent when comparing runs.

docs.title: Changes Requiring Adaptation from 3.1
docs.text: The table below covers changes to existing 3.1 workflows. C6 is new in 3.2 and has no equivalent 3.1 output layout. Its per-sample results are under outs/rna/per_sample_outs/<sample>/, and pooled matrices are under outs/rna/. The new C6 detail table is outs/rna/singlecell.csv.gz; read it with gzip support and use is_cell_barcode to select called cells.

docs.title: Output Directory & File Format Changes
docs.text: Change Item Version 3.1 Version 3.2 Migration Action RNA Matrix Directories raw_matrix/filter_matrix/ raw_feature_bc_matrix/filtered_feature_bc_matrix/ Aligned with standard 10X directory naming; companion .h5 files added for single-file loading. ATAC Matrix Directories raw_peak_matrix/filter_peak_matrix/ raw_peak_bc_matrix/filtered_peak_bc_matrix/ Standardized directory naming; companion .h5 files added. ATAC Text Matrix matrix.mtx.gz tab-separated matrix.mtx.gz single-space separated Update custom scripts to split on whitespace (line.split()) or use standard MatrixMarket readers. Batch Analysis Scripts Written to output directory Generated only in the current working directory Run scripts from the current directory; --outdir sets analysis output; existing scripts are not overwritten.

docs.title: Quick Start Guide
docs.text: This guide provides end-to-end operational walkthroughs for the DNBelab C Series™ single-cell analysis suite (dnbc4tools), covering system prerequisites, reference genome indexing, single-modality pipelines, integrated multi-omics orchestration, C6 multiplexed single-cell RNA analysis, and batch analysis script generation.

docs.title: Choose a Workflow
docs.text:
Select the appropriate command entry point according to your experimental design and library preparation:

Workflow Command Entry Point Scope & Description Single-Cell RNA Analysis dnbc4tools rna run Single-sample gene expression quantification, EmptyDrops cell calling, and clustering Single-Cell ATAC Analysis dnbc4tools atac run Single-sample chromatin accessibility analysis, peak calling, and QC Single-Cell V(D)J Analysis dnbc4tools vdj run De novo assembly of full-length TCR / BCR sequences, annotation, and clonotype identification Integrated Multi-Omics dnbc4tools multi run --csv multi.config.csv Unified orchestration and cross-modality reporting for RNA + ATAC + VDJ C6 Multiplexed RNA dnbc4tools multi run --csv sample.config.csv Sample Barcode pooled RNA-seq demultiplexing and per-sample dedicated delivery Batch Script Generation dnbc4tools <rna/atac> multi Batch-generate standalone analysis scripts for queued HPC scheduling

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Before you begin:

  • Environment & Paths: Ensure software installation is verified (see Installation Guide). Replace placeholder paths like $dnbc4tools, /test/data/..., and /database/... with actual paths on your system.
  • Output Directory: By default, a task directory named after --name is created under the current working directory (results saved in ./<name>/outs/). You can also explicitly specify a custom output root via --outdir.

docs.title: --fastqs Directory Auto-Detection Rules
docs.text:
When using directory-based input via --fastqs <dir>, the pipeline automatically scans the folder and pairs paired-end reads matching the following patterns:

Read End Match Pattern Example Filenames Read 1 (R1) Contains _R1_, _R1, _1, or _read1 sample_R1.fastq.gz, sample_1.fq.gz, sample_R1_001.fastq.gz Read 2 (R2) Contains _R2_, _R2, _2, or _read2 sample_R2.fastq.gz, sample_2.fq.gz, sample_R2_001.fastq.gz
  • Supported Extensions: .fastq.gz, .fq.gz, .fastq, .fq
  • Explicit File Arguments Bypass Naming Restrictions: If files are provided via explicit flags (e.g., --fastq1/--fastq2 or RNA --cDNAfastq1/2, --oligofastq1/2), file names do not need to follow these patterns, but the list ordering between paired reads must match strictly.

docs.title: Single-Cell RNA Analysis
docs.text: Designed for standard single-sample 3′ or 5′ single-cell transcriptomic profiling and clustering.

docs.title: Step 1: Build Reference Genome
docs.text:
If a compatible reference is already available, skip rebuilding and use its complete directory in the run command. Choose the appropriate species example below and run it in a separate working directory. mkref --genomeDir /database/scRNA specifies the reference output root; the software adds a species subdirectory, producing /database/scRNA/Homo_sapiens, /database/scRNA/Mus_musculus, or /database/scRNA/hg38_and_mm10. Pass that species directory to run --genomeDir, not the output root or an original FASTA/GTF file. For the mixed-species example, prepare the two filtered GTF files at the indicated hg38/ and mm10/ paths first.

Using Human, Mouse, and Human-Mouse dual-species as common references:

Human (GRCh38) 

# 1. Download GENCODE annotation and genomic FASTA
wget http://ftp.ebi.ac.uk/pub/databases/gencode/Gencode_human/release_32/GRCh38.primary_assembly.genome.fa.gz
wget http://ftp.ebi.ac.uk/pub/databases/gencode/Gencode_human/release_32/gencode.v32.primary_assembly.annotation.gtf.gz

# 2. Decompress files
gzip -d GRCh38.primary_assembly.genome.fa.gz
gzip -d gencode.v32.primary_assembly.annotation.gtf.gz

# 3. Filter GTF and generate STAR genome index
$dnbc4tools tools mkgtf --ingtf gencode.v32.primary_assembly.annotation.gtf --output genes.filtered.gtf
$dnbc4tools rna mkref --genomeDir /database/scRNA --ingtf genes.filtered.gtf --fasta GRCh38.primary_assembly.genome.fa --threads 10 --species Homo_sapiens

Mouse (Mus musculus, GRCm38) 

# 1. Download annotation and FASTA
wget http://ftp.ebi.ac.uk/pub/databases/gencode/Gencode_mouse/release_M23/GRCm38.primary_assembly.genome.fa.gz
wget http://ftp.ebi.ac.uk/pub/databases/gencode/Gencode_mouse/release_M23/gencode.vM23.primary_assembly.annotation.gtf.gz

# 2. Decompress files
gzip -d GRCm38.primary_assembly.genome.fa.gz
gzip -d gencode.vM23.primary_assembly.annotation.gtf.gz

# 3. Filter GTF and generate STAR genome index
$dnbc4tools tools mkgtf --ingtf gencode.vM23.primary_assembly.annotation.gtf --output genes.filtered.gtf
$dnbc4tools rna mkref --genomeDir /database/scRNA --ingtf genes.filtered.gtf --fasta GRCm38.primary_assembly.genome.fa --threads 10 --species Mus_musculus

Human-Mouse Mixed-Species Reference 

# Combine FASTA and GTF after preparing both species
$dnbc4tools rna mkref --genomeDir /database/scRNA \
    --fasta GRCh38.primary_assembly.genome.fa,GRCm38.primary_assembly.genome.fa \
    --ingtf hg38/genes.filtered.gtf,mm10/genes.filtered.gtf \
    --species hg38,mm10 \
    --threads 10

docs.title: Step 2: Prepare RNA Sequencing Data
docs.text:
Organize your sequencing files under structured subdirectories containing cDNA/ and oligo/. The pipeline will automatically identify and pair FASTQ files:

/test/data/rna_fastqs/          # Root directory passed to --fastqs
├── cDNA/                       # Transcriptomic cDNA sequencing reads
│   ├── sample_cDNA_R1.fastq.gz
│   └── sample_cDNA_R2.fastq.gz
└── oligo/                      # Bead/barcode Oligo sequencing reads
    ├── sample_oligo_R1.fastq.gz
    └── sample_oligo_R2.fastq.gz

--fastqs points to the root containing both cDNA/ and oligo/; all four paired input streams are required for this standard example. Keep data from one sample/library in the directory. Multiple files from the same library may be placed in the corresponding subdirectories, with compatible read structures and dark-cycle settings. Do not mix unrelated samples. See the filename pairing rules.

docs.title: Step 3: Run RNA Analysis
docs.text:
Method 1: Directory Input (Recommended)

$dnbc4tools rna run \
    --fastqs /test/data/rna_fastqs \
    --genomeDir /database/scRNA/Homo_sapiens \
    --name test_rna \
    --threads 30

Method 2: Explicit Individual FASTQ Inputs

When sequencing files are not grouped into cDNA/ and oligo/ subdirectories, or are distributed across separate storage paths, specify each input file explicitly using dedicated arguments (comma-separated lists supported):

$dnbc4tools rna run \
    --cDNAfastq1 /test/data/rna_fastqs/cDNA/sample_cDNA_R1.fastq.gz \
    --cDNAfastq2 /test/data/rna_fastqs/cDNA/sample_cDNA_R2.fastq.gz \
    --oligofastq1 /test/data/rna_fastqs/oligo/sample_oligo_R1.fastq.gz \
    --oligofastq2 /test/data/rna_fastqs/oligo/sample_oligo_R2.fastq.gz \
    --genomeDir /database/scRNA/Homo_sapiens \
    --name test_rna \
    --threads 30

Choose one input method; do not combine --fastqs with explicit FASTQ arguments. --name test_rna names the run and report, results are stored in ./test_rna/outs/ (use --outdir to customize the root), and --threads sets the CPU thread count. Explicit R1/R2 lists must match in order.

For 5′ RNA, add --end5 to the chosen run command; leave it off for the 3′ example. BAM output is enabled by default. Add the flag --no_bam to omit BAM files and their indexes when saving storage. Further cell-calling and library options are described in RNA parameters.

docs.title: Step 4: Inspect RNA Outputs
docs.text:
Upon completion, results are stored in ./test_rna/outs/:

  • Interactive Report: Open test_rna_scRNA_report.html in a web browser to review cell counts, sequencing QC, gene expression, and clustering charts;
  • Quantification Matrices: Standard MEX directory, .h5, and AnnData .h5ad formats (located in filtered_feature_bc_matrix/ and analysis/QC_Cluster.h5ad);
  • QC & Single-Cell Metadata: singlecell.csv (bead/droplet metrics; filter cells via is_cell_barcode == 1) and metrics_summary.xls.

For the complete directory structure, metric explanations, and programmatic loading examples, see scRNA Output Details and Reading Results in R / Python.

docs.title: Single-Cell ATAC Analysis
docs.text: Designed for single-cell chromatin accessibility analysis, peak calling, and quality control.

docs.title: Step 1: Build ATAC Reference
docs.text:
If a compatible reference is already available, skip rebuilding and use its complete directory in the run command. Choose the appropriate species example below and run it in a separate working directory. mkref --genomeDir /database/scATAC specifies the reference output root; the software adds a species subdirectory, producing /database/scATAC/Homo_sapiens, /database/scATAC/Mus_musculus, or /database/scATAC/hg38_and_mm10. Pass that species directory to run --genomeDir, not the output root or an original FASTA/GTF file. For the mixed-species example, prepare the two filtered GTF files at the indicated hg38/ and mm10/ paths first.

Human (GRCh38) 

# 1. Download GENCODE annotation and genomic FASTA
wget http://ftp.ebi.ac.uk/pub/databases/gencode/Gencode_human/release_32/GRCh38.primary_assembly.genome.fa.gz
wget http://ftp.ebi.ac.uk/pub/databases/gencode/Gencode_human/release_32/gencode.v32.primary_assembly.annotation.gtf.gz

# 2. Decompress files
gzip -d GRCh38.primary_assembly.genome.fa.gz
gzip -d gencode.v32.primary_assembly.annotation.gtf.gz

# 3. Filter GTF and build Chromap reference index
$dnbc4tools tools mkgtf --ingtf gencode.v32.primary_assembly.annotation.gtf --output genes.filtered.gtf
$dnbc4tools atac mkref --genomeDir /database/scATAC --fasta GRCh38.primary_assembly.genome.fa --ingtf genes.filtered.gtf --species Homo_sapiens --prefix chr

Mouse (Mus musculus, GRCm38) 

# 1. Download annotation and FASTA
wget http://ftp.ebi.ac.uk/pub/databases/gencode/Gencode_mouse/release_M23/GRCm38.primary_assembly.genome.fa.gz
wget http://ftp.ebi.ac.uk/pub/databases/gencode/Gencode_mouse/release_M23/gencode.vM23.primary_assembly.annotation.gtf.gz

# 2. Decompress files
gzip -d GRCm38.primary_assembly.genome.fa.gz
gzip -d gencode.vM23.primary_assembly.annotation.gtf.gz

# 3. Filter GTF and build Chromap reference index
$dnbc4tools tools mkgtf --ingtf gencode.vM23.primary_assembly.annotation.gtf --output genes.filtered.gtf
$dnbc4tools atac mkref --genomeDir /database/scATAC --fasta GRCm38.primary_assembly.genome.fa --ingtf genes.filtered.gtf --species Mus_musculus --prefix chr

Human-Mouse Mixed-Species Reference 

# Combine FASTA and filtered GTF after preparing both species (--prefix is not supported for mixed-species)
$dnbc4tools atac mkref --genomeDir /database/scATAC \
    --fasta GRCh38.primary_assembly.genome.fa,GRCm38.primary_assembly.genome.fa \
    --ingtf hg38/genes.filtered.gtf,mm10/genes.filtered.gtf \
    --species hg38,mm10

docs.title: Step 2: Prepare ATAC Sequencing Data
docs.text:
Place sequencing files in a designated folder or provide paired-end files explicitly:

/test/data/atac_fastqs/          # Root directory passed to --fastqs
├── sample_R1.fastq.gz
└── sample_R2.fastq.gz

--fastqs points directly to the directory containing this ATAC library's paired FASTQs; no cDNA/ or oligo/ layout is needed. Keep unrelated samples separate. Multiple files from one library must have matching paired-file names and compatible read structures and dark-cycle settings; see the filename pairing rules.

docs.title: Step 3: Run ATAC Analysis
docs.text:
Method 1: Directory Input (Recommended)

$dnbc4tools atac run \
    --fastqs /test/data/atac_fastqs \
    --genomeDir /database/scATAC/Homo_sapiens \
    --name test_atac \
    --threads 10

Method 2: Explicit Individual FASTQ Inputs

$dnbc4tools atac run \
    --fastq1 /test/data/atac_fastqs/sample_R1.fastq.gz \
    --fastq2 /test/data/atac_fastqs/sample_R2.fastq.gz \
    --genomeDir /database/scATAC/Homo_sapiens \
    --name test_atac \
    --threads 10

Choose one input method; do not combine --fastqs with explicit FASTQ arguments. --name test_atac names the run and report, results are stored in ./test_atac/outs/ (use --outdir to customize the root), and --threads sets the CPU thread count. Explicit R1/R2 lists must match in order.

The reference must be an ATAC reference built with atac mkref; an RNA STAR reference is not interchangeable. BAM output requires --need_bam. See ATAC parameters for cell-calling and peak-calling settings.

docs.title: Step 4: Inspect ATAC Outputs
docs.text:
Upon completion, results are stored in ./test_atac/outs/:

  • Interactive Report: Open test_atac_scATAC_report.html in a web browser to review cell calling counts, TSS enrichment curves, and FRIP QC metrics;
  • Peak Count Matrices: MEX directory (filtered_peak_bc_matrix/) and .h5 file based on 9-bp shifted cutsite quantification;
  • Fragment Files: fragments.tsv.gz and filtered.fragments.tsv.gz (both indexed with .tbi, ready for ArchR / Signac / SnapATAC2).

For the complete directory layout, field descriptions, and downstream analysis workflows, see scATAC Output Details and Reading Results in R / Python.

docs.title: Single-Cell V(D)J Analysis
docs.text:
Designed for de novo assembly of full-length TCR / BCR immune receptor sequences, annotation, and clonotype identification.

VDJ modes: Two modes are supported: provide --beadstrans to use an RNA cell table for bead mapping and RNA-based cell filtering; or omit it to run VDJ without an RNA cell table. When omitted, keep_all_cells is enabled automatically, so assembled barcodes are not filtered by RNA cell calls and must not be treated as an RNA-confirmed cell set.

The following steps demonstrate RNA-associated VDJ analysis. An existing cell table can be reused, so RNA does not need to be rerun solely for this example.

docs.title: Step 1: Prepare VDJ Data and Reference
docs.text:
Keep TCR and BCR libraries in separate directories, matching the commands below:

/test/data/
├── tcr_fastqs/
│   ├── sample_TCR_R1.fastq.gz
│   └── sample_TCR_R2.fastq.gz
└── bcr_fastqs/
    ├── sample_BCR_R1.fastq.gz
    └── sample_BCR_R2.fastq.gz
Parameter or input Description --fastqs Directory of paired FASTQs for the TCR or BCR library; keep the two library types separate. Alternatively, use --fastq1 and --fastq2 with matching paired-file order. --ref Use human or mouse for these species. These are software reference identifiers, not paths. For a custom reference, supply a VDJ reference directory containing reference.json, not a FASTA file or RNA / ATAC reference directory. --chain Use TR for TCR or IG for BCR, matching the input library. --beadstrans For RNA-associated analysis, use the corresponding RNA outs/singlecell.csv from the same experiment, not an expression matrix, barcodes.tsv.gz, or another sample's cell table. Omit this option for analysis without RNA.

Replace the /test/data/... placeholders with actual paths. See the input naming rules and VDJ parameters for custom reference requirements.

docs.title: Step 2: Prepare an RNA Cell Table (RNA-Associated Mode Only)
docs.text:
If the corresponding RNA singlecell.csv already exists, reuse it and skip this command. Otherwise, prepare the RNA FASTQs using the RNA input layout at /test/data/rna_5p_fastqs, then run the corresponding 5′ RNA data. For the mode without an RNA table, skip this step entirely.

$dnbc4tools rna run \
    --fastqs /test/data/rna_5p_fastqs \
    --genomeDir /database/scRNA/Homo_sapiens \
    --name test_rna_5p \
    --threads 30 \
    --end5

docs.title: Step 3: Run VDJ Analysis
docs.text:
For RNA-associated mode, the command above produces ./test_rna_5p/outs/singlecell.csv. Use this path with --beadstrans, or replace it with your existing corresponding cell table. Choose directory input or explicit files; do not combine them.

Method 1: Directory Input (Recommended)

Human TCR Analysis 

$dnbc4tools vdj run \
    --fastqs /test/data/tcr_fastqs \
    --beadstrans ./test_rna_5p/outs/singlecell.csv \
    --ref human \
    --name test_human_tcr \
    --threads 20 \
    --chain TR

Human BCR Analysis 

$dnbc4tools vdj run \
    --fastqs /test/data/bcr_fastqs \
    --beadstrans ./test_rna_5p/outs/singlecell.csv \
    --ref human \
    --name test_human_bcr \
    --threads 20 \
    --chain IG

Method 2: Explicit Individual FASTQ Inputs

When files are located in separate storage paths, provide them via --fastq1 and --fastq2:

Human TCR Analysis (Explicit Files) 

$dnbc4tools vdj run \
    --fastq1 /test/data/tcr_fastqs/sample_TCR_R1.fastq.gz \
    --fastq2 /test/data/tcr_fastqs/sample_TCR_R2.fastq.gz \
    --beadstrans ./test_rna_5p/outs/singlecell.csv \
    --ref human \
    --name test_human_tcr \
    --threads 20 \
    --chain TR

Human BCR Analysis (Explicit Files) 

$dnbc4tools vdj run \
    --fastq1 /test/data/bcr_fastqs/sample_BCR_R1.fastq.gz \
    --fastq2 /test/data/bcr_fastqs/sample_BCR_R2.fastq.gz \
    --beadstrans ./test_rna_5p/outs/singlecell.csv \
    --ref human \
    --name test_human_bcr \
    --threads 20 \
    --chain IG

Click to expand: Mouse TCR and BCR Analysis Examples

These examples assume the corresponding mouse RNA cell table already exists at ./test_mouse_rna_5p/outs/singlecell.csv. Replace it with your actual path; use mouse FASTQs, reference, and RNA cell table consistently.

Mouse TCR Analysis

$dnbc4tools vdj run \
    --fastqs /test/data/mouse_tcr_fastqs \
    --beadstrans ./test_mouse_rna_5p/outs/singlecell.csv \
    --ref mouse \
    --name test_mouse_tcr \
    --threads 20 \
    --chain TR

Mouse BCR Analysis

$dnbc4tools vdj run \
    --fastqs /test/data/mouse_bcr_fastqs \
    --beadstrans ./test_mouse_rna_5p/outs/singlecell.csv \
    --ref mouse \
    --name test_mouse_bcr \
    --threads 20 \
    --chain IG

docs.title: VDJ Without an RNA Cell Table
docs.text:
Omit --beadstrans; a preceding RNA run is not required for this mode. Other input and reference requirements remain the same.

$dnbc4tools vdj run \
    --fastqs /test/data/tcr_fastqs \
    --ref human \
    --name test_vdj_without_rna \
    --threads 20 \
    --chain TR

The software automatically enables keep_all_cells. Review the VDJ annotation flags before counting cells or comparing them with RNA results.

docs.title: Step 4: Inspect VDJ Outputs
docs.text:
Upon completion, results are stored in ./<name>/outs/ (e.g., ./test_human_tcr/outs/):

  • Interactive Report: Open *_report.html in a web browser to review assembly rates, productive contig proportions, and clonotype diversity distributions;
  • Assembly & Annotations: Primary filtered annotations in filtered_contig_annotations.csv and assembly sequences in filtered_contig.fasta;
  • Immune Repertoire Standards: Standard clonotypes.csv and airr_annotations.tsv (directly compatible with scRepertoire or immunarch).

For complete output files and annotation definitions, see scVDJ Output Details and Reading Results in R / Python.

docs.title: Integrated Multi-Omics Analysis
docs.text:
Use one configuration file to run RNA, ATAC, TCR, and BCR libraries and generate a combined report. The example below uses 5′ RNA + ATAC + TCR + BCR from one biological sample. Keep only the modalities available in your experiment; all four libraries are not required. Configure and run independent samples separately. For pooled C6 RNA libraries labeled with Sample Barcodes, use the C6 multiplexed workflow below.

Scope of integration

RNA and V(D)J can share cell information. ATAC is currently analyzed independently and summarized in the combined report. This command does not perform joint RNA + ATAC dimensionality reduction or clustering.

docs.title: Step 1: Prepare Sequencing Data and References
docs.text:
Place each library from the sample in its own directory, for example:

/test/data/
├── rna/
│   ├── cDNA/
│   │   ├── sample_cDNA_R1.fastq.gz
│   │   └── sample_cDNA_R2.fastq.gz
│   └── oligo/
│       ├── sample_oligo_R1.fastq.gz
│       └── sample_oligo_R2.fastq.gz
├── atac/
│   ├── sample_ATAC_R1.fastq.gz
│   └── sample_ATAC_R2.fastq.gz
├── vdj-t/
│   ├── sample_TCR_R1.fastq.gz
│   └── sample_TCR_R2.fastq.gz
└── vdj-b/
    ├── sample_BCR_R1.fastq.gz
    └── sample_BCR_R2.fastq.gz
  • RNA: Set fastqs to /test/data/rna, the root containing both cDNA/ and oligo/. Do not point it to cDNA/ alone or to an individual FASTQ file.
  • ATAC, TCR, and BCR: Provide the directory containing the paired FASTQs for each library. Keep TCR and BCR separate. See the automatic filename pairing rules.
  • Only one FASTQ root is supported per modality, and each modality may appear only once in [libraries]. If a library has multiple sequencing files, place matched R1/R2 files in the corresponding directory, with compatible read structures and dark-cycle settings. Do not include other samples or unrelated libraries.
  • RNA / ATAC references: Use reference directories already built with rna mkref and atac mkref, respectively. Do not supply a FASTA, GTF, or a directory containing only the original reference files. See the RNA and ATAC sections above for reference building.
  • VDJ reference: Use human or mouse for these species, or provide a custom VDJ reference directory containing reference.json. See the VDJ parameters.

The /test/data/... paths above and /database/... paths below are placeholders. Replace them with existing data and reference directories on your system before running.

docs.title: Step 2: Write the Multi-Omics Configuration
docs.text:
Save the following as a plain-text file named multi.config.csv. The configuration uses [sections] with comma-separated content: retain the header in [libraries], and use parameter,value rows in each modality section.

[libraries]
fastqs,feature_types
/test/data/rna,rna
/test/data/atac,atac
/test/data/vdj-t,vdj-t
/test/data/vdj-b,vdj-b

[rna]
genomeDir,/database/scRNA/Homo_sapiens
end5,true

[atac]
genomeDir,/database/scATAC/Homo_sapiens

[vdj-t]
ref,human

[vdj-b]
ref,human
Setting Meaning and value [libraries] fastqs FASTQ root for the library, following the layout above. [libraries] feature_types rna, atac, vdj-t (TCR), or vdj-b (BCR); must match the corresponding modality section. [rna] genomeDir / [atac] genomeDir Previously built reference directory for each modality; provide the RNA and ATAC references separately. [rna] end5,true Specifies 5′ RNA data in this example. For 3′ RNA, remove this line instead of copying the setting. [vdj-t] ref / [vdj-b] ref VDJ species identifier or custom reference directory; human in this example is a species identifier, not a file path.

Remove modalities you do not have: For RNA + TCR only, delete the atac and vdj-b rows from [libraries] and remove the entire [atac] and [vdj-b] sections. Declare only available libraries; do not leave empty paths. When 5′ RNA is enabled and its cell table is generated successfully, VDJ uses that table by default. You do not need to run RNA separately first or set beadstrans manually.

Path resolution: Relative paths inside the configuration are resolved against the directory containing multi.config.csv. Absolute paths are recommended for your first run. For example, if the CSV is /project/config/multi.config.csv, ../fastqs/rna resolves to /project/fastqs/rna. Relative --csv and --outdir command-line paths are resolved against the current working directory when you run the command.

For other modality parameters, Boolean values, and values containing commas, see the Multi parameters.

docs.title: Step 3: Run the Multi-Omics Analysis
docs.text:
Run this command from the directory containing multi.config.csv:

$dnbc4tools multi run \
    --name test_multi \
    --csv ./multi.config.csv \
    --threads 20

Here, --name test_multi sets the run name; by default, outputs are generated under ./test_multi/outs/ (use --outdir to specify another root directory); and --threads 20 sets the CPU thread count.

docs.title: Step 4: Inspect Multi-Omics Outputs
docs.text:
Upon completion, results are consolidated in ./test_multi/outs/:

  • Combined Interactive Report: Open test_multi_multi_report.html in a web browser to inspect cross-modality summary QC across RNA, ATAC, TCR, and BCR;
  • Decoupled Modality Subdirectories: Output directories (rna/, atac/, vdj-t/, vdj-b/) follow standard single-modality specifications and can be analyzed independently;
  • Execution Audit Manifest: logs/run_manifest.json tracks per-modality execution status and runtimes.

For full multi-omics directory hierarchy and file specifications, see Multi-Omics Output Details.

docs.title: C6 Multiplexed Single-Cell RNA Analysis
docs.text: Use this workflow for C6 RNA samples labeled with Sample Barcodes and pooled during library preparation. Multiple biological samples share one set of cDNA and Oligo sequencing data. The software uses the configured barcode assignments to demultiplex samples, then performs cell calling, counting, and downstream analysis separately for each sample. For samples with independent libraries and FASTQs, use single-sample RNA analysis or batch script generation.

docs.title: Step 1: Prepare Shared Data, Reference, and Sample Assignments
docs.text:
Place paired cDNA and Oligo reads from one pooled C6 library in the following directories:

/test/data/c6_pooled_data/
├── cDNA/
│   ├── pooled_cDNA_R1.fastq.gz
│   └── pooled_cDNA_R2.fastq.gz
└── oligo/
    ├── pooled_oligo_R1.fastq.gz
    └── pooled_oligo_R2.fastq.gz
  • Shared FASTQ root: Set [libraries] fastqs to /test/data/c6_pooled_data, not to cDNA/, oligo/, or an individual FASTQ file. All samples share this single input row; do not create FASTQ directories per sample or repeat the rna row.
  • Multiple sequencing files: For multiple files from the same pooled library, place matched pairs in the corresponding cDNA/ and oligo/ directories. Read structures and dark-cycle settings must be compatible. See the automatic filename pairing rules. Configure and run different pooled libraries separately.
  • Reference: Prepare a reference directory already built with rna mkref. Set genomeDir to that directory, not to a FASTA or GTF file. See RNA reference building above.
  • Sample assignments: Check your experimental records for the Sample Barcode assigned to each biological sample. The mappings Sample_01 → BC01 and Sample_02 → BC02;BC03 below are examples only. Replace them with the actual assignments; do not infer barcodes from sample order.

Both /test/data/c6_pooled_data and /database/scRNA/Homo_sapiens are placeholders. Replace them with existing data and reference directories on your system.

docs.title: Step 2: Write the C6 Configuration
docs.text:
Save the following as a plain-text file named sample.config.csv, retaining all three sections and both table headers:

[rna]
genomeDir,/database/scRNA/Homo_sapiens
chemistry,scRNAC6
darkreaction,auto
no_bam,false

[libraries]
fastqs,feature_types
/test/data/c6_pooled_data,rna

[samples]
sample_id,probe_barcode_ids
Sample_01,BC01
Sample_02,BC02;BC03
Setting Meaning and value [rna] genomeDir RNA reference directory. [rna] chemistry,scRNAC6 C6 read structure; fixed to scRNAC6 when [samples] is present. An omitted value is also normalized to this name. [rna] darkreaction,auto Automatically detect cDNA and Oligo dark cycles; this does not select the chemistry version. [rna] no_bam,false Retain the default BAM output. Change to true to save storage by omitting per-sample, unassigned, and Oligo BAMs and their indexes. [libraries] fastqs / feature_types Shared FASTQ root and library type; use one row with type rna in this example. [samples] sample_id Biological sample name used for output directories and reports; it does not need to match a FASTQ filename. [samples] probe_barcode_ids Sample Barcode IDs actually used for that sample; separate multiple IDs for the same sample with semicolons ;.

Sample table rules: Use one row per biological sample. In this example, data labeled BC02 and BC03 are assigned together to Sample_02, rather than creating two separate samples. Sample names must be unique ignoring case, begin with a letter or digit, and contain only letters, digits, ., _, or -. Do not use the reserved names unassigned or non_multiplexed. Do not repeat a barcode within a row or assign it to multiple samples. Built-in IDs and custom DNA sequences are supported; see the C6 sample table specification.

Path resolution: Relative paths inside the configuration are resolved against the directory containing sample.config.csv. Relative --csv and --outdir command-line paths are resolved against the current working directory. Absolute paths in the configuration are recommended for your first run.

Optional cell-calling settings: Add expectcells, forcecells, or minumi columns to [samples] when per-sample settings are needed, using positive integers. Empty fields inherit global settings. Do not copy the pooled experiment's expected cell count into every sample row. high_occupancy_filter is an experiment-wide switch, enabled by default, and belongs only in [rna]. See the C6 parameter examples.

docs.title: Step 3: Run the C6 Analysis
docs.text:
Run this command from the directory containing sample.config.csv:

$dnbc4tools multi run \
    --name test_c6 \
    --csv ./sample.config.csv \
    --threads 40

--name test_c6 names the entire pooled-library run, separately from Sample_01 and Sample_02 in [samples]. This command writes results to ./test_c6/outs/ under the current working directory (use --outdir to specify another root directory) and uses 40 CPU threads.

docs.title: Step 4: Inspect Global and Per-Sample Outputs
docs.text:
Upon completion, results are stored in ./test_c6/outs/:

  • Batch Summary Report: Open test_c6_multi_report.html in a web browser to inspect overall library QC, Sample Barcode demultiplexing yield, and per-sample cell count comparisons;
  • Per-Sample Dedicated Deliverables: Each sample has dedicated results in rna/per_sample_outs/<sample>/, including individual interactive reports (<sample>_scRNA_report.html), count matrices (MEX / .h5 / .h5ad), and alignment BAMs (if enabled);
  • Physical Library Pooled Matrix: rna/filtered_feature_bc_matrix/ (and .h5 / .h5ad) retains the global unintegrated counts across the pooled library.

For detailed C6 directory specifications and batch integration considerations, see C6 Output Details and Reading Results in R / Python.

docs.title: Batch Script Generation
docs.text: Designed for scaling up analysis across dozens of independent single-cell samples. By providing a tab-separated sample list, dnbc4tools automatically generates standalone shell scripts for each sample, ready to run directly or queue through workload managers such as Slurm or SGE.

docs.title: Step 1: Prepare Sample Manifest
docs.text:
RNA Sample Manifest (rna_samples.tsv)

Tab-delimited with 3 columns: sample_id, cDNA_R1;cDNA_R2, oligo_R1;oligo_R2 (comma-separated for multi-lane files per read):

Sample1 sample1_cDNA_R1.fq.gz;sample1_cDNA_R2.fq.gz sample1_oligo_R1.fq.gz;sample1_oligo_R2.fq.gz
Sample2 sample2_cDNA_R1.fq.gz;sample2_cDNA_R2.fq.gz sample2_oligo_R1.fq.gz;sample2_oligo_R2.fq.gz

ATAC Sample Manifest (atac_samples.tsv)

Tab-delimited with 2 columns: sample_id, FASTQ_R1;FASTQ_R2 (comma-separated for multi-lane files per read):

Sample1 sample1_R1.fq.gz;sample1_R2.fq.gz
Sample2 sample2_R1.fq.gz;sample2_R2.fq.gz

docs.title: Step 2: Generate Analysis Scripts
docs.text:
# Batch generate RNA execution scripts
$dnbc4tools rna multi \
    --list ./rna_samples.tsv \
    --genomeDir /database/scRNA/Homo_sapiens \
    --threads 20

# Batch generate ATAC execution scripts
$dnbc4tools atac multi \
    --list ./atac_samples.tsv \
    --genomeDir /database/scATAC/Homo_sapiens \
    --threads 20

Execution Behavior: The multi command generates standalone .sh scripts (e.g., run_Sample1.sh) in the current working directory without automatically starting computational workloads. Execute generated scripts on demand (e.g., sh run_Sample1.sh) or submit them to your HPC cluster queue.

After completing the quick start walkthroughs, consult detailed documentation for advanced options:

  • Explore underlying pipeline workflows: Pipeline Overview
  • Learn comprehensive parameters and CLI options: Parameters Overview
  • Understand structured deliverable files: Output Deliverables Overview

docs.title: Release Notes
docs.text:
Release history of DNBelab C Series™ HT Single-Cell Analysis Software

Development Version • Previous Releases • Version Guide

docs.title: Development Version
docs.text:
dnbc4tools 3.2 — Development Documentation (unreleased), updated October 23, 2026.

The formal release date, installation package and checksums await confirmation. The latest release documented before this update was 3.1 (May 15, 2026).

docs.title: 3.2 Key Updates
docs.text:
• C6 Multiplexed scRNA Analysis: Enables pooled sequencing within a single physical library with automatic Sample Barcode demultiplexing, delivering independent expression matrices (MEX / H5 / H5AD), aligned BAMs (when [rna] no_bam is false, the default), and interactive HTML reports for each sample.
  • Dual-Species Classification Upgrade: Introduces bidirectional background prediction bands and two-stage robust Huber regression to replace rigid cutoffs, to assess cell species assignments.
  • scRNA Algorithmic & Filtering Optimizations: Updates Oligo Read 2 filtering rules; optimizes multi-gene duplicate UMI conflict resolution; adds bound safeguards for automatic cell calling.
  • scATAC Core Upgrades: Switches peak calling and matrix quantification to cutsite mode (9-bp offset adjusted Tn5 insertion sites); preserves fragment-based FRIP and TSS metrics.
  • scVDJ Algorithmic Upgrades: Updates chain pairing, full-length contig assembly, and deterministic handling of multi-threaded sampling.
  • Standardized Outputs & Infrastructure: Standardizes RNA/ATAC matrix directory structures with companion .h5 files; decouples batch script generation to the working directory; adds startup preflight, process file locks, structured error tracking, and compressed diagnostic archives.

For detailed algorithmic rationale, parameter behavior, and migration guidelines, see the Upgrade Guide. Use the header menu to view the frozen 3.1 manual.

docs.title: Previous Release History
docs.text:
The previous release records are listed below in reverse chronological order:

3.1 (2026-05-15)
  • Multi-omics Mode: Added support for single-sample multi-omics analysis, enabling combined RNA + VDJ workflows or standalone single-modality execution.
  • RNA Enhancements & Bug Fixes: Added --consistent_cells to reuse merged bead assignments for downstream consistency; resolved calculation error in Fraction Reads in Cells; fixed dual-species database handling for species names containing underscores.
  • Performance & CLI Consistency: Accelerated bam2fastq and fqsubC4 processing; standardized help text and parameter formatting across all modules (including multi-sample commands).
3.0 (Dec 18, 2025)
  • RNA-Seq Enhancements:
    • Refined prioritization of exonic loci to improve quantification accuracy and resolve multi-gene mapping ambiguities;
    • Implemented error correction logic for cell barcodes containing ambiguous 'N' bases;
    • Added robust support for building and analyzing mixed-species reference genomes;
    • Enriched BAM files with cell tags (CC/CB), updated feature matrices to include gene ID, gene name, and library type;
    • Introduced automatic estimation for expectcells and added a new minumi threshold parameter.
  • ATAC-Seq Enhancements:
    • Expanded QC metrics to include barcode/read Q30 statistics and insert size distributions derived from deduplicated fragments;
    • Upgraded alignment engine to chromap v0.3.3, enhanced barcode correction algorithms, and enriched BAM outputs.
  • VDJ Enhancements:
    • Advanced per-cell assembly algorithms to maximize full-length contig recovery with stricter filtering criteria;
    • Optimized memory management to eliminate the need for full data preloading during analysis;
    • Enhanced contig_annotations.csv with comprehensive details, improved QC metrics, and added consensus sequence annotations;
    • Enabled support for custom reference generation for non-human/mouse species.
  • Cross-Module Improvements:
    • Unified the customize parameter usage across all analysis modules;
    • Achieved significant reduction in disk usage through optimized file organization;
    • Deprecated the process parameter and automated the cleanup of intermediate files to streamline execution.
2.1.3 (October 9, 2024)
  • New Features:
    • Added RNA 5' transcriptome analysis module;
    • Added single-cell VDJ analysis module;
    • Added GTF file format checking and correction functionality.
  • Installation & Performance:
    • Released as tar.gz with no additional environment configuration needed;
    • Removed conda installation method;
    • Fixed memory exceptions in scATAC bead merging;
    • Optimized RNA alignment and interval annotation performance.
2.1.2 (April 24, 2024)
  • ATAC Analysis Improvements:
    • Updated algorithm: Jaccard-based merging → cell calling via peak fragments;
    • Added multiple filtering parameters and BAM format support;
    • Enhanced chloroplast handling in database construction;
    • Unified web report style with RNA analysis.
  • General Improvements:
    • Streamlined installation process (removed R package requirements);
    • Improved N filtering logic for cell barcodes and UMI regions.
