docs.title: Running & Troubleshooting
docs.text: This guide provides comprehensive information on execution workflows, log auditing, troubleshooting diagnostics, and checkpoint recovery for the DNBelab C Series™ single-cell analysis software (dnbc4tools).

docs.title: 1. Basic Environment Verification
docs.text: Before launching large-scale production analyses, verify the following prerequisites: * Software Version: Confirm your installation by running dnbc4tools --version (ensuring it matches 3.2 or higher); * Tool Dependencies: Ensure that native system dependencies (such as STAR, SAMtools, MACS2, etc.) are available in the system $PATH; * Input Integrity: Paired-end FASTQ files must be intact, uncorrupted, and properly paired (MD5 checksum validation is recommended); * Reference Compatibility: Ensure reference files (FASTA, GTF, and aligner indexes) match the experimental organism and library chemistry version.

docs.title: 2. Preflight Snapshot & Run Locking
docs.text:
At startup, the pipeline executes strict preflight checks before any heavy computation: * Preflight Snapshot (logs/preflight.json): Records resolved execution parameters including thread count (Threads), requested execution steps (Steps), reference genome directory (Reference), library chemistry protocol (Chemistry), and the memory budget (resource_budget, detailing available system RAM and configured ceilings); * Exclusive Run Lock (logs/run.lock): An exclusive filesystem lock file is established under the log directory during execution to prevent concurrent write collisions on the same output directory. If a run is terminated abnormally by external signals (e.g. kill -9), confirm the previous process is dead before removing the lock or retrying.

Batch Script Generation vs. Execution

  • Commands such as dnbc4tools rna multi and atac multi only generate .sh batch shell scripts in the working directory; they do not create analysis logs by themselves;
  • Executing the generated .sh scripts (or invoking multi run directly) initializes the full output hierarchy, creates the logs/ directory, and records comprehensive step logs.
  • Batch sample lists should use plain-text TAB delimiters, with semicolons ; separating R1/R2 pairs, and commas , separating multiple lane files of the same read.

docs.title: Logging System & logs Directory Structure
docs.text: Once a pipeline run starts, all terminal logs, subprocess command invocations, performance metrics, structured errors, and stage completion markers are stored under <outdir>/<name>/logs/.

docs.title: Directory Overview
docs.text:
<outdir>/<name>/logs/
├── YYYYMMDD.txt                          # Main daily execution log (chronological record of all stages)
├── run_manifest.json                     # Run audit manifest (records stage statuses, durations, and errors)
├── preflight.json                        # Startup preflight snapshot (records runtime environment and budgets)
├── errors.jsonl                          # Structured error tracking records (JSON Lines format)
├── run.lock                              # Exclusive process file lock (prevents concurrent write conflicts)
├── report_model.snapshot.json            # Complete web report data model snapshot
├── runs/                                 # Historical invocation audit directory
│   └── <run_id>/                         # Independent snapshots per invocation
│       ├── run.json                      # Parameter and status backup for this invocation
│       └── preflight.json                # Preflight configuration backup for this invocation
├── stage_manifests/                      # Stage execution manifests & fingerprints (checkpoint resume validation)
│   └── <pipeline>.<stage>.json
├── stage_completion/                     # Lightweight stage completion pointers
│   └── <pipeline>.<stage>.json
└── <sample>_upload.info                  # Compressed log & diagnostic archive (can be provided to MGI support for troubleshooting)

docs.title: 1. Main Daily Execution Log (logs/YYYYMMDD.txt)
docs.text:
• Role: The primary chronological log for pipeline execution, dynamically named by current date (e.g., logs/20261106.txt).
  • Standard Format: Follows the canonical format: 
    %(asctime)s - %(name)s - %(levelname)s - %(message)s
  • Recorded Information:
  • Initialization, input parameters, progress milestones, and completion status for every bioinformatics stage (data/QC, alignment, count, similarity, analysis, report, etc.);
  • Exact shell invocations, working directories, and standard output streams for underlying algorithms and external tools (STAR, SAMtools, MACS2);
  • Processed biological metrics including cell counts, feature dimensions, and matrix shapes;
  • Resource Profiling & Timing: Stage elapsed durations (seconds) are always recorded. When export DNBC4TOOLS_PROFILE_RESOURCES=1 is set, the main log also outputs detailed CPU and resident memory usage (e.g., process CPU user=142.50s, system=18.20s; process lifetime peak RSS=12.45 GiB).

docs.title: 2. Structured Error Tracking Log (logs/errors.jsonl)
docs.text:
• Role: Machine-readable structured error tracking log in JSON Lines format (one JSON object per line). This is the definitive record for diagnosing pipeline crashes.
  • Schema & Fields: 
    {
  "timestamp": "2026-11-06T13:00:00.123+08:00",
  "error_id": "e4f1a23b9c0d",
  "error_code": "TOOL",
  "run_id": "20261106T130000-12345-a1b2c3d4",
  "sample": "demo_sample",
  "pipeline": "rna",
  "stage": "align",
  "fatal": true,
  "error_type": "ToolExecutionError",
  "message": "STAR alignment failed with exit code 104",
  "traceback": "Traceback (most recent call last):\n  File ...\nToolExecutionError: ...",
  "context": {
    "command": "STAR --genomeDir /ref/STAR_index ...",
    "exit_code": 104,
    "stderr_tail": "EXITING because of FATAL ERROR: could not open genome file ..."
  }
}
  • Diagnostic Value: Terminal crashes print a 12-character Error ID: <id>. Searching this ID in errors.jsonl immediately surfaces the full Python stack trace, the failed shell command, and captured standard error lines (stderr_tail).

docs.title: 3. Run Audit Manifest (logs/run_manifest.json)
docs.text:
• Role: Top-level audit manifest summarizing execution status for the sample, consumed by cluster automation and downstream workflows.
  • Recorded Information:
  • Execution status: status (success, failed, aborted, etc.) and boolean success;
  • Invocation ID: Unique run_id (format: YYYYMMDDTHHMMSS-<pid>-<hash>);
  • Timestamps and duration: start_time, end_time, and total runtime duration_sec;
  • Terminal error detail: When execution fails, the terminal_error dictionary captures error_id, error_type, and message;
  • Modality statuses: Separate completion records for active modalities (RNA, ATAC, VDJ-T, VDJ-B).

docs.title: 4. Stage Checkpoints (stage_manifests/ & stage_completion/)
docs.text:
• stage_manifests/<pipeline>.<stage>.json:
  • Records detailed execution metadata, including the stage_fingerprint (binding the software version and contract schema) and the input_fingerprint (hash of inputs and arguments);
  • When running with --resume, the pipeline verifies fingerprint consistency. Stage results are reused only when checks of inputs, parameters, tool versions, and output integrity pass.
  • stage_completion/<pipeline>.<stage>.json:
  • Lightweight atomic completion pointer tracking generated output files (outputs), integrity hashes (output_integrity), and completion timestamps (completed_at).

docs.title: 5. Compressed Log & Diagnostic Archive (logs/<sample>_upload.info)
docs.text:
• Role: A binary streaming compressed archive automatically generated by internal pipeline tools upon web report creation;
  • Included Data: Securely packages and compresses the sample's execution log (YYYYMMDD.txt), stage run manifests, intermediate QC diagnostic tables, and execution context;
  • Submitting to MGI Support for Troubleshooting: When encountering intricate algorithmic abnormalities, unexpected runtime crashes, or when requesting assistance from MGI technical support, users do not need to manually gather scattered log files—simply provide the <sample>_upload.info file to MGI technical support. MGI support engineers can read the execution information and logs stored in the archive using diagnostic utilities (c4_diagnose) to assist troubleshooting.

docs.title: Error Classification & Troubleshooting Guide
docs.text:
When a run exits with an error, the terminal and logs report a standardized Error code. The table below outlines common error codes, typical root causes, and recommended investigation paths:

Error code Category & Common Causes Investigation & Resolution Paths CLI-CONFIG Option or syntax misconfiguration• Misspelled options or missing required parameters• Missing section headers in multi-omics configs (e.g. missing [libraries], [rna], [samples]) • Inspect CLI syntax and option spellings;• Check that configuration CSVs adhere to required section syntax. INPUT Input files missing, unreadable, or truncated• FASTQ path does not exist or lacks read permission• Paired FASTQ line counts do not match or file truncated• Barcode whitelist file missing • Verify file paths and Linux read permissions;• Test archive integrity using gzip -t <file.fq.gz>;• Ensure paired R1 and R2 files contain identical numbers of reads. REFERENCE Reference genome or annotation issue• Genome directory invalid or missing required index files• STAR index version mismatch with installed STAR binary• GTF missing gene_id or transcript_id attributes • Verify genome directory contains intact FASTA, GTF, and index files;• Confirm species configuration (e.g. Human / Mouse) matches the experimental chemistry. TOOL External tool or binary failure• STAR out of memory (OOM killed)• MACS2 or SAMtools error or terminated by signal• Shared dynamic library incompatibilities (glibc, libz) • Open logs/errors.jsonl to review the command and context.stderr_tail;• Increase RAM allocation or reduce thread counts if out-of-memory occurs;• Verify system shared libraries. OUTPUT Output filesystem or disk errors• Output directory does not exist and cannot be created• Disk storage capacity exhausted (No space left on device)• Disk quota or inode quota exceeded • Check available space using df -h;• Verify write permissions on <outdir>;• Check cluster storage quota or inode limits. INTERRUPTED Process terminated externally• Cluster schedulers (SLURM/SGE/PBS) sending SIGKILL/SIGTERM due to timeout or memory limits• Manual Ctrl+C or kill termination • Inspect cluster job logs (e.g. slurm-<jobid>.out) for node eviction or timeout reasons;• Confirm prior processes are terminated, then restart with resume options if desired. INTERNAL Unexpected Python runtime exception• Unhandled corner case or internal logic exception • Note the 12-character Error ID from the console;• Extract the complete traceback from logs/errors.jsonl for in-depth resolution.

docs.title: Scenario 1: Non-Zero Exit Code with TOOL Error
docs.text:
1. Locate Error ID: Check the terminal output for the error footer, e.g., Error ID: a7f8b91c2d3e (Error code: TOOL);
  2. Search Error Record: Grep the error ID in the log directory: 
    grep "a7f8b91c2d3e" <outdir>/<sample>/logs/errors.jsonl
  3. Identify Root Cause: Inspect context.command and context.stderr_tail, and check the cluster job log for memory-limit or OOM-kill messages. Identify whether the failure occurred during alignment, matrix generation, or BAM output before changing resource settings;
  4. Apply Resolution: For memory exhaustion, increase the job memory allocation or reduce --threads to lower concurrency. If BAM output is unnecessary, use --no_bam for RNA runs or no_bam,true in the [rna] section for multi/C6 runs. Version 3.2 uses embedded STAR alignment; STAR does not create or sort BAM files in this mode. Do not use --limitBAMsortRAM or pass --limitBAM* through --star_parameters to tune BAM output; these parameters are not applicable and are rejected by parameter validation.

docs.title: Scenario 2: Resuming an Interrupted or Cancelled Run
docs.text:
1. Ensure Process Cleanup: Verify that no zombie processes from the previous run are active;
  2. Clear Run Lock: If an interrupted run left a stale lock file, remove it cleanly: 
    rm -f <outdir>/<sample>/logs/run.lock
  3. Inspect Completed Stages: Review logs/stage_completion/ to verify which stages completed successfully;
  4. Execute Resume: Re-run the original command with the --resume flag appended. The runner will validate fingerprints and bypass previously verified stages, picking up directly from the point of interruption.

docs.title: Artifact Validation & Advanced Diagnostics (validate-artifacts)
docs.text:
To assist bioinformatics engineers and operations teams in validating deliverable integrity post-analysis, dnbc4tools includes an internal artifact validation utility:

# Lightweight structural check (verifies required directories and files exist and are non-empty)
dnbc4tools validate-artifacts --sample-dir /path/to/sample --level shallow

# Deep content and consistency inspection (verifies HDF5 structures, MEX dimensions, BAM indexes)
dnbc4tools validate-artifacts --sample-dir /path/to/sample --level deep --json /path/to/sample/logs/artifact-validation.json
  • --level shallow: Performs rapid checks, confirming required delivery files are present and non-empty;
  • --level deep: Scans H5/H5AD datasets, compares matrix row/column dimensions, and verifies BAM index headers, exporting diagnostics to a JSON manifest;
  • Note: This command provides structural integrity validation and does not replace biological review of QC metrics.

docs.title: C6 Multi-Sample Analysis Output Guide
docs.text:
Output scope: Directory trees describe a typical completed run. Optional outputs depend on enabled modules and successful stages. Quality ranges below are interpretation guidance, not software pass/fail rules; use the configured thresholds and report status for this run.

C6 multi-sample RNA outputs are organized into pooled results and per-sample results. Pooled results support comparisons of sample QC metrics; per-sample results contain expression matrices, clustering results, and reports. See Downstream Analysis for loading examples.

docs.title: Deliverables at a Glance
docs.text:
The table below summarizes the key deliverables of C6 multi-sample single-cell RNA analysis, file formats, primary use cases, and recommended downstream ecosystem integrations:

File Format Purpose <name>_multi_report.html HTML Batch summary and sample comparisons filtered_feature_bc_matrix.* MEX / H5 / H5AD Pooled called-cell counts raw_feature_bc_matrix.* MEX / H5 Unfiltered counts singlecell.csv.gz CSV.GZ Bead/droplet metadata and cell calls multi_sample/ CSV / TSV / JSON Sample assignment and QC metrics per_sample_outs/<sample>/ Directory Per-sample matrices, analysis, and reports metrics_summary.xls TSV Global QC summary oligo.records.bam, unassigned_alignments.bam BAM Shared oligo and unassigned alignments

File names above are relative to outs/rna/, except the batch report, which is under outs/. Exact paths appear in the directory tree below.

MEX matrices are directories; H5 and H5AD matrices are sibling files. Pooled counts do not include joint dimensionality reduction or clustering. Filter singlecell.csv.gz with is_cell_barcode == 1 for called cells; read large tables in chunks. BAM files and their indexes are generated only when [rna] no_bam is false (the default). The summary and per-sample HTML reports can be opened locally in a desktop browser. See detailed files and report interpretation below for fields, loading guidance, and report tabs.

The pooled and per-sample filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5ad files contain raw counts before downstream analysis. Load each sample's analysis/QC_Cluster.h5ad for saved clustering/embeddings. Samples that are empty or fail under sample_failure_policy=skip may lack analysis files or HTML reports; inspect report status and logs/run_manifest.json instead of treating the directory tree as a mandatory bundle.

docs.title: Output Directory Structure
docs.text:
Upon completion, results are archived under <outdir>/<name>/outs/. BAM files and their indexes in the tree below are generated only when [rna] no_bam is false (the default); no_bam,true skips all BAM outputs:

<outdir>/<name>/
├── outs/
│   ├── <name>_multi_report.html              # Batch multi-sample summary report (4 interactive tabs)
│   └── rna/
│       ├── raw_feature_bc_matrix/            # Global unfiltered expression matrix (MEX format)
│       ├── raw_feature_bc_matrix.h5          # Global unfiltered expression matrix (HDF5 format)
│       ├── filtered_feature_bc_matrix/       # Global real-cell expression matrix (MEX format)
│       ├── filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5     # Global real-cell expression matrix (HDF5 format)
│       ├── filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5ad   # Global real-cell expression matrix (AnnData format, no joint clustering)
│       ├── singlecell.csv.gz                 # Global droplet metadata table (with is_cell_barcode flag)
│       ├── metrics_summary.xls               # Global analysis metrics summary (tab-delimited TSV)
│       ├── oligo.records.bam                 # Shared Oligo alignment records (output when BAM enabled)
│       ├── unassigned_alignments.bam         # Alignments for unassigned reads (output when BAM enabled)
│       ├── multi_sample/                     # Sample demultiplexing and QC metrics
│       │   ├── per_sample_metrics.csv        # Cross-sample comparative metrics table
│       │   ├── sample_metrics_summary.xls    # Sample-level QC summary table
│       │   ├── barcode_assignment_metrics.json # Sample barcode identification and splitting statistics
│       │   └── high_occupancy_metrics.json   # High-occupancy droplet filtering statistics
│       └── per_sample_outs/<sample>/         # 【Per-Sample Output Directory】
│           ├── raw_feature_bc_matrix/        # Sample-specific unfiltered expression matrix (MEX)
│           ├── raw_feature_bc_matrix.h5      # Sample-specific unfiltered expression matrix (H5)
│           ├── filtered_feature_bc_matrix/   # Sample-specific real-cell expression matrix (MEX)
│           ├── filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5 # Sample-specific real-cell expression matrix (H5)
│           ├── filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5ad # Sample-specific real-cell expression matrix (AnnData format)
│           ├── <sample>_scRNA_report.html    # Sample-specific interactive HTML report
│           ├── metrics_summary.xls           # Sample-specific quality metrics table
│           ├── <sample>_alignments.bam       # Sample-specific BAM (when enabled; with .bai / .csi)
│           └── analysis/                     # Sample-specific clustering and marker gene analysis
│               ├── cluster.csv               # Cell clustering assignments & UMAP 2D coordinates
│               ├── marker.csv                # Long-format cluster marker gene differential analysis
│               ├── marker_table.csv          # Wide-format cluster marker summary table
│               ├── QC_Cluster.h5ad           # Complete AnnData object with clustering and embeddings
│               ├── raw_qc.xls                # Per-cell raw quality metrics table (TSV text)
│               ├── raw_QCplot.png            # Pre-filtering single-cell QC violin plot
│               ├── filter_QCplot.png         # Post-filtering single-cell QC violin plot
│               ├── cluster_annotation.png    # Cell type annotation scatter plot (when reference configured)
│               └── cell_classification.csv   # Species classification & multiplet calls (mixed-species only)
└── logs/
    └── run_manifest.json                      # Pipeline step status and runtime audit manifest

docs.title: 1. Multi-Sample Summary Report
docs.text: Path: outs/<name>_multi_report.html. * Role: Central quality control dashboard and overview for the entire C6 multiplexed experiment. * Four Core Interactive Tabs: * Summary: Batch-level summary cards (cells, median UMIs/genes), chemistry and runtime configuration, cross-sample bar chart/table comparisons, and expanded parameter manifests; * Cells: Sample-level RNA QC table, single-cell violin distributions, overlaid barcode rank curves, bead merging distributions, and probe barcode demultiplexing statistics; * Library: Shared cDNA and Oligo library sequencing fidelity (Q30, valid barcodes/UMIs), mapping breakdowns for All Reads vs. Filtered Cells, and saturation curves; * Samples: Decoupled support for all-sample comparative QC summaries (All samples mode) as well as per-sample details (Single sample mode, featuring sample-specific UMAP clustering, UMI overlays, cell type annotation, and cluster marker tables). * For detailed metric and chart interpretations, refer to Multi-Sample Web Report Interpretation below.

docs.title: 2. Globally Merged Expression Matrix
docs.text: Path: filtered_feature_bc_matrix.*. * Role: Pooled high-confidence count matrix for real cells across all multiplexed samples, provided in MEX, H5, and H5AD formats. * Feature & Design Rationale: Preserves raw counts without joint dimensionality reduction or clustering across samples. For joint analysis, assess batch effects in the context of the experimental design and select an appropriate integration method. * Namespace Protection: Cells in different samples may carry identical bead barcodes. Distinction relies strictly on sample barcode tags. When performing cross-sample pooling, do not truncate barcode suffixes; we recommend prefixing sample IDs during import into Seurat / Scanpy (e.g., add.cell.ids = c("SampleA", "SampleB")).

docs.title: 3. Global Droplet Metadata
docs.text:
Path: singlecell.csv.gz. Compressed in streaming gzip format, recording metrics across all beads and droplets (including ambient noise).

Column Description cell Aggregated cell identifier (may be blank for unassigned background droplets) reads Number of transcriptomic reads associated with this bead/droplet gene Number of distinct genes detected (UMI ≥ 1) umi Total number of transcript molecules (UMIs) detected is_cell_barcode Real cell call flag (1 or True indicates high-confidence real cell; 0 or False indicates background; unmatched records may be blank) barcode Raw cell barcode sequence (retaining sample tag suffix)

Downstream Usage Tips

  • Filter Real Cells: When reading this table into R or Python, always filter rows where is_cell_barcode == 1; do not treat all rows as cells.
  • Streaming Large Tables: With millions of candidate droplets, reading into Python should use chunking (pd.read_csv(..., chunksize=100_000)) or Polars for high performance.

docs.title: 4. Per-Sample Output Directories
docs.text:
Path: per_sample_outs/<sample>/.

Each sample output directory contains the files below. Optional files are generated under the conditions described for each file:

  • Sample HTML Report (<sample>_scRNA_report.html): Sample-specific Barcode Rank Plot, UMAP cell clusters, marker gene heatmaps, and sequencing saturation curves;
  • Sample Matrices: Independent MEX directory, H5 format, and AnnData filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5ad;
  • Sample BAM File (<sample>_alignments.bam): Generated only when [rna] no_bam is false; contains only reads assigned to this sample (with .bai or .csi index) for locus inspection in IGV;
  • Sample Analysis Directory (analysis/): dnbc4tools independent graph clustering, differential marker analysis, and QC figures.

marker.csv uses the same positive-marker selection as ordinary RNA: adjusted P < 0.05, positive log fold change, and at most 50 genes per cluster. cluster{K}_pval in marker_table.csv stores an adjusted P-value despite its shorter column name. Optional gene_symbols is present only if available in the source metadata.

docs.title: Per-Sample Analysis Directory Detail
docs.text:
Path: per_sample_outs/<sample>/analysis/.

File Name Format Primary Purpose & Field Description cluster.csv CSV Single-cell cluster assignments and coordinates. Records cell barcodes (row index), nGene, nUMI, leiden (cluster ID), UMAP_1, UMAP_2 coordinates, Cluster (with cell count label), and optional Predict_number and Predicted cell type. marker.csv CSV Long-format differential marker gene table for cell type identification and functional enrichment. Includes cluster, gene, score, avg_log2FC, p_val, p_val_adj, pct.1 (in-cluster fraction), and pct.2 (out-of-cluster fraction). marker_table.csv CSV Wide-format marker table suitable for cross-cluster comparison. Includes gene_ids, gene_name, and corresponding cluster{K}_lg2fc and cluster{K}_pval for each cluster. QC_Cluster.h5ad H5AD Full AnnData object encompassing downstream filtering, normalization, highly variable genes, PCA, Leiden graph clustering, UMAP coordinates, rank_genes_groups marker statistics, and cell annotations. Use Scanpy to read the saved clustering assignments, embeddings, and marker statistics. raw_qc.xls TSV Text Per-cell quality metrics table (note: tab-delimited plain text TSV, not a binary Excel spreadsheet). Rows represent cell barcodes; columns include n_genes_by_counts, total_counts, and mitochondrial percentages. raw_QCplot.png PNG Pre-filtering violin distribution of cellular features (UMI counts, gene counts, and mitochondrial percentages). filter_QCplot.png PNG Post-filtering violin distribution displaying the effect of QC cutoff filtering. cluster_annotation.png PNG (Optional) Generated when reference annotations (HCL for human, MCA for mouse) are enabled, displaying the UMAP scatter plot projected with predicted cell types. cell_classification.csv CSV (Optional) Generated in mixed-species experiments (e.g. Human_and_Mouse), recording species calls and multiplet calls for each cell in this sample.

Global Analysis Directory Scope

  • Single-Species C6 Runs: The global output does not include an outs/rna/analysis/ directory; independent clustering outputs are located exclusively in each sample's per_sample_outs/<sample>/analysis/.
  • Mixed-Species Runs: The global outs/rna/analysis/ delivers only the global cell_classification.csv species assignment table.
  • Count Matrix H5AD Location: filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5ad, serving as the count matrix deliverable, is located in the sample root per_sample_outs/<sample>/ alongside the MEX and H5 formats.

docs.title: Web Report Guide
docs.text:
Path: outs/<name>_multi_report.html.

Overview: The HTML report provides shared library metrics, sample QC comparisons, and per-sample analysis results. Use the top modality navigation and left functional navigation to select a view.

C6 Multi-Sample Quality Assessment Principles & Review Guide

  • Tiered Evaluation Strategy: C6 multiplexing combines shared library construction with sample tagging. Review should proceed in three stages: Global Library QC → Cross-Sample Uniformity → Individual Cell Biology.
  • Library Metrics First: Inspect the Library tab first for shared cDNA and Oligo throughput, Q30 base quality, valid barcodes, and genomic mapping rates to rule out global sequencing risks.
  • Cross-Sample Uniformity Check: In the Summary and Cells tabs, evaluate assigned reads, cell counts, and median genes/UMIs across samples to identify outliers caused by viability differences or tagging efficiency variations.
  • Individual Sample Biological Validation: In the Samples tab or sample reports, verify UMAP cluster topology, automated cell annotations, and canonical marker gene expression for biological consistency.

docs.title: Two-Level Navigation Architecture
docs.text:
The interactive report decouples content through primary top and secondary left navigation bars:

  • Top Modality Bar (Primary Tab): Displays active modality as RNA;
  • Left Navigation Bar (Secondary Tabs):
  • Summary: Global batch overview cards, cross-sample comparative charts, and runtime configuration;
  • Cells: Single-cell level QC metrics, violin distributions, barcode rank curves, bead merging, and probe demultiplexing;
  • Library: Physical sequencing library metrics (Q30, valid barcodes/UMIs), mapping distributions, and sequencing saturation;
  • Samples: Decoupled views for all-sample comparative summaries (All samples) and per-sample details (Single sample clustering and markers).

docs.title: Summary Page (Assay overview)
docs.text: The Summary tab provides global batch statistics and cross-sample metric comparisons to rapidly spot outlier samples:

docs.title: 1. Global Summary Cards
docs.text:
Prominent metric cards at the top highlight overall batch performance:

Metric Card Calculation & Statistical Scope Interpretation & Guidance Estimated number of cells Total number of barcodes identified as real cells across all samples (sum of called cells before downstream QC). Compare against total targeted cell input. If recovery is below expectations, review cell viability and microfluidic encapsulation alongside other QC metrics. Median UMIs per cell Median of per-sample median UMI counts (cross-sample median, not a pooled cell median). Reflects the batch-wide transcript capture baseline. Median genes per cell Median of per-sample median detected genes (genes with UMI ≥ 1). Reflects overall library complexity and transcriptome coverage. Mean reads per cell Assigned RNA read pairs / called cells in this sample, including assigned reads outside called-cell barcodes. Measures average raw sequencing depth. Sequencing depth requirements depend on cell type, library complexity, and analysis goals.

docs.title: 2. Pipeline Information & Chemistry
docs.text: Displays core execution parameters: * Chemistry: Library protocol (displayed as SCRNAC6); * Include Introns: Indicates whether intronic alignments contribute to gene expression quantification (Yes recommended, particularly for single-nuclei RNA-seq snRNA-seq); * Reference: Reference genome and annotation build.

docs.title: 3. Cross-Sample Comparison (Sample overview)
docs.text: Provides toggles between Chart and Table views: * Chart View: Bar charts ranking samples on the selected metric with a dashed line marking the across-sample median; supports sorting by Sample ID or Value to identify demultiplexing imbalances. * Table View: Interactive table listing Sample ID, Assigned reads (count and percentage), Called cells, Median genes, and Median UMIs; click View cells → on any row to open details for that sample in the Samples tab.

docs.title: Configuration Parameters
docs.text:
Clicking the parameters toggle in the header expands the complete execution manifest:

  • Input Configuration (Input CSV): Fully documents the run configuration table, including library blocks ([libraries]), sample demultiplexing mappings and expected cell numbers ([samples]), and RNA alignment parameters ([rna]: reference genome path, no_bam flag, etc.);
  • Raw Sequencing Inputs (Input FASTQs): Records absolute physical FASTQ paths for cDNA and Oligo libraries, providing complete traceability for reproducible bioinformatics audits.

docs.title: Cells: Cell QC
docs.text: The Cells tab focuses on single-cell level QC, comparing signal specificity and cellular uniformity across samples:

docs.title: 1. RNA Quality Metrics Table
docs.text:
Comprehensive per-sample single-cell QC table:

Metric Calculation & Definition Interpretation & Guidance Estimated number of cells Number of called real cells in this sample before downstream QC. Evaluates whether sample-specific cell recovery meets expectations. Mean reads per cell Assigned RNA read pairs / called cells in this sample, including assigned reads outside called-cell barcodes. Measures raw physical sequencing depth allocated per cell. Mean cell-associated reads per cell cDNA reads associated with called-cell barcodes / Total called cells. Measures effective sequencing depth within real cells (excluding ambient loss). Mean UMI counts per cell Mean UMI counts detected per called cell. Measures average transcript capture levels. Median UMI counts per cell Median deduplicated UMI counts per called cell. Physical molecular capture baseline per cell. Mean genes per cell Mean genes detected (UMI ≥ 1) per called cell. Evaluates average transcriptional richness. Median genes per cell Median genes detected (UMI ≥ 1) per called cell. Measures cell transcriptional activity and library diversity. Total genes detected Total distinct genes detected in at least one cell in this sample. Typically 15,000–35,000 for mammalian tissues. Fraction reads in cells Fraction of confidently mapped transcriptomic reads with valid barcodes that fall within called cells. Assesses the fraction of reads in called cells. For low values, review cell viability, barcode assignment, and other QC metrics when investigating ambient RNA or cell damage.

docs.title: 2. Barcode Ranking & Bead Merging (RNA Beads to Cells)
docs.text:
• RNA Barcode Rank Plot (Left): Overlays barcode rank curves for all samples on logarithmic axes. High-quality samples show a wide plateau followed by a steep drop-off at the inflection point.
  • RNA Violin Plot (Middle): Mitochondrial percentage violin distribution (Mito percent), monitoring cellular integrity during sample preparation and microfluidic encapsulation (typically recommended median < 10%–15%).
  • Bead Count Distribution (Right): Histogram showing the number of bead barcodes merged into each called cell barcode, confirming that the vast majority of droplets encapsulate a single bead.

docs.title: 3. Probe Barcode Demultiplexing Table (Metrics per probe barcode)
docs.text: Documents the demultiplexing efficiency and yield for each Sample Barcode probe: * Probe barcode ID: Probe barcode identifier (e.g., BC09, BC11, BC12); * Sample ID: Bound sample identifier (e.g., demo_1, demo_3); * UMIs per probe barcode: Total UMI counts assigned to this probe and percentage share of the run; * Cells per probe barcode: Total called cells assigned to this probe and percentage share of the batch.

docs.title: Library: Library QC
docs.text: The Library tab details physical sequencing fidelity for shared cDNA and Oligo libraries, genome mapping distributions, and sequencing saturation:

docs.title: 1. Sequencing Metrics
docs.text:
Reports quality separately for the transcriptomic cDNA library and sample tagging Oligo library:

Library Type Core Metrics Interpretation & Guidance cDNA Library • Number of reads: Total input raw reads• Valid cell barcodes: Barcode whitelist matching fraction (≥ 80%)• Valid probe barcodes: Probe barcode validity (if applicable)• Corrected barcodes: 1bp error-corrected barcodes (5%–10%)• Valid UMIs: Valid non-N, non-homopolymer UMI fraction (> 99%)• Q30 bases in barcode / UMI / RNA read: Phred quality scores (> 85%) Evaluates sequencing instrument performance and cDNA library integrity. Oligo Library • Number of reads: Total Oligo reads• Valid barcodes in Read1 / Read2: Barcode match rate in paired reads (≥ 85%)• Corrected barcodes in Read1 / Read2: 1bp correction rate• Q30 bases in barcode / index read: Base quality for sample tags Evaluates sample tagging fidelity, directly determining demultiplexing accuracy.

docs.title: 2. Mapping Metrics
docs.text: Provides views for All Reads (entire library) and Filtered Cells (real-cell reads): * Reads mapped to genome: Fraction of reads aligning to the reference genome (recommended ≥ 85%–90%); * Reads mapped confidently to genome: Uniquely aligned high-confidence fraction (recommended ≥ 65%–80%); * Reads mapped confidently to transcriptome: Fraction aligning confidently to annotated transcripts (recommended ≥ 50%); * Reads mapped to mitochondrial genome: Percentage assigned to mitochondrial genes; * Confidently mapped to Exonic / Intronic / Intergenic: Alignment distribution across genomic feature classes (when Include Introns is enabled, both exonic and intronic reads contribute to UMI quantification); * Mapped antisense to gene: Fraction aligning antisense to annotated transcripts.

docs.title: 3. Saturation Analysis
docs.text:
• Sequencing Saturation Curve: Plots sequencing saturation as a function of mean cDNA reads per cell estimated via downsampling. Saturation levels around 50%–70% generally satisfy standard clustering and cell type identification needs.
  • Median Genes per Cell Curve: Illustrates gene discovery plateauing with sequencing depth, identifying points of diminishing returns.

docs.title: Samples: Sample Results
docs.text: The C6 report in version 3.2 provides two views in the Samples tab: an all-sample overview and individual sample details:

docs.title: 1. All-Sample Overview (All samples View)
docs.text:
When All samples (15) is selected from the dropdown menu, comprehensive comparative tables and curve previews are displayed across all multiplexed samples:

  • Cell Calling Quality Table: Horizontally compares Cells, Fraction reads in cells, Median Genes per Cell, Median UMI Counts per Cell, Mitochondrial %, Total Genes Detected, Assigned Reads, and Mean Reads per Cell across all samples;
  • Mapping Quality - All Reads Table: Horizontally compares genomic mapping rate, confident genomic rate, transcriptomic rate, exonic/intronic/intergenic breakdown, and antisense rate;
  • Cross-Sample Curve Previews: Barcode rank curves, violin plots, and saturation curves overlaid across all samples.

docs.title: 2. Sample Details (Single sample View)
docs.text: Selecting an individual sample from the dropdown (e.g., demo_17) reveals its independent biological clustering and marker expression:

docs.title: Sample-Specific Quick QC Cards (Cell Calling & Mapping Quality)
docs.text: Selecting a sample immediately updates two key metric card sets: * Cell Calling Quality: Cells, Fraction reads in cells, Median Genes/UMIs, and Assigned Reads for this sample; * Mapping Quality — All Reads: Genomic mapping rate, transcriptomic rate, mitochondrial ratio, and exonic/intronic proportions.

docs.title: Independent Barcode Rank & Violin Plots
docs.text:
• Displays the independent Barcode Rank curve and inflection point for this sample;
  • Displays independent single-cell violin plots for Genes, UMIs, and mitochondrial percentage.

docs.title: Independent UMAP Clustering & UMI Overlay
docs.text:
• Left Plot (RNA Cluster Assignment): 2D UMAP projection colored by unsupervised graph-based clusters (subsampled up to 10,000 cells for browser responsiveness; full cell sets are retained in output files);
  • Right Plot (UMI Count Overlay): UMAP colored by total UMI counts per cell, confirming whether clusters are driven by biological expression or sequencing depth variations.

docs.title: Automated Cell Annotation
docs.text: When supported reference annotations are enabled, predicted cell identities (such as B cells, T cells, NK cells, Monocytes) are projected onto the UMAP scatter plot.

docs.title: Differential Marker Gene Analysis (Top Features by Cluster)
docs.text: Interactive marker gene table comparing each cluster against remaining cells: * Cluster: Cluster number; * Gene: Marker gene symbol; * p_val_adj: Adjusted p-value returned by Scanpy rank_genes_groups; * avg_log2FC: Log2 fold change of gene expression in this cluster; * pct.1 / pct.2: Percentage of cells expressing the gene within vs. outside the cluster.

docs.title: Sample Saturation Analysis
docs.text: Displays independent sequencing saturation and median genes per cell curves for this sample.

docs.title: Core Metrics & Denominator Scope
docs.text:
The denominators used for C6 metrics are defined below:

Metric Scope & Calculation Definition Assigned Reads Actual read pairs assigned to this sample based on Sample Barcode recognition (not total raw reads). Mean Reads per Cell Assigned Reads / Cells within the sample (shows N/A if cell count is 0). Mean cell-associated reads per cell cDNA reads associated with called-cell barcodes / Total called cells, representing effective sequencing depth within real cells. Fraction Reads in Cells Confidently mapped transcriptomic reads from called cells divided by total valid-barcode reads in this sample. Mapping Quality Calculated using evaluated reads assigned to this sample; does not pool cross-sample reads. cDNA Valid Barcodes Stably reported as 100% when Assigned Reads > 0 (describes the subset already assigned). Library-Level Metrics (Q30 / Valid UMI) Measures shared sequencing quality; annotated as cDNA QC scope. Sample Barcode Validity Fraction of Oligo reads matching the expected sample barcode whitelist.

docs.title: Multi-Omics Analysis Output
docs.text:
Output scope: Directory trees describe a typical completed run. Optional outputs depend on enabled modules and successful stages. Quality ranges below are interpretation guidance, not software pass/fail rules; use the configured thresholds and report status for this run.

Single-Cell Multi-Omics Integrated Analysis Output Guide

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The multi-omics workflow coordinates RNA, ATAC, and V(D)J analysis from one configuration file and organizes their outputs by modality. The combined HTML report presents QC metrics and analysis results from the enabled modalities. ATAC is analyzed independently and summarized; RNA and V(D)J support cell association analysis. A combined report does not itself perform joint dimensionality reduction or clustering across modalities.

docs.title: Deliverables at a Glance
docs.text:
The table below summarizes the key deliverables of multi-omics analysis, file formats, primary use cases, and recommended downstream ecosystem integrations:

Deliverable & Core Files Format Description & Ecosystem Integration Combined Multi-Omics Report• outs/<sample>_multi_report.html HTML Comprehensive offline visual dashboard covering core metrics, barcode rank curves, clustering, automated cell annotations, and library alignment stats across RNA, ATAC, VDJ-T, and VDJ-B.• How to Open: No internet required; double-click to view directly in any modern desktop browser. Single-Cell RNA Outputs• outs/rna/ Directory Complete scRNA output directory containing filtered and raw matrices (MEX / H5 / H5AD), clustering and marker analyses (analysis/), single-cell metadata (singlecell.csv), and coordinate-sorted alignment BAM (only when [rna] no_bam is false). Chromatin Accessibility Outputs• outs/atac/ Directory Complete scATAC output directory containing filtered and raw peak matrices (MEX / H5), high-confidence cell fragments (filtered.fragments.tsv.gz and Tabix index), TSS enrichment, and cell metadata. TCR Immune Repertoire Outputs• outs/vdj-t/ Directory Complete TCR repertoire outputs containing filtered contig annotations (filtered_contig_annotations.csv), FASTA sequences, clonotype statistics (clonotypes.csv), and international AIRR annotations (airr_annotations.tsv). BCR Immune Repertoire Outputs• outs/vdj-b/ Directory Complete BCR repertoire outputs containing paired heavy/light chain contig annotations, consensus sequences (consensus.fasta), clonotype frequencies, and AIRR standard files. Pipeline Run Manifest• logs/run_manifest.json JSON Audit log recording execution time and status (success, success_existing cache hit, or failed) per modality, facilitating automated operations and provenance tracking.

docs.title: Output Directory Structure
docs.text:
Upon completion, results are archived under <outdir>/<sample>/outs/:

<outdir>/<sample>/
├── outs/
│   ├── <sample>_multi_report.html             # Multi-omics integrated interactive visual report
│   ├── rna/                                   # Complete RNA module output directory (if enabled)
│   │   ├── filtered_feature_bc_matrix/        # Filtered high-confidence expression matrix (MEX)
│   │   ├── filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5      # Expression matrix (HDF5 format)
│   │   ├── filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5ad    # Expression matrix (AnnData format)
│   │   ├── singlecell.csv                     # Single-cell QC metadata table
│   │   ├── metrics_summary.xls                # RNA metrics summary table
│   │   └── analysis/                          # Dimensionality reduction, clustering, and marker genes
│   ├── atac/                                  # Complete ATAC module output directory (if enabled)
│   │   ├── filtered.fragments.tsv.gz          # High-confidence cell fragments and Tabix index
│   │   ├── filtered_peak_bc_matrix/           # Filtered peak matrix (MEX)
│   │   ├── filtered_peak_bc_matrix.h5         # Peak matrix (HDF5 format)
│   │   ├── peak_annotation.tsv               # Optional peak annotations
│   │   ├── singlecell.csv                     # ATAC cell-level QC metadata table
│   │   └── metrics_summary.xls                # ATAC metrics summary table
│   ├── vdj-t/                                 # Complete VDJ-T module output directory (if enabled)
│   │   ├── filtered_contig_annotations.csv    # Filtered high-confidence contig annotations
│   │   ├── clonotypes.csv                     # TCR clonotype statistics table
│   │   ├── airr_annotations.tsv               # International AIRR standard annotations
│   │   └── metrics_summary.xls                # VDJ-T metrics summary table
│   └── vdj-b/                                 # Complete VDJ-B module output directory (if enabled)
│       ├── filtered_contig_annotations.csv    # Filtered high-confidence contig annotations
│       ├── clonotypes.csv                     # BCR clonotype statistics table
│       ├── airr_annotations.tsv               # International AIRR standard annotations
│       └── metrics_summary.xls                # VDJ-B metrics summary table
└── logs/
    └── run_manifest.json                      # Per-modality execution manifest and audit log

docs.title: 1. Combined Multi-Omics Report (outs/<sample>_multi_report.html)
docs.text:
• Content: Centralized visual presentation of core metric cards, barcode rank curves, cluster plots, cell annotations, and sequencing/mapping quality across RNA, ATAC, VDJ-T, and VDJ-B.
  • Role: Single offline HTML file allowing researchers to perform cross-modal QC inspection, metric cross-validation, and biological discovery in one view.

docs.title: 2. Modality-Specific Output Directories (outs/rna, outs/atac, outs/vdj-t, outs/vdj-b)
docs.text:
• Content & Specification: Each enabled modality features an independent standardized directory whose file layout, naming, and formats are completely equivalent to individual standalone runs (e.g., MEX/H5/H5AD for RNA, fragments and peak matrices for ATAC, AIRR annotations for VDJ).
  • Multi-Omics Joint Analysis: In multi-omics experiments, cross-modal barcodes from the same cell share strict correspondence, enabling direct integration in Seurat (WNN multimodal integration), Signac, or Muon for joint clustering and gene regulatory network inference.
  • Modality Documentation Links:
  • scRNA Analysis Output Guide
  • scATAC Analysis Output Guide
  • scVDJ Analysis Output Guide

docs.title: 3. Execution Manifest & Audit Log (logs/run_manifest.json)
docs.text:
Records execution runtime and completion status per modality: * success: Clean execution completed successfully; * success_existing: Cache hit reusing previous checkpoint results; * failed: Modality failed during execution, logging error stages for rapid troubleshooting.

[!NOTE] Note: C6 Multiplexed Outputs Outputs and directory structures for C6 multi-sample single-cell RNA analysis based on Sample Barcode pooling are documented separately; please refer to C6 Multi-Sample Output Guide.

docs.title: Web Report Interpretation
docs.text:
Overview: The integrated multi-omics HTML report features a two-tier navigation architecture, decoupling overall summary metrics from modality-specific cell QC and physical library statistics.

Multi-Omics Quality Assessment Principles & Review Guide

  • Global Overview First: On the report's Summary tab (Assay overview), review the core metric cards (cell counts, median UMIs/fragments, VDJ productive pairs) across all enabled modalities to verify healthy recovery in every assay.
  • Modality-Specific Tiered Review: Navigate through each modality tab (RNA, ATAC, VDJ-T, VDJ-B) in the top bar, using the left navigation bar to inspect Cells (single-cell QC) and Library (sequencing fidelity and mapping rates).
  • Cross-Modal Biological Concordance: Cross-examine RNA gene expression clusters, ATAC chromatin accessibility patterns, and V(D)J clonal expansions to ensure biological consistency across cell identities.

docs.title: Two-Tier Navigation Architecture
docs.text:
The interactive report decouples content via top and left navigation bars:

  • Top Modality Bar (Primary Tabs): Dynamically displays active modalities for this run, including RNA, VDJ-T, VDJ-B, and ATAC;
  • Left Functional Bar (Secondary Tabs):
  • Summary: Core metric cards, multi-assay summary, and run configuration parameters;
  • Cells: Single-cell level QC tables, violin plots, barcode rank curves, clustering, cell annotation, and marker genes;
  • Library: Physical sequencing library quality (Q30, valid barcodes/UMIs), genomic mapping breakdowns, and saturation analysis.

docs.title: Summary Tab (Assay overview)
docs.text:
The Summary tab provides overview metric cards for all enabled modalities in this run:

  • Assay Overview Cards:
  • RNA Overview: Displays Estimated number of cells, Median UMIs per cell, and Median genes per cell;
  • VDJ-T Overview: Displays Estimated number of cells, Cells with productive V-J spanning pair, and chain recovery counts;
  • VDJ-B Overview: Displays Estimated number of cells and productive heavy/light chain pairing metrics;
  • ATAC Overview (if enabled): Displays Estimated number of cells, Median fragments per cell, and Fraction of fragments in cells.
  • Core Value: Centrally presents cell recovery and signal baselines across all modalities on one screen, rapidly identifying capture balance across assays.

docs.title: Configuration Parameters
docs.text:
Clicking the parameters button opens the configuration details modal:

  • Input Configuration (Input CSV): Fully logs configuration parameters, including modality-specific blocks ([rna], [atac], [vdj-t], [vdj-b]) and reference genome paths;
  • Library FASTQ Mappings ([libraries]): Records raw FASTQ file paths and feature_types assignments, providing complete provenance for analysis reproducibility.

docs.title: RNA > Cells (Single-Cell QC & Clustering)
docs.text:
Presents single-cell transcriptomic quality control, unsupervised clustering, and differential marker genes:

  • RNA Quality Metrics: Cell count, Fraction reads in cells (signal-to-noise ratio), median genes/UMIs, and mean sequencing depth;
  • RNA Beads to Cells:
  • RNA Barcode Rank Plot (Left): Log-log barcode rank curve exhibiting a steep cliff-like inflection point (Knee Point) separating real cells from ambient noise;
  • Bead Count Distribution (Right): Distribution of bead barcodes merged per real cell droplet;
  • RNA Cluster Analysis:
  • Left Plot (RNA Cluster Assignment): 2D UMAP projection colored by unsupervised graph-based clusters;
  • Right Plot (UMI Count Overlay): UMAP colored by total UMI counts per cell to verify that clustering is biologically driven;
  • RNA Cell Annotation: Predicted cell type identities based on reference models;
  • Top Features by Cluster: Interactive marker gene table with p_val_adj, avg_log2FC, and expressing percentages (pct.1 / pct.2).

docs.title: RNA > Library (Sequencing Fidelity, Mapping & Saturation)
docs.text:
Evaluates physical sequencing quality and genome alignment:

  • Sequencing Metrics: Raw read pairs, valid cell barcodes, valid UMIs, and Q30 base quality percentages;
  • Mapping Metrics: Evaluates All Reads vs. Filtered Cells, reporting genomic mapping, transcriptomic mapping, mitochondrial fraction, and exonic/intronic/intergenic proportions;
  • Saturation:
  • Sequencing Saturation Curve: Saturation as a function of mean reads per cell;
  • Median Genes per Cell Curve: Gene discovery plateauing with depth.

docs.title: ATAC > Cells (Chromatin Accessibility & Clustering)
docs.text:
Details chromatin accessibility signals, TSS enrichment, and epigenetic clusters:

  • ATAC Quality Metrics: Estimated cells, median fragments per cell, FRIP (Fraction of fragments overlapping peaks), and TSS overlapping fractions;
  • ATAC Beads to Cells: Fragment barcode rank plot and bead count distribution;
  • ATAC Cluster Analysis:
  • Left Plot (ATAC Cluster Assignment): Latent Semantic Indexing (LSI) reduction and UMAP projection showing chromatin subclusters;
  • Right Plot (Fragment Count Overlay): Fragment count gradients projected onto UMAP;
  • Targeting:
  • TSS Enrichment Profile: Normalized Tn5 insertion frequency across ±1,000 bp of annotated transcription start sites;
  • TSS Targeting Plot: Bivariate scatter plot of fragments vs. TSS scores separating real cells from background.

docs.title: ATAC > Library (Insert Size Periodicity & Metrics)
docs.text:
Assesses library physical properties and chromatin structure:

  • ATAC Metrics: Raw read pairs, valid barcodes, genomic mapping rates, mitochondrial ratio, and nucleosome-free / mono-nucleosome fractions;
  • Insert Size Distribution: Fragment length periodicity displaying nucleosome-free regions (< 147 bp) and ~200 bp nucleosomal phasing;
  • Cell Quality Metrics: Saturation curves and bead Jaccard similarity thresholds.

docs.title: 4. VDJ Modality (TCR & BCR Repertoires)
docs.text: Presents decoupled analyses for TCR (VDJ-T) and BCR (VDJ-B) immune receptor repertoires:

docs.title: VDJ-T / VDJ-B > Cells (Productive Pairing & Clonotypes)
docs.text:
• VDJ Quality Metrics:
  • Estimated Cells: High-confidence barcodes expressing target receptor transcripts;
  • Cells with Productive V-J Spanning Pair: Count and percentage of cells harboring full functional pairs (TRA/TRB or IGH/light chain; recommended ≥ 40%);
  • Mean Reads per Cell: Average reads dedicated per cell.
  • VDJ Barcode Rank Plot: Cumulative productive UMI curves. In BCR datasets, prominent peaks correspond to antibody-secreting plasma cells.
  • V(D)J Annotation: Detection rates and V-J spanning statistics per chain (TRA/TRB or IGH/IGK/IGL).
  • VDJ Clonotypes:
  • Top 10 Clonotypes Plot: Bar chart visualizing clonal expansion;
  • Top 10 Clonotypes Table: Lists clonotype IDs, CDR3 amino acid and nucleotide sequences per chain, cell frequencies, and proportions.
  • VDJ Target: Projects TCR/BCR clonally expanded cells onto RNA gene expression UMAP space, connecting clonal expansion with transcriptional phenotypes.

docs.title: VDJ-T / VDJ-B > Library (Enrichment Efficiency & Sequencing)
docs.text:
Details targeted library quality:

  • Sequencing: Read pair count, valid barcode fraction, valid UMI fraction, and Q30 base quality metrics;
  • Enrichment:
  • Reads mapped to any V(D)J gene: Fraction of reads mapping to known germline V(D)J segments (recommended ≥ 50%);
  • Chain-Specific Mapping: Alignment proportions across specific chains (TRA/TRB or IGH/IGK/IGL) to evaluate balanced targeted capture.

docs.title: Outputs and Reports
docs.text:
Output scope: Directory trees describe a typical completed run. Optional outputs depend on enabled modules and successful stages. Quality ranges below are interpretation guidance, not software pass/fail rules; use the configured thresholds and report status for this run.

Find output directories, file fields, and web report metrics by module. Independent pipeline runs write to <outdir>/<name>/outs/; Multi-omics (Multi) and C6 multiplexed workflows organize results hierarchically by modality and sample.

Module Main Deliverables Documentation scRNA Gene expression matrices (MEX / H5 / H5AD), cell metadata table, clustering, and HTML QC report scRNA Outputs Guide scATAC Chromatin accessibility peak matrices, Tabix-indexed fragments, cell QC, and HTML QC report scATAC Outputs Guide scVDJ TCR / BCR contig sequences, full-length functional annotations, clonotypes, and HTML QC report scVDJ Outputs Guide Multi-omics (Multi) Cross-modality combined QC report, modularized outputs for each modality (RNA / ATAC / VDJ) Multi Outputs Guide C6 Multiplexed Root combined expression matrix, singlecell.csv.gz, per-sample dedicated matrices, BAMs (when [rna] no_bam is false), and reports C6 Outputs Guide

docs.title: Universal Delivery Standards & Architecture
docs.text: dnbc4tools follows unified data delivery standards and directory organization across all omics workflows:

docs.title: 1. Standard Output Directory Hierarchy
docs.text:
• Independent Single-Modality Workflows: Output directly to <outdir>/<name>/outs/, housing delivered matrices, metric summary tables, BAM alignments (if enabled), and HTML interactive reports.
  • Multi-Omics Workflows (Multi): Deliver a combined cross-modality report <name>_multi_report.html in the root outs/ directory, while decoupling each modality into dedicated subdirectories (rna/, atac/, vdj-t/, vdj-b/) fully compatible with single-modality standards.
  • C6 Multiplexed Workflows: The combined report is outs/<name>_multi_report.html; pooled matrices and singlecell.csv.gz are under outs/rna/, and per-sample outputs are under outs/rna/per_sample_outs/<sample>/.

docs.title: 2. Feature & Expression Matrix Formats
docs.text:
All single-cell quantification matrices are delivered simultaneously in mainstream standard formats:

  • MEX Matrices: RNA uses matrix.mtx.gz, barcodes.tsv.gz, and features.tsv.gz. ATAC uses peaks.bed.gz instead of features.tsv.gz; read its matrix, barcodes, and peak coordinates explicitly rather than assuming an RNA feature file is present. See the loading guide.
  • H5 Format (*.h5): Single-file binary sparse matrix with metadata, loaded rapidly in R via Seurat::Read10X_h5() and in Python via scanpy.read_10x_h5().
  • H5AD Format (*.h5ad): RNA/C6 count matrices and RNA analysis objects are separate files. Count exports do not include clustering; use analysis/QC_Cluster.h5ad for saved downstream analysis. ATAC does not publish a count H5AD under outs/.

docs.title: 3. Unified Cell Calling & Metadata Filtering Rule
docs.text:
• singlecell.csv (or singlecell.csv.gz) records metrics across all candidate droplets/beads, including ambient noise and zero-UMI rows.
  • Universal Rule: In downstream analysis, always filter authentic cells using is_cell_barcode (selecting rows where value is 1 or True). Never use the total row count of the table as the delivered cell count.

docs.title: 4. Metric Summary File Format
docs.text:
• metrics_summary.xls uses the .xls extension for convenient double-click inspection in spreadsheet software, but its underlying format is standard tab-separated text (TSV).
  • Programmatic Reading: In R, use read.delim("metrics_summary.xls", check.names = FALSE) (do not use readxl::read_excel); in Python, use pd.read_csv("metrics_summary.xls", sep="\t").

docs.title: 5. Alignment BAM & Adaptive Indexing Rules
docs.text:
• Delivery Flags: scRNA generates BAM by default (skip with --no_bam); scATAC skips BAM by default to save I/O and disk (enable with --need_bam).
  • BAM Indexes: The native writer selects CSI when the maximum reference length exceeds 2^29 bases (536,870,912); otherwise it selects BAI. Header-only zero-result RNA BAMs may lack an index. Oligo BAMs are not required to have a coordinate index.
  • C6 BAM Output: [rna] no_bam defaults to false. Set no_bam,true to skip per-sample, unassigned, and oligo BAM files and their indexes.
  • BAM Tags: RNA/C6 cDNA records may carry UMI tags such as UB; ATAC does not use RNA UMI tags. Use CB to select records with a merged-cell identifier; tags on unmatched, unmapped, or oligo records differ.

docs.title: Modality Highlights & Caveats Quick Reference
docs.text:
Different modalities involve specific biological mechanisms and data structures. The table below summarizes key downstream considerations with links to dedicated sections:

Modality / Workflow Key Caveats & Best Practices See Section scRNA • Matrices feature UMI deduplication and conflict resolution for multi-gene mapping UMIs.• Multiple beads per droplet are merged into Cell IDs formatted as CELL<ID>_N<count>. scRNA Feature Matrices scATAC • Crucial: Peak matrices count 9-bp shifted cutsites, whereas cell QC metrics (FRIP/TSS) are based on unique fragments; never use matrix column sums as fragment sequencing depth.• 3.2 matrix.mtx.gz uses single space delimiters. scATAC Fragments & Peaks scVDJ • Primary downstream entry point is filtered_contig_annotations.csv (excluding non-productive and ambient noise).• AIRR standard file (airr_annotations.tsv) loads directly into scRepertoire/immunarch.• --beadstrans maps cell identifiers for RNA association; contig tables remain one-to-many per cell. scVDJ Assembly & Annotation C6 Multiplexed • The pooled matrix under outs/rna/ retains raw counts and does not include joint clustering/UMAP.• Demultiplexed outputs live in outs/rna/per_sample_outs/<sample>/.• Preserve barcode suffixes to prevent cross-sample collisions. C6 Deliverables Guide Multi-Omics (Multi) • Modularized directories (rna/, atac/, vdj-t/, vdj-b/) enable standalone analysis and cross-modality studies.• logs/run_manifest.json tracks execution and resume cache status. docs.title: scATAC Analysis Output
docs.text:
Output scope: Directory trees describe a typical completed run. Optional outputs depend on enabled modules and successful stages. Quality ranges below are interpretation guidance, not software pass/fail rules; use the configured thresholds and report status for this run.

Single-Cell ATAC Sequencing Output File Guide

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: After single-cell ATAC sequencing analysis is complete, a standardized structure of files and subdirectories is generated in the specified output directory for chromatin accessibility analysis and epigenomic research. Matrix and fragment files can be imported into tools such as Signac and ArchR using the appropriate format readers. See Downstream Analysis for loading examples.

docs.title: Deliverables at a Glance
docs.text:
The table below summarizes the key deliverables of scATAC analysis, file formats, primary use cases, and recommended downstream ecosystem integrations:

Deliverable & Core Files Format Description & Ecosystem Integration Filtered Cell Fragments• filtered.fragments.tsv.gz• filtered.fragments.tsv.gz.tbi BED (TSV.GZ)TBI Index QC-filtered high-confidence fragments from real cells in BED format, recommended primary input for downstream analysis.• Recommended Tools: Signac (CreateChromatinAssay) / ArchR (createArrowFiles) All Aligned Fragments• fragments.tsv.gz• fragments.tsv.gz.tbi BED (TSV.GZ)TBI Index Contains all uniquely aligned fragments with genomic coordinates and barcode tags, used for full provenance and background assessment.• Ecosystem: Can be directly loaded as BED tracks in IGV or UCSC Genome Browser. Chromatin Peak Matrix• filtered_peak_bc_matrix/• filtered_peak_bc_matrix.h5 MEX Sparse MatrixHDF5 (H5) Filtered peak quantification count matrix.• Counting Metric: Matrix values default to Cutsites (transposition insertion endpoints) for higher sensitivity; never use column sums (colSums) as fragment sequencing depth for filtering. Raw Peak Matrix• raw_peak_bc_matrix/• raw_peak_bc_matrix.h5 MEX Sparse MatrixHDF5 (H5) Unfiltered raw peak count matrix covering all candidate beads/droplets and background noise, used for custom filtering models. Cell Metadata• singlecell.csv CSV Records per-cell fragments, peaks, TSS/peak region fragments, cutsite counts, and real-cell flags (is_cell_barcode).• Filtering: Filter real cells where is_cell_barcode == 1. Metrics Summary• metrics_summary.xls TSV Text Global summary of sequencing quality, alignment rates, cell count, median fragments, and TSS enrichment.• Format: Tab-delimited text; read with read.delim() in R or pd.read_csv(sep='\t') in Python. Interactive Web Report• <sample>_scATAC_report.html HTML Comprehensive offline visual report for reviewing barcode rank curves, TSS enrichment profiles, fragment length distribution, and UMAP clustering.• How to Open: No internet connection required; double-click to open in any modern desktop browser. Alignment BAM• alignment.fragments.sorted.tagged.bam• alignment.fragments.sorted.tagged.bam.bai BAMBAI / CSI Coordinate-sorted BAM file with error-corrected cell barcode tags (CB, CR).• Condition: Requires --need_bam flag during analysis; used for locus-level IGV inspection. Peak Annotation• peak_annotation.tsv TSV Filtered-peak gene associations; optional, see annotation fields. Optional Diagnostics• cell_classification.csv• whitelist_contamination*.json CSV / JSON Mixed-species assignments and C4 whitelist diagnostics when produced.

Raw and filtered peak matrices also have H5 exports. Matrix counts default to cutsites; cell calling, FRIP, and TSS fractions retain unique-fragment statistics. BAM requires --need_bam; indexes can be BAI or CSI.

docs.title: ATAC Fragment and Peak Files
docs.text: Core Content: ATAC-seq fragment information and peak identification results, containing complete chromatin accessibility data and cell barcode tags.

docs.title: fragments.tsv.gz
docs.text:
fragments.tsv.gz is a compressed TSV file containing ATAC-seq fragment information, serving as one of the core data files for downstream analysis.

  • Purpose:

    • Chromatin Accessibility Analysis: Precisely locate the genomic coordinates of each open chromatin region.
    • Data Visualization: Can be loaded directly as a BED file into genome browsers such as IGV and UCSC.
    • Downstream Tool Input: Fully compatible with mainstream single-cell analysis tools including ArchR and Signac.

  • Content & Format:

    • The file is in BED-like format, with each row representing a unique ATAC-seq fragment.

    • Contains the following 5 columns:

      Field Name Description chrom Reference genome chromosome name identifying the fragment location chromStart 0-based adjusted start position on the chromosome, corrected for transposase insertion offset chromEnd Adjusted end position on the chromosome (exclusive), corrected for transposase insertion offset barcode Cell barcode ID corresponding to the CB tag in the BAM file, used to attribute fragments to specific cells readSupport Total number of read pairs associated with this fragment (including unique and duplicate reads)

  • Coordinate Adjustment:

    • To accurately map Tn5 transposase cleavage sites, fragment coordinates are shifted: the start position is moved 4 bp forward from the leftmost alignment, and the end position is moved 5 bp backward from the rightmost alignment.

docs.title: fragments.tsv.gz.tbi
docs.text:
The Tabix index file for fragments.tsv.gz.

  • Core Purpose: Enables rapid, interval-based random access queries on large fragment files without loading the entire dataset into memory.
  • Format: Standard binary index file generated by tabix.

docs.title: filtered.fragments.tsv.gz
docs.text:
The QC-filtered ATAC-seq fragment file, representing a curated subset of fragments.tsv.gz containing only high-confidence real cells.

  • Core Purpose:
    • Primary Downstream Input: Recommended input for cell clustering, differential accessibility, and transcription factor motif analyses.
    • Signal-to-Noise Enhancement: Drastically reduces background noise by removing debris and low-quality non-cell barcodes.
  • Content & Format:
    • Identical in format to fragments.tsv.gz (5 columns, compressed BED-like TSV).
    • Contains only fragments assigned to barcodes that passed cell calling algorithms.

docs.title: filtered.fragments.tsv.gz.tbi
docs.text:
The Tabix index file for filtered.fragments.tsv.gz.

  • Core Purpose: Ensures fast region-based access when downstream tools (such as ArchR and Signac) query the filtered fragments.
  • Format: Standard binary Tabix index file.

docs.title: alignment.fragments.sorted.tagged.bam
docs.text:
The coordinate-sorted BAM file containing all validly barcoded and successfully aligned reads.

  • Core Purpose:
    • Visualization & Verification: Inspect alignment coverage across specific loci in IGV.
    • Custom Pipeline Input: Serves as raw aligned data for custom epigenetic processing.

  • Key TAG Fields:

    TAG Type Description CB Z Error-corrected and merged cell barcode identifier CC Z Error-corrected cell barcode sequence CR Z Raw cell barcode sequence as reported by the sequencer

docs.title: alignment.fragments.sorted.tagged.bam.bai
docs.text:
Index file for alignment.fragments.sorted.tagged.bam.

  • Core Purpose: Enables fast random access and visualization in tools like IGV and Samtools.
  • Format: Standard BAI index format (or .csi when reference chromosomes exceed standard BAI size limits).

docs.title: Peak Matrix Files
docs.text:
Core Content: Single-cell peak quantification matrices in raw and filtered states, formatted as standard sparse matrices.

Crucial Note: Matrix Counting Metric (Cutsite) vs. Cell QC Metric (Unique Fragment)

  • Cutsite Counting Metric: Values in the peak matrix (filtered_peak_bc_matrix) represent two-end cleavage site counts (cutsites) after Tn5 9-bp offset adjustment, providing maximal sensitivity for local chromatin accessibility.
  • Fragment QC Metric: In singlecell.csv, metrics including peak_region_fragments, FRIP (Fraction of Reads in Peaks), TSS enrichment fraction, and cell calling filters are strictly based on deduplicated unique fragments.
  • Usage Warning: In R (Signac) or Python, never use matrix column sums (colSums(mtx)) as cell fragment sequencing depth for QC filtering! Theoretically, 1 fragment ≈ 2 cutsites, and their statistical distributions and biological implications differ significantly.
  • Delimiter Specification: Since version 3.2, matrix.mtx.gz uses a single space delimiter. Custom parsing scripts should use line.split() (matching arbitrary whitespace) or standard Matrix::readMM.

docs.title: Filtered Peak Matrix (filtered_peak_bc_matrix/)
docs.text:
Contains the peak count matrix filtered for high-confidence real cells, serving as the primary quantification input for downstream analysis.

  • Format: Standard Matrix Market Exchange (MEX) format, composed of three compressed files:

    File Name Description barcodes.tsv.gz Cell barcode ID list for high-quality real cells, corresponding to matrix columns peaks.bed.gz Peak position file in BED format (chromosome, start, end), corresponding to matrix rows matrix.mtx.gz Sparse count matrix in Matrix Market format, recording non-zero row/column indices and cutsite values

docs.title: Raw Peak Matrix (raw_peak_bc_matrix/)
docs.text:
Contains the unfiltered peak count matrix for all detected barcodes (including real cells and background droplets).

  • Core Purpose: Used to evaluate cell calling thresholds or apply custom filtering models.
  • Format: Identical structure to filtered_peak_bc_matrix/ in MEX format.

docs.title: Analysis Metrics Summary
docs.text: Core Content: Comprehensive quality assessment and statistical metrics covering sequencing, alignment, and cell calling.

docs.title: metrics_summary.xls
docs.text:
A structured table of key quality metrics in tab-delimited text format (TSV).

  • Core Purpose: Rapidly inspect data quality, alignment efficiency, cell yields, and chromatin accessibility enrichment.

  • Metric Categories:

    Metric Category Contents Sequencing Statistics Total raw read pairs, valid barcode fraction, Q30 base quality metrics Cell Calling Metrics Estimated number of cells, median fragments per cell, FRIP, TSS fraction, number of peaks Alignment & Structural Metrics Confidently mapped read pairs, mitochondrial ratio, nucleosome-free and mono-nucleosome fractions

  • Usage: Tab-delimited plain text; read with read.delim("metrics_summary.xls") in R or pd.read_csv("metrics_summary.xls", sep="\t") in Python. For metric descriptions and recommended benchmarks, refer to Web Report Interpretation.

docs.title: Peak Annotation
docs.text:
peak_annotation.tsv is a tab-delimited annotation table for filtered peaks. It is published when the filtered peaks.bed.gz and reference GTF are available and annotation succeeds. Annotation failures do not make this a mandatory output. A peak may have multiple gene associations, so the table is not guaranteed to have one row per matrix feature.

Fields Meaning chrom, start, end Peak coordinates, using 0-based start and exclusive end gene, gene_id Associated gene symbol and reference gene ID distance Signed distance from the associated TSS to the nearest peak base; zero for overlap, positive downstream along transcription peak_type Promoter/distal association or an intergenic/unannotated result genomic_region Genomic region classification gene_biotype, tss_source GTF gene biotype and annotation source of the selected TSS

Additional optional files: cell_classification.csv at the ATAC output root for mixed-species classification; whitelist_contamination.json and whitelist_contamination_cells.json when the C4 whitelist/low-targeting policy emits diagnostics (audit or apply). Multiplet is a mixed-species candidate and Unassigned means no confident species assignment. These are not confirmed biological doublet labels.

docs.title: singlecell.csv
docs.text:
Cell-level multi-dimensional QC and metadata table in CSV format.

  • Columns: Cell,totalFrags,fragments,mt_region_fragments,chloroplast_region_fragments,TSS_region_fragments,blacklist_region_fragments,peaks_number,peak_region_fragments,peak_region_cutsites,is_cell_barcode,Cellbarcode.
  • Core Purpose:
    • Fine-grained QC: Extract real cells by is_cell_barcode == 1, or apply custom secondary filtering on fragments and TSS proportions.
    • Downstream Metadata: Integrates directly as cell metadata (adata.obs in Scanpy or cell_metadata in ArchR/Signac).

totalFrags counts fragment-supporting read pairs including duplicate support; fragments counts deduplicated unique fragments. The report summary uses nuclear fragments for FRIP/TSS fractions. Targeting scatter plots instead divide by all unique fragments; the normalized TSS enrichment profile is a separate signal. Empty fragment gzip files may have no .tbi index. ATAC clustering objects remain in processing and are not published as an outs/analysis/ bundle.

docs.title: *_scATAC_report.html
docs.text:
Self-contained interactive visual analysis report in HTML format.

  • Core Purpose: Provides interactive charts for QC metrics, barcode rank curves, TSS profiles, fragment length periodicity, and cell clustering.
  • Convenient Sharing: Single offline file; opens directly in any desktop browser without an internet connection.

docs.title: Matrix Market Format (.mtx.gz)
docs.text:
The Matrix Market Exchange Format (MEX) is the community standard for storing sparse single-cell count matrices.

  • File Components:

    File Name Description matrix.mtx.gz Compressed sparse matrix. Header records dimensions and total non-zero entries; subsequent lines record row/column indices and values barcodes.tsv.gz Compressed barcode file; each row corresponds to a cell ID and matrix column peaks.bed.gz Compressed peak feature file; each row corresponds to a peak BED coordinate and matrix row

docs.title: Web Report Interpretation
docs.text:
Overview: The HTML report provides visual summaries and quality metrics for single-cell ATAC sequencing, covering library quality, chromatin structure, and downstream clustering.

Quality Assessment Principles & Guide

  • Holistic Assessment: The HTML report provides a comprehensive summary of scATAC results, spanning cell calling, sequencing fidelity, fragment length periodicity, TSS enrichment, and peak distribution.
  • Baseline Context: Benchmark thresholds reflect standard primary tissue samples. Actual metrics vary across tissue types (e.g., solid tumors, primary neural tissue, frozen nuclei), cell states, and sequencing depth. Interpret metrics in context.
  • Review Workflow: We recommend inspecting base sequencing quality and alignment first, followed by mitochondrial ratio, TSS enrichment, and FRIP, before verifying the biological plausibility of UMAP clusters.

docs.title: Cell Metrics
docs.text:
Core Function: Evaluates cell calling yield, library quality, and chromatin accessibility enrichment.

Quality Reference Benchmarks:

Metric Optimal Acceptable Suboptimal Median fragments per cell ≥ 10,000 2,000 – 10,000 < 2,000 Median fraction of fragments overlapping peaks ≥ 30% 15% – 30% < 15% Median fraction of fragments overlapping TSS ≥ 20% 10% – 20% < 10% Fraction fragments in cells ≥ 50% 20% – 50% < 20%

Detailed Metric Definitions & Interpretation:

Metric Calculation & Definition Interpretation & Troubleshooting Estimated number of cells Total number of high-confidence real cell barcodes identified after bead merging and filtering based on fragment count and TSS enrichment. Evaluate against targeted cell input. If substantially lower than expected, check cell viability, microfluidic encapsulation, or nuclear integrity. Species Reference organism and genome build used for alignment and annotation. First checkpoint to verify that reference genome configurations match the biological specimen. Median fragments per cell Median number of unique ATAC-seq fragments assigned to real cells. Core measure of per-cell sequencing depth and capture sensitivity. Optimal is ≥ 10,000 (minimum ≥ 2,000); low values reduce power in peak calling and clustering. Mean raw read pairs per cell Total raw read pairs / Estimated number of cells. Evaluates overall sequencing depth. Recommended ≥ 25,000 read pairs/cell to ensure sufficient chromatin coverage. Fraction overlapping peaks Median across called cells of peak_region_fragments / nuclear_fragments, where nuclear_fragments = fragments − mt_region_fragments − chloroplast_region_fragments; the implementation clips the denominator to at least 1. Gold standard for ATAC signal specificity and signal-to-noise ratio. Recommended ≥ 30%; < 15% indicates high ambient DNA background or poor transposition. Fraction overlapping TSS Median across called cells of TSS_region_fragments / nuclear_fragments for regions within ±1,000 bp of annotated TSSs. The denominator is the same as for the peak-overlap summary. Reflects promoter accessibility signal enrichment. Recommended ≥ 20%; < 10% suggests non-specific cleavage or chromatin degradation. Fraction of fragments in cells Sum of totalFrags for called cells / sum of totalFrags for all rows. This counts fragment-supporting read pairs including duplicate support, not deduplicated fragments. Measures real cellular signal relative to ambient background and empty droplets. Recommended ≥ 50%; low values suggest abundant cell-free chromatin debris. Number of peaks Total number of open chromatin peaks identified across all pooled high-quality cells. Typically ranges from 50,000 to 150,000, depending on cell heterogeneity, cell count, and sequencing depth.

docs.title: Sequencing Metrics
docs.text:
Core Function: Assesses primary sequencing quality, barcode validity, and alignment fidelity.

Quality Reference Benchmarks:

Metric Optimal Acceptable Suboptimal Valid barcodes ≥ 80% 70% – 80% < 70% Q30 bases in barcode > 85% 75% – 85% < 75% Q30 bases in read > 85% 75% – 85% < 75% Confidently mapped read pairs > 80% 50% – 80% < 50%

Detailed Metric Definitions & Interpretation:

Metric Calculation & Definition Interpretation & Troubleshooting Total number of reads pairs Total raw paired-end reads generated for the sample. Direct measure of total raw sequencing volume and baseline for sequencing depth. Valid barcodes Fraction of reads whose cell barcodes match the pre-defined whitelist (with error correction). Recommended ≥ 80%. Low fractions indicate barcode sequencing errors, primer abnormalities, or index drift.
