Confidently mapped read pairs Fraction of read pairs uniquely aligned to the reference genome. Recommended ≥ 80%. Values < 50% warrant checking for sample contamination, incorrect reference build, or excess repeat multi-mapping. Mitochondria reads ratio Percentage of aligned reads mapping to the mitochondrial genome. Core indicator of nuclear isolation purity. Unprotected mtDNA is hyper-accessible to Tn5; recommended < 10%, > 20% indicates nuclear envelope rupture. Nucleosome-free regions Percentage of transposition fragments shorter than 147 bp. Reflects active accessible chromatin at promoters and enhancers. Recommended > 40%; low values indicate under-transposition or chromatin compaction. Mono-nucleosome regions Percentage of fragments between 147 bp and 294 bp (spanning a single nucleosome). Complements nucleosome-free fragments to verify nucleosomal phase periodicity. Q30 bases in barcode Percentage of bases in barcode reads with Phred quality score ≥ 30 (error rate < 0.1%). Evaluates primary sequencing quality for cell identity assignment. Recommended > 85%. Q30 bases in read Percentage of genomic insert read bases with quality score ≥ 30. Determines alignment fidelity and peak boundary resolution.

docs.title: Interactive Visualization Charts
docs.text: The HTML report includes multi-dimensional interactive charts covering cell QC, chromatin periodicity, and clustering.

docs.title: 1. Barcode Rank Plot
docs.text:
Chart Function: Displays cumulative fragments across all cell barcodes ranked in descending order to separate real cells from background noise.

How to Interpret:

  • Axes:
    • X-axis (Barcode Rank): All barcodes ranked by peak fragment count in descending order (log scale).
    • Y-axis (Fragment Counts): Fragment count per barcode (log scale).
  • Knee Point Characteristics:
    • High-quality libraries exhibit a steep cliff-like inflection (knee point).
    • Blue region: High-confidence real cells identified by the calling algorithm.
    • Gray region: Background ambient fragments and empty droplets.
  • Interactive Features: Hover to inspect individual barcode rankings; blue color gradient reflects local cell density.

docs.title: 2. Droplet Beads Distribution
docs.text:
Chart Function: Displays the distribution of bead counts captured per real cell droplet.

How to Interpret:

  • Theoretical Model: Microfluidic co-encapsulation follows a Poisson distribution, reflecting random capture mechanics.
  • Practical Context: Deviations reflect microfluidic droplet uniformity, cell suspension concentration, or sequencing saturation.

docs.title: 3. Cell Data Distribution
docs.text:
Chart Function: Displays violin plots for real cells across three core metrics: Fragments, TSS Proportion, and Peak Proportion.

How to Interpret:

  • Violin Shape: Width represents cell density; wider bodies indicate consistent cell properties. Internal box plots show medians and quartiles.
  • Quality Guidance: Higher centers for Fragments and TSS/Peak proportions indicate robust signal and low noise.

docs.title: 4. Fragment Length Distribution
docs.text:
Chart Function: Plots the frequency distribution of deduplicated fragment insert sizes, serving as a structural "fingerprint" of chromatin integrity.

How to Interpret:

  • Periodicity Peaks:
    • < 147 bp (First peak): Nucleosome-Free Regions (NFR), enriched in promoters and active enhancers.
    • ~200 bp (Second peak): Mono-nucleosomal fragments.
    • ~400 bp / ~600 bp (Subsequent peaks): Di-nucleosomal and multi-nucleosomal fragments.
  • QC Interpretation: High-quality libraries exhibit prominent NFR peaks and distinct ~200 bp periodicity; flat curves indicate over-lysis or chromatin degradation.

docs.title: 5. Cluster Analysis
docs.text:
Chart Function: Visualizes cell chromatin accessibility patterns in 2D space using Latent Semantic Indexing (LSI) dimensionality reduction and UMAP projection.

How to Interpret:

  • Left Plot (Cell Clusters): Each dot represents a cell colored by cluster identity. Distinct separation reflects successful capture of epigenetic heterogeneity.
  • Right Plot (Fragment Depth): Colors cells by fragment count to check whether clusters are driven by sequencing depth artifacts.

docs.title: 6. TSS Enrichment Profile
docs.text:
Chart Function: Aggregates Tn5 cleavage frequencies across ±1,000 bp of all annotated TSS sites to quantify chromatin signal-to-noise ratio.

How to Interpret:

  • Axes: X-axis is distance from TSS (0 = TSS center); Y-axis is normalized insertion signal.
  • Peak Shape: High-quality samples show a sharp, symmetrical peak at TSS center with rapid decay to baseline.
  • Enrichment Score: Higher scores (> 4–6) indicate excellent signal-to-noise; flat profiles suggest sample degradation or poor transposition.

docs.title: 7. Single Cell Targeting Plot
docs.text:
Chart Function: Bivariate scatter plot of total fragments (X-axis, log scale) vs. TSS enrichment score (Y-axis).

How to Interpret: Real cells cluster in the top-right quadrant (high fragments + high TSS enrichment); background noise clusters in the bottom-left. Ideal datasets show a clear bimodal separation.

docs.title: 8. Saturation Curve
docs.text:
Chart Function: Evaluates sequencing depth sufficiency and library complexity yield.

How to Interpret: * Axes: X-axis is mean read pairs per cell; Y-axis is median unique fragments per cell. * Curve Behavior: A steep linear phase indicates high discovery of new unique fragments; a flattening plateau indicates library saturation (20%–50% duplication rate is a typical cost-effective target).

docs.title: 9. Bead Similarity Ranking
docs.text:
Chart Function: Ranks bead pairs by Jaccard similarity to merge barcodes originating from the same multi-bead droplet.

How to Interpret: * Blue region: Bead pairs with similarity above the Otsu threshold are merged as single-cell origins. * Gray region: Pairs below threshold are retained as distinct cells.

docs.title: 10. Additional Algorithmic Metrics
docs.text: Metric Definition & Computation Interpretation & Guidance Percent duplicates Fraction of aligned fragments flagged as PCR duplicates. Reflects library complexity and depth saturation. Typically 20%–50%; > 50% indicates near saturation with diminishing returns for further sequencing; < 15% suggests potential benefit from deeper sequencing. Jaccard threshold Similarity threshold used to determine whether two beads originated from the same droplet. In multi-bead droplet platforms, calculated adaptively via Otsu's method (floored at 0.02) to merge split barcodes and prevent artificial doublets.

docs.title: scRNA Analysis Output
docs.text:
Output scope: Directory trees describe a typical completed run. Optional outputs depend on enabled modules and successful stages. Quality ranges below are interpretation guidance, not software pass/fail rules; use the configured thresholds and report status for this run.

Single-Cell RNA Sequencing Output File Guide

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: After the single-cell RNA analysis is complete, a standardized file and subdirectory structure is generated in the specified output directory for gene expression profiling, clustering, and cell type identification. Matrix and annotation files can be imported into tools such as Scanpy and Seurat using the appropriate format readers. See Downstream Analysis for loading examples.

docs.title: Core Deliverables At-a-Glance
docs.text:
The table below summarizes the core deliverables, file formats, primary purposes, and recommended downstream ecosystem integrations for scRNA analysis:

Deliverable & Core Files Format Primary Purpose & Downstream Ecosystem Integration Gene Expression Matrices• filtered_feature_bc_matrix/• filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5• filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5ad MEXH5H5AD High-confidence expression quantification for true cells; primary input for downstream analysis.• R (Seurat): Read10X() / Read10X_h5()• Python (Scanpy): read_h5ad() / read_10x_h5() / read_10x_mtx() Raw Unfiltered Matrices• raw_feature_bc_matrix/• raw_feature_bc_matrix.h5 MEXH5 Complete expression counts across all candidate droplets and background; for custom EmptyDrops cell calling and QC auditing. Clustering & Cell Phenotyping• analysis/QC_Cluster.h5ad• analysis/cluster.csv• analysis/marker.csv H5ADCSV Contains dimensionality reduction coordinates (UMAP/t-SNE), graph clustering clusters, and marker gene lists.• Recommended: Scanpy / statistical visualization Single-Cell Metadata Table• singlecell.csv CSV Detailed metrics per bead/droplet (sequencing reads, genes, UMIs, and called cell flag).• Analysis Note: Filter via is_cell_barcode; primary input for V(D)J linkage. Experiment Metrics Summary• metrics_summary.xls TSV Text Global sequencing, alignment, cell count, and median UMI quality metrics.• Loading Guide: Tab-delimited text; use read.delim() in R, pd.read_csv(sep='\t') in Python. Interactive HTML Report• <sample>_scRNA_report.html HTML Standalone interactive web report displaying barcode rank plots, UMAP clusters, and sequencing metrics.• Viewing: Offline-ready; open directly in any modern desktop web browser. Genomic Alignment BAM• anno_decon_sorted.bam• anno_decon_sorted.bam.bai (or .csi) BAMBAI / CSI Coordinate-sorted BAM file with error-corrected single-cell tags (CB, UB, GN).• Ecosystem Integration: Supports IGV browsing, samtools queries, and RNA velocity (Velocyto). Mixed-Species Classification• analysis/cell_classification.csv CSV Classifies cell species origins and multiplet rates in mixed-species experiments (e.g. human-mouse).• Generation: Created only when analyzing mixed-species reference genomes.

docs.title: Output Directory Structure
docs.text:
outs/
├── filtered_feature_bc_matrix/              # High-confidence filtered gene expression matrix directory (MEX)
│   ├── barcodes.tsv.gz                      # High-confidence called cell IDs
│   ├── features.tsv.gz                      # Gene IDs, names, and feature types
│   └── matrix.mtx.gz                        # Sparse expression count matrix
├── filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5            # Filtered expression matrix (Single HDF5 file, preferred for Seurat)
├── filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5ad          # Filtered expression matrix (AnnData format, preferred for Scanpy)
├── raw_feature_bc_matrix/                   # Unfiltered raw gene expression matrix directory (MEX, all droplets)
│   ├── barcodes.tsv.gz
│   ├── features.tsv.gz
│   └── matrix.mtx.gz
├── raw_feature_bc_matrix.h5                 # Unfiltered raw gene expression matrix (Single HDF5 file)
├── analysis/                                # Downstream clustering and marker gene results
│   ├── QC_Cluster.h5ad                      # Complete AnnData object with QC, reduction, clustering, and markers
│   ├── cluster.csv                          # Cell cluster assignments and 2D UMAP coordinates
│   ├── marker.csv                           # Differentially expressed marker gene table per cluster
│   └── cell_classification.csv              # Species assignment and multiplet calls (mixed-species runs only)
├── singlecell.csv                           # Comprehensive single-cell metadata and droplet metrics
├── metrics_summary.xls                      # Experiment-level QC and sequencing metrics summary (TSV)
├── <sample>_scRNA_report.html               # Interactive HTML quality and clustering report
├── anno_decon_sorted.bam                    # Coordinate-sorted alignment BAM file (when BAM enabled)
├── anno_decon_sorted.bam.bai                # BAM index file (automatically switches to .csi for large chromosomes)
└── oligo.records.bam                        # Oligo alignment records (when BAM enabled with an oligo library)

Version Delivery Notes

filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5ad contains filtered count data. BAM indexes automatically generate as BAI or CSI based on chromosome lengths. Passing --no_bam skips both cDNA and oligo BAM generation to save ~70% disk space. For Sample Barcode multiplexed C6 outputs, see C6 Outputs.

docs.title: 1. Feature & Expression Matrix Files
docs.text:
Core Content: Single-cell gene expression count matrices, available as filtered high-quality cell datasets and unfiltered raw candidate datasets across MEX, H5, and H5AD standard formats.

Bead Merging & Cell Identifiers

In the DNBelab C system, droplets containing multiple beads are merged and designated as CELL<number>_N<bead_count> (e.g., CELL1118_N3; single beads are _N1). The CB tag in delivered BAM files and the cell names in barcodes.tsv.gz use these merged Cell IDs, while singlecell.csv retains the semicolon-separated raw bead barcodes.

docs.title: Filtered Gene Expression Matrix (filtered_feature_bc_matrix/)
docs.text:
Contains gene expression counts for cells identified by EmptyDrops quality filtering, serving as the primary input for downstream clustering, differential expression, and cell type annotation.

Delivered in the standard Matrix Market Exchange (MEX) sparse format, consisting of three compressed files:

File Name Format Content Description & Mapping matrix.mtx.gz MatrixMarket text (gzip compressed) Sparse expression matrix. Header specifies rows, columns, and non-zero counts; subsequent lines record non-zero coordinates and counts (row col value). Only non-zero values are stored. barcodes.tsv.gz Single-column plain text (gzip compressed) High-quality called cell IDs (e.g. CELL1_N2), where each line corresponds to the column index of the matrix. features.tsv.gz Three-column tab-delimited text (gzip compressed) Feature (gene) annotations including Gene ID, Gene Name, and Feature Type (Gene Expression), corresponding to the row index of the matrix.
  • Quick Loading Example:
  • R (Seurat): 
    library(Seurat)
counts <- Read10X(data.dir = "filtered_feature_bc_matrix")
seu <- CreateSeuratObject(counts = counts)
  • Python (Scanpy): 
    import scanpy as sc
adata = sc.read_10x_mtx("filtered_feature_bc_matrix", var_names="gene_symbols")

docs.title: Single-File HDF5 Expression Matrix (filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5)
docs.text:
Encapsulates the sparse count matrix, cell barcodes, and gene features into a single compressed HDF5 binary file. - Recommended Usage: Fast cross-platform single-file loading in both R (Seurat) and Python (Scanpy). - Quick Loading Example: - R (Seurat): 

library(Seurat)
counts <- Read10X_h5("filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5")
seu <- CreateSeuratObject(counts = counts)
- Python (Scanpy): 
import scanpy as sc
adata = sc.read_10x_h5("filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5")

docs.title: AnnData Expression Matrix (filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5ad)
docs.text:
Dedicated binary format for Python single-cell ecosystems, packaging the count matrix X, cellular metadata obs, and gene annotations var. - Recommended Usage: The preferred format for Python (Scanpy / scvi-tools) workflows. - Quick Loading Example: 

import scanpy as sc
adata = sc.read_h5ad("filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5ad")

AnnData internal slots are organized as follows:

Component Saved Content X Cell-by-gene raw counts (n_cells × n_genes) exported before downstream QC and normalization obs Cell/barcode identifiers; this export does not guarantee downstream QC or annotation fields var Gene metadata available from the input matrix, such as gene_ids and feature_types

filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5ad is a count-matrix export, not the clustering object. PCA/UMAP embeddings, cluster labels, and marker statistics belong to analysis/QC_Cluster.h5ad when those analysis steps complete. Spliced/unspliced layers are not generated by this workflow.

docs.title: Raw Unfiltered Expression Matrix (raw_feature_bc_matrix/ & .h5)
docs.text: Contains the complete expression count matrix for all detected barcodes without quality filtering. - Core Purpose: Preserves data from authentic cells, damaged cells, and background ambient droplets; ideal for evaluating barcode rank plots, testing custom empty-droplet calling algorithms, or setting customized filtering cutoffs.

docs.title: 2. Analysis Results Directory (analysis/)
docs.text: Core Content: Automated downstream analysis outputs, including PCA/UMAP embeddings, graph-based clustering, differential marker genes, and mixed-species cell assignments.

docs.title: QC_Cluster.h5ad
docs.text:
A fully analyzed AnnData object containing normalized counts, highly variable genes, PCA, neighborhood graphs, Leiden/Louvain clusters, and UMAP projections. - Core Purpose: Integrates the expression matrix with all downstream analysis results. Directly loadable in Python to replicate report plots and downstream exploration without re-running time-consuming clustering pipelines. - Key Components: - adata.obs['leiden']: Cluster assignment per cell; - adata.obsm['X_umap']: 2D UMAP scatter coordinates; - adata.uns['rank_genes_groups']: Statistical marker gene tables per cluster.

Only analysis steps that complete contribute fields to QC_Cluster.h5ad; small or empty datasets may have empty marker tables or reduced analysis results. The count export at the output root remains distinct from this processed analysis object.

docs.title: cluster.csv
docs.text: Cell clustering results table exported in CSV format. - Column Descriptions: - First CSV column (row index): Cell identifier; the column is not guaranteed to be named Barcode; - leiden: Cluster ID; Cluster: display label including the cluster cell count; - UMAP_1, UMAP_2: 2D coordinates from UMAP projection; - nGene, nUMI: Number of detected genes and total UMIs for the cell.

docs.title: marker.csv
docs.text:
Differentially expressed marker genes identified for each cell cluster (CSV format), used for cell type annotation and functional enrichment. - Column Descriptions: - cluster: Target cluster identifier; - gene: Gene symbol; - avg_log2FC: Average log2 fold change compared to all other clusters; - p_val_adj: Adjusted p-values returned by Scanpy rank_genes_groups; - pct.1: Percentage of cells expressing the gene in the target cluster; - pct.2: Percentage of cells expressing the gene across other clusters.

marker.csv contains positive markers with non-null log fold changes and p_val_adj < 0.05, sorted by log fold change, with at most 50 genes retained per cluster. An empty table does not by itself indicate a missing export.

docs.title: cell_classification.csv (Mixed-Species Runs Only)
docs.text:
Generated when aligning against dual-species references (e.g., human-mouse hg38 + mm10), classifying the species identity of each barcode. - Column Descriptions: - barcode: Cell barcode identifier; - <species1> (e.g., hg38): UMI count aligned to the first species; - <species2> (e.g., mm10): UMI count aligned to the second species; - call: Final species call (hg38, mm10, Multiplet, or Unassigned). Multiplet denotes a cross-species mixed candidate, not a confirmed biological doublet.

Data Example:

barcode,hg38,mm10,call
CELL1_N2,17098,821,hg38
CELL2_N8,56978,1939,hg38
CELL5_N2,868,4216,mm10
CELL8_N2,2371,71601,mm10
CELL27_N3,64247,90800,Multiplet

docs.title: 3. Analysis Metrics Summary & Single-Cell Table
docs.text: Core Content: Overall experiment-level quality evaluation summaries, single-cell level QC metrics, and the interactive HTML report.

docs.title: *_scRNA_report.html
docs.text: All-in-one interactive web report. - Core Purpose: Standalone HTML viewable in any desktop browser offline, visualizing barcode rank plots, UMAP clusters, top marker heatmaps, and sequencing/alignment quality metrics. For chart interpretations, see Web Report Interpretation below.

docs.title: metrics_summary.xls
docs.text: Key sequencing and analysis quality summary table. Despite the .xls file extension, the underlying format is standard tab-separated text (TSV). - Core Purpose: Summarizes overall experiment statistics including sequencing quality, mapping rates, cell count, mean reads per cell, and median genes/UMIs. - Loading Guideline: Use read.delim("metrics_summary.xls", check.names = FALSE) in R, and pd.read_csv("metrics_summary.xls", sep="\t") in Python.

docs.title: singlecell.csv
docs.text: Comprehensive single-cell level quality control metrics table in CSV format. - Core Purpose: Contains detailed metrics across every detected droplet and bead, allowing customized secondary filtering and serving as the cell whitelist input for V(D)J immune repertoire analysis (via --beadstrans). - Key Fields: - cell: Aggregated cell identifier (e.g. CELL1_N2); - barcode: Raw bead barcode sequence(s) (multiple beads separated by ;); - reads: Total transcriptomic reads assigned to the droplet; - gene: Number of distinct genes detected; - umi: Total transcript molecules (UMIs) detected; - is_cell_barcode: Authentic cell flag (1 or True indicates a called cell; 0 or False indicates background; unmatched groups may have blank cell IDs and flags).

docs.title: 4. Genomic Alignment and Annotation Files
docs.text: Core Content: Coordinate-sorted BAM alignment files with index, enriched with single-cell and genomic annotation tags.

docs.title: anno_decon_sorted.bam
docs.text:
Coordinate-sorted alignment file in Binary Alignment Map (BAM) format. - Core Purpose: Inspect alignment coverage and splicing patterns in genome browsers such as IGV; provides raw inputs for variant calling, alternative splicing, and RNA velocity (Velocyto). - Skipping BAM Generation: BAM files require substantial storage; if only gene expression matrices are needed, pass --no_bam at run time to save ~70% disk space.

Key TAG Field Descriptions:

The BAM file stores single-cell metadata and gene annotations using standard SAM tags:

Tag Type Description and Function CB String Error-corrected unified Cell ID (final cell ID after bead merging, e.g. CELL1_N2, matching matrix column names) CC String Error-corrected cellular barcode sequence CR String Raw cellular barcode sequence reported by the sequencer CY String Phred sequencing quality score for cellular barcode UB String Processed UMI sequence; its presence does not mean that BAM records have been reduced to one record per molecule UR String Raw UMI sequence reported by the sequencer UY String Phred sequencing quality score for UMI GX String Gene ID from the reference annotation (not necessarily an Ensembl ID) GN String Gene symbol / name TX String Mapped transcript identifier (Transcript ID) AN String Antisense transcript flag (used to assess strand specificity) RE Character (A) Genomic alignment region: exonic (E), intronic (N), or intergenic (I)

docs.title: anno_decon_sorted.bam.bai (or .csi)
docs.text:
Index file for anno_decon_sorted.bam, enabling fast random access to genomic intervals. - Adaptive Indexing: - Standard .bai index is generated when the maximum reference chromosome length is ≤ 2^29 bases (536,870,912 bp); - Automatically switches to .csi indexing for large chromosomes or artificial contigs (> 2^29 bp).

Header-only zero-result RNA BAMs may be published without a coordinate index.

docs.title: oligo.records.bam
docs.text: Generated when an oligo capture library is sequenced and --no_bam is not specified, recording oligo alignment and barcode matching details.

docs.title: Web Report Interpretation
docs.text:
The interactive HTML web report (report.html) generated by dnbc4tools provides a comprehensive visual entry point for reviewing experimental quality and downstream analysis performance. The report presents end-to-end quality metrics and interactive charts spanning sequencing quality, genomic alignment, cell identification, clustering, and biological annotation.

Quality Assessment Principles & Review Guide

  • Macro to Micro: It is recommended to review overall summary metrics (cell count, sequencing throughput, mapping rates) first, followed by in-depth examination of violin plots, barcode knee curves, and UMAP clustering.
  • Contextual Evaluation: Reference thresholds are based on standard mammalian cell preparation experience. Quality assessment should account for tissue type (e.g., solid tumor vs. peripheral blood), cell viability, and experimental goals.
  • Metric Denominators: Read-pair counts, valid-barcode transcriptomic reads, called-cell molecule-supporting reads, and per-region base counts are different denominators. Use each metric definition; percentages must not all be normalized to raw input reads.

docs.title: Detailed Explanation of Core Analysis Metrics
Cell Metrics
docs.text:
Cell metrics evaluate single-cell capture efficiency, cell calling sensitivity, and per-cell transcript detection levels.

Quality Control Reference Standards:

Metric Recommended Acceptable Needs Investigation Key Focus Mean reads per cell ≥ 30,000 15,000 – 30,000 < 15,000 Whether sequencing depth is sufficient for stable subpopulation clustering Median genes per cell ≥ 1,000 500 – 1,000 < 500 Single-cell transcriptome complexity and informational content Fraction reads in cells ≥ 60% 30% – 60% < 30% Ambient RNA contamination level and cell membrane integrity Sequencing saturation ≥ 40% 20% – 40% < 20% Library coverage depth and marginal returns of additional sequencing

Detailed Metric Definitions & Technical Guidelines:

Metric Calculation & Statistical Definition Interpretation Guide & Troubleshooting Estimated number of cells Total number of valid, high-confidence real cells identified from sequencing data. Determined using barcode UMI rank curves combined with the EmptyDrops model to distinguish true cells from background noise. Evaluate in conjunction with cell input quantity and viability. If substantially lower than expected, inspect for microfluidic clogging, excessive cell lysis, or insufficient sequencing depth. Species Reference genome species identifier designated for the pipeline (e.g., Human GRCh38 or Mouse GRCm38). Verify that the reference genome matches the actual biological sample, which is fundamental to all quantification and QC metrics. Mean reads per cell Number of reads / Estimated number of cells. Recommended ≥ 30,000. Low values reduce sensitivity for low-abundance transcripts and degrade subpopulation clustering stability. Median/Mean UMI per cell Median and mean unique transcript molecule (UMI) counts captured per identified true cell. Directly reflects single-cell transcript molecular yield. Substantially influenced by cell size and lineage (e.g., plasma cells or tumor cells are typically much higher than resting lymphocytes). Median/Mean genes per cell Median and mean number of distinct genes detected (UMI ≥ 1) per cell. Assesses transcriptome complexity per cell. Naturally lower in small or quiescent cells (e.g., PBMCs) and higher in metabolically active tissue cells. Total genes detected Total number of genes with at least 1 valid UMI count across the entire cell population. Measures overall transcriptome breadth and sample heterogeneity. Unusually low numbers indicate under-sequencing or homogeneous cell composition. Fraction reads in cells Called-cell confidently mapped transcriptomic reads / all confidently mapped transcriptomic reads with valid barcodes; use the report metric rather than summing raw singlecell.csv reads. Recommended ≥ 60%. Lower fractions indicate elevated ambient RNA background from cell lysis, or a high proportion of cell-free beads. Sequencing saturation 1 − distinct molecules / supporting reads within called cells. Molecules are distinguished by cell barcode, gene, and corrected UMI. Recommended 40%–85%. Reflects library sequencing completeness. Below 40% indicates strong potential for additional gene discovery; above 85% suggests near-complete library saturation.

docs.title: Sequencing Metrics
docs.text:
Sequencing metrics evaluate the raw instrument output quality, including barcode validity, UMI integrity, and base accuracy.

Quality Control Reference Standards:

Metric Recommended Acceptable Needs Investigation Key Focus Valid barcodes ≥ 80% 70% – 80% < 70% Barcode matching rate; < 70% indicates library or run issues Valid UMIs ≥ 80% 70% – 80% < 70% Molecular barcode synthesis quality and sequencing fidelity Q30 Base Quality ≥ 85% 75% – 85% < 75% Phred quality score, governing alignment and error correction

Detailed Metric Definitions & Technical Guidelines:

Metric Calculation & Statistical Definition Interpretation Guide & Troubleshooting Number of reads Total paired-end sequencing read pairs allocated to this sample. Measures input cDNA sequencing volume and is used for raw mean reads per cell; other rates have metric-specific denominators. Valid barcodes Percentage of reads whose cell barcodes match the preset whitelist directly or within 1-bp mismatch tolerance. Recommended ≥ 80%. Low rates typically indicate barcode sequencing errors, adaptor contamination, primer synthesis defects, or library anomalies. Valid UMIs Percentage of reads whose UMI sequences contain no uncertain N bases and are not single-base homopolymers (e.g., AAAAAA). Ensures molecular tags can reliably deduplicate PCR artifacts. Unusually low values warrant inspection of UMI read cycle quality. Q30 bases in barcode / UMI / read Percentage of bases with Phred quality scores ≥ 30 (error rate < 0.1%) in barcode, UMI, and cDNA read segments. Recommended ≥ 85%. Low Read Q30 decreases alignment confidence; low Barcode/UMI Q30 compromises error correction accuracy.

docs.title: Mapping Metrics
docs.text:
Mapping metrics assess alignment performance against the reference genome, including overall alignment rate, transcriptome confidence, and structural genomic distributions.

Quality Control Reference Standards:

Metric Recommended Acceptable Needs Investigation Key Focus Reads mapped to genome ≥ 80% 50% – 80% < 50% Overall alignment rate; low rate implies reference mismatch, contamination, or excessive rRNA multi-mapping Reads mapped confidently to transcriptome ≥ 50% 30% – 50% < 30% Core informative reads eligible for gene expression quantification Reads mapped antisense to gene < 10% 10% – 30% > 30% Antisense rate; high values suggest compromised strand specificity

Detailed Metric Definitions & Technical Guidelines:

Metric Calculation & Statistical Definition Interpretation Guide & Troubleshooting Reads mapped to genome Fraction of reads successfully aligned to the reference genome (including both unique and multi-mapped reads). Recommended ≥ 80%. If < 50%, check for foreign contamination (e.g., mycoplasma/bacteria), incorrect species reference, or multi-mapping dropouts (too many loci) from high rRNA contamination. Reads mapped confidently to genome Fraction of reads uniquely aligned with high quality (STAR MAPQ = 255) to a single genomic locus. Measures high-confidence unique genomic output. Multi-mapping reads are rescued only if one locus is exonic while all others are non-exonic. Reads mapped confidently to transcriptome Fraction of reads uniquely and confidently mapped to a single distinct gene model (spanning both exonic and intronic regions). Represents reads directly usable for gene expression quantification. Reads falling into overlapping multi-gene regions are filtered out to prevent ambiguity. Reads mapped confidently to exonic regions Fraction of confidently genome-mapped reads where at least 50% of bases intersect annotated exons. Represents mature spliced mRNA in standard whole-cell scRNA-seq; interpret alongside intronic rates when values appear low. Reads mapped confidently to intronic regions Fraction of confidently genome-mapped reads intersecting introns that do not meet the exonic threshold. Captures unspliced pre-mRNA. In single-nucleus RNA-seq (snRNA-seq), this fraction naturally reaches 30%–60%, which is expected biology. Reads mapped confidently to intergenic regions Fraction of confidently genome-mapped reads that do not intersect any annotated genes (neither exons nor introns). Recommended < 10%. High percentages indicate genomic DNA contamination, non-specific PCR amplification, or incomplete gene annotations. Reads mapped antisense to gene Fraction of reads aligning to gene loci on the opposite strand of annotated transcription. Recommended < 10%. Higher values indicate natural antisense transcripts, non-specific primer annealing, or library strand-inversion artifacts. Include introns Gene quantification mode toggle: True (default, counts intronic reads) / False (exonic reads only). Enabled by default to capture nascent transcripts and boost detection sensitivity (especially for snRNA-seq); can be disabled for strictly mature mRNA studies.

docs.title: Visualization Chart Group One: Cell Quality Control Analysis
Barcode Rank Plot (Knee Plot)
docs.text:
Ranks all cell barcodes in descending order of UMI counts to visually delineate high-quality authentic cells from background noise.

  • Visual Encoding: Deep blue curve represents identified valid cells; grey curve represents background noise or empty droplets; the blue gradient band marks the EmptyDrops transition boundary.
  • Axes & Interactivity: X-axis is Barcode Rank (descending UMI order, log scale); Y-axis is UMI Counts (log scale). Hovering displays rank position, UMI counts, and local cell fraction.
  • Quality Interpretation:
    • Ideal Pattern: Displays a sharp, distinct "knee point" where the curve drops steeply from a high plateau into a gentle background slope, indicating clean separation between cells and ambient RNA.
    • Troubleshooting: A flat curve without a clear inflection point indicates excessive ambient RNA, severe cell breakage, or inadequate cell input.

docs.title: Droplet Beads Distribution
docs.text:
Displays the frequency distribution of captured bead barcodes per real cell droplet.

  • Theoretical Distribution: Microfluidic bead capture follows a Poisson distribution.
  • Key Takeaways: Single-bead droplets should comprise the vast majority. Abnormally high multiple-bead fractions indicate excessive bead loading concentrations, insufficient mixing, or bead clumping.

docs.title: Cell Data Distribution (Violin Plots)
docs.text:
Presents three side-by-side violin plots (displayed at the bottom-right of the web report Summary page) displaying the distribution of Gene counts (nGenes), UMI counts (nUMI), and Mitochondrial percentage (percent.mt) in filtered true cells.

  • Gene & UMI Counts (nGenes / nUMI): A higher violin peak indicates superior capture efficiency and library complexity. Bimodal distributions typically indicate distinct subpopulation sizes or presence of doublets.
  • Mitochondrial Percentage (percent.mt): High-quality cells should predominantly exhibit low mitochondrial percentages (typically < 10%–20%). Elevated levels indicate stressed, dying, or ruptured cells where cytoplasmic mRNA was partially lost.

docs.title: Visualization Chart Group Two: Downstream Biological Analysis
docs.text: The Analysis page of the web report concentrates downstream results including UMAP dimensionality reduction, marker gene tables/heatmaps, cell type annotation, and sequencing saturation curves.

docs.title: Cell Clustering Analysis (UMAP)
docs.text:
Projects cells onto a 2D UMAP space based on highly variable gene selection, PCA dimensionality reduction, and Louvain/Leiden graph clustering.

  • Left Panel (Cluster Subpopulations): Each dot represents a single cell; distinct colors indicate different cell clusters. Spatial proximity reflects transcriptomic similarity.
  • Right Panel (UMI Depth Distribution): Overlays total UMI counts onto the identical UMAP coordinates using color gradients. Helps identify spurious clusters driven purely by sequencing depth disparities or low-quality cells.

docs.title: Marker Gene Analysis
docs.text:
Provides a differential expression table and heatmap highlighting characteristic marker genes for each subpopulation cluster.

  • Core Metric Definitions:
    • p_val & p_val_adj: Raw test P-value and the adjusted P-value returned by Scanpy rank_genes_groups; marker export uses p_val_adj < 0.05.
    • avg_log2FC: Average log2 fold change, quantifying marker enrichment relative to all other clusters.
    • pct.1 / pct.2: Fraction of cells expressing the gene in the target cluster versus all other clusters (pct.1 near 1 and pct.2 near 0 represents an ideal specific marker).
  • Interactive Features: Filter table by cluster dropdown and search for specific genes of interest in real time.

docs.title: Automated Cell Type Annotation
docs.text:
Assigns predicted cell identities to each cluster based on reference databases (e.g., human scHCL, mouse scMCA).

  • Species Scope: Currently supports Human and Mouse; other species do not generate automated annotation labels.
  • Interpretation Advice: Automatic predictions serve as initial references; always validate using canonical marker genes and biological domain literature.

docs.title: Sequencing Saturation Curve
docs.text:
Evaluates whether sequencing depth is approaching saturation, guiding decisions on whether additional sequencing is beneficial.

  • Coordinate System: X-axis shows Mean Reads per Cell; Y-axis shows sequencing saturation or median genes detected.
  • Trend Interpretation:
    • Plateau Phase: A flattening curve indicates diminishing marginal returns from additional sequencing.
    • Steep Ascent: An ascending curve suggests that substantial undiscovered transcript diversity remains and further sequencing will yield meaningful gains.

docs.title: Dual-Species Assignment Page (Dual-Species Mode Only)
docs.text:
When utilizing a joint reference genome (e.g., hg38 + mm10), the web report activates a specialized species assignment panel to evaluate microfluidic multiplet rates and cross-species separation.

  • Droplet Overview (Top-Left):
    • Droplets with >0 Cell: Total droplets containing at least one captured cell.
    • Droplets with >1 Cell (Observed / Inferred): Observed and statistically inferred doublet/multiplet droplet counts.
    • Fraction Droplets with >1 Cell: Inferred multiplet percentage; elevated values point to cell overloading or incomplete single-cell dissociation.
  • Cell UMI Counts Scatter (Top-Right):
    • X-axis shows Species A (e.g., hg38) UMI counts; Y-axis shows Species B (e.g., mm10) UMI counts.
    • Points along either axis represent pure single cells; points along the diagonal represent cross-species multiplets.
  • Summary Panel (Bottom):
    • Reports cell counts, median UMI/gene statistics, and alignment metrics separately for Species A and Species B. Severe divergence between species flags uneven loading or differential viability.
  • Downstream Recommendations:
    • Exclude call == "Multiplet" cells prior to downstream clustering.
    • Combine with analysis/cell_classification.csv for fine-grained custom filtering.

docs.title: scVDJ Analysis Output
docs.text:
Output scope: Directory trees describe a typical completed run. Optional outputs depend on enabled modules and successful stages. Quality ranges below are interpretation guidance, not software pass/fail rules; use the configured thresholds and report status for this run.

Single-Cell V(D)J Sequencing Output File Guide

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
After single-cell V(D)J analysis is complete, a standardized set of files and subdirectories is generated in the specified output directory for immune receptor repertoire analysis. All output files adhere to international AIRR Community standards and are fully compatible with mainstream single-cell immunoinformatics tools (such as scRepertoire, immunarch, and scirpy).

Tip: Two modes are supported: provide --beadstrans to use an RNA cell table for bead mapping and RNA-based cell filtering; or omit it to run VDJ without an RNA cell table. When omitted, keep_all_cells is enabled automatically, so assembled barcodes are not filtered by RNA cell calls and must not be treated as an RNA-confirmed cell set.

docs.title: Deliverables at a Glance
docs.text:
The table below summarizes the key deliverables of scVDJ analysis, file formats, primary use cases, and recommended downstream ecosystem integrations:

Deliverable & Core Files Format Description & Ecosystem Integration Filtered Contig Annotations• filtered_contig_annotations.csv CSV High-confidence contig annotations from real cells; primary entry point for downstream clonotype and receptor analyses.• Ecosystem: Directly compatible with R (scRepertoire) and Python (scirpy). Filtered Contig Sequences• filtered_contig.fasta• filtered_contig.fasta.fai FASTAFAI Index Nucleotide sequences and index for high-confidence real cell contigs, used for BLAST searches or synthesis validation. AIRR Standard Annotations• airr_annotations.tsv TSV Text Immune receptor repertoire annotations adhering strictly to international AIRR Community standards.• Ecosystem: Directly supported by Immcantation, Change-O, immunarch, and downstream pipelines. Clonotype Statistics• clonotypes.csv CSV Summary of identified clonotypes, recording cell frequencies, proportions, and paired CDR3 sequences. Consensus Sequences & Annotations• consensus_annotations.csv• consensus.fasta (and .fai) CSVFASTA Detailed annotations and representative nucleotide sequences for each consensus clonotype. All Assembled Contigs (Unfiltered)• all_contig_annotations.csv• all_contig.fasta (and .fai) CSVFASTA Unfiltered contigs (including low-confidence, non-productive, and background droplets) for quality audit and algorithmic traceback. Analysis Metrics Summary• metrics_summary.xls TSV Text Global summary of sequencing quality, cell yield, V(D)J mapping rates, and productive pairing percentages.• Format: Tab-delimited text; read with read.delim() in R or pd.read_csv(sep='\t') in Python. Interactive Web Report• <sample>_scVDJ_TR(IG)_report.html HTML Comprehensive offline visual report for reviewing barcode rank curves, V(D)J enrichment, and top 10 dominant clonotypes.• How to Open: No internet connection required; double-click to open in any desktop browser.

docs.title: Output Directory Structure
docs.text:
FASTA indexes (*.fasta.fai) are copied only when produced and are not required outputs. Zero-contig results may contain empty FASTAs and header-only CSV/TSV files with a reduced column set. Contig CSV booleans are true/false; AIRR booleans are T/F. The report filename is <sample>_scVDJ_TR_report.html for TCR or <sample>_scVDJ_IG_report.html for BCR; TR(IG) below is shorthand, not a literal filename.

outs/
├── filtered_contig_annotations.csv         # QC-filtered contig annotations from real cells (preferred downstream input)
├── filtered_contig.fasta                   # QC-filtered contig nucleotide sequences (FASTA format)
├── filtered_contig.fasta.fai               # Index file for filtered contigs (optional)
├── airr_annotations.tsv                    # AIRR Community standard annotation file (TSV format)
├── clonotypes.csv                          # Clonotype statistics and paired CDR3 sequences
├── consensus_annotations.csv               # Detailed annotations for consensus sequences
├── consensus.fasta                         # Consensus contig sequences for each clonotype (FASTA format)
├── consensus.fasta.fai                     # Consensus sequence index file (optional)
├── all_contig_annotations.csv              # Annotation table for all assembled contigs (including background)
├── all_contig.fasta                        # Nucleotide sequences for all contigs (FASTA format)
├── all_contig.fasta.fai                    # Index file for all contigs (optional)
├── metrics_summary.xls                     # Analysis quality and performance metrics summary (tab-delimited TSV)
└── <sample>_scVDJ_TR(IG)_report.html       # Comprehensive interactive web QC and clonotype report

docs.title: V(D)J Assembly and Annotation Files
docs.text: Core Content: Assembled V(D)J contig sequences, precise structural annotations, and quality evaluations covering TCR and BCR rearrangements.

docs.title: V(D)J Transcript Structure and Composition
docs.text:
Diagram of a Typical V(D)J Transcript Structure:

Key Structural Elements:

Region Abbreviation Biological Function Untranslated Region UTR Regulates mRNA stability and translation efficiency; non-protein coding Framework Region FWR (FWR1–4) Conserved structural scaffolds that maintain the 3D folding of immunoglobulins or TCRs Complementarity Determining Region CDR (CDR1–3) Hypervariable loops directly contacting antigen epitopes (CDR3 exhibits the highest diversity)

Technical Note: The pipeline annotates full amino acid and nucleotide sequences for both FWR and CDR regions. Output annotations are exported in multiple standardized formats.

docs.title: Full-Length Contig Criteria
docs.text:
A contig is declared Full Length when it meets both conditions:

  • Fully spans the annotated 5' start of the V gene.
  • Fully extends through the 3' end of the J gene.

docs.title: Productive Contig Criteria
docs.text: Use the productive flag emitted by V(D)J annotation. It is distinct from full_length and is not recomputed from chain count or FASTA length when publishing outputs. Filtered contigs require productive, is_cell, and high_confidence to all be true.

docs.title: High Confidence & Receptor Configuration
docs.text: The assembly and clonotype stages produce high_confidence. A fixed “one chain of each type” rule does not define this output flag. The filtered annotation writer applies productive && is_cell && high_confidence; a cell may still have multiple contig rows. Interpret chain pairing alongside the reported flags and clonotype assignments.

docs.title: airr_annotations.tsv
docs.text:
Rearrangement annotations formatted strictly according to the international AIRR Community standards.

  • Primary Uses: Standardized exchange with immunoinformatics ecosystems such as scRepertoire, immunarch, and Change-O.
  • Key Fields:
Field Name Description cell_id Unique cell identifier associating the contig with single-cell transcriptomic data clone_id Clonotype identifier grouping cells belonging to the same clonal lineage sequence_id Unique contig identifier sequence Full nucleotide sequence of the rearranged V(D)J transcript sequence_aa Translated amino acid sequence representing the functional protein product productive Boolean flag indicating whether the rearrangement is productive (in-frame, no stop codons) rev_comp Reverse-complement flag, serialized as AIRR T/F v_call / d_call / j_call / c_call Identified germline V, D, J, and C gene segment alleles v_cigar / d_cigar / j_cigar / c_cigar CIGAR alignment strings detailing matches, insertions, and deletions sequence_alignment Query nucleotide alignment against reference germline sequences germline_alignment Inferred germline sequence alignment used for somatic hypermutation (SHM) analysis junction / junction_aa Nucleotide and amino acid sequences of the CDR3 junction region junction_length / junction_aa_length CDR3 length in nucleotides and amino acids v_sequence_start / v_sequence_end 1-based start and end coordinates of the V segment d_sequence_start / d_sequence_end 1-based start and end coordinates of the D segment j_sequence_start / j_sequence_end 1-based start and end coordinates of the J segment c_sequence_start / c_sequence_end 1-based start and end coordinates of the C segment consensus_count Total raw reads supporting this assembled contig duplicate_count Number of unique UMI molecules supporting this rearrangement is_cell Flag indicating whether the barcode is assigned to a real cell

docs.title: all_contig_annotations.csv
docs.text:
Comprehensive annotation table for all assembled contigs, spanning real cells and background droplets.

  • Core Purpose: Algorithmic auditing, full provenance inspection, and technical troubleshooting.
  • Key Fields:
Field Name Description sample Sample identifier for the VDJ library barcode Associated cell barcode ID is_cell Boolean flag indicating cell calling status (true / false) contig_id Unique contig identifier high_confidence High-confidence status flag (excluding amplicons with chimeric or artifactual characteristics) length Contig length in nucleotides (bp) chain Receptor chain locus: TRA, TRB, IGK, IGL, or IGH v_gene / d_gene / j_gene / c_gene Top-scoring V, D, J, and C gene calls full_length Boolean flag indicating whether full-length criteria are met productive Boolean flag indicating productive open reading frame status fwr1–fwr4 / fwr1_nt–fwr4_nt Predicted amino acid and nucleotide sequences for FWR1 through FWR4 cdr1–cdr3 / cdr1_nt–cdr3_nt Predicted amino acid and nucleotide sequences for CDR1 through CDR3 reads Number of reads aligned to this contig umis Number of unique UMI molecules supporting this contig raw_clonotype_id Assigned clonotype identifier raw_consensus_id Assigned consensus sequence identifier exact_subclonotype_id Exact subclonotype identifier, when assigned

docs.title: all_contig.fasta
docs.text: FASTA file containing nucleotide sequences for all assembled contigs across cells and background.

docs.title: filtered_contig_annotations.csv
docs.text:
Curated subset of all_contig_annotations.csv containing only high-confidence, productive contigs originating from real cells.

Downstream File Selection & Multi-Modal Integration

  • Preferred Downstream Input: filtered_contig_annotations.csv strictly excludes non-productive, low-support, and ambient contigs, making it the primary entry point for clonotype diversity and V/D/J gene usage profiling.
  • AIRR Standard Compatibility: The companion airr_annotations.tsv adheres to AIRR specifications for seamless loading into R (scRepertoire, immunarch) or Python (scirpy).
  • 5' scRNA Barcode Harmonization: When --beadstrans outs/singlecell.csv is supplied, VDJ barcodes are harmonized to match RNA cell IDs (e.g., CELL1118_N3), use this as the join key for RNA metadata. Contig annotations have one row per contig, so a cell can appear multiple times; aggregate by cell before a one-row-per-cell join.

docs.title: filtered_contig.fasta
docs.text: FASTA file containing high-confidence, real cell contig sequences.

docs.title: Clonotype Analysis Files
docs.text: Core Content: Precise clonal lineage identification, clonal frequency calculation, and CDR3 sequence diversity.

docs.title: clonotypes.csv
docs.text:
Statistical summary table for each unique clonotype identified across the dataset.

  • Key Fields:
Field Name Description clonotype_id Unique clonotype identifier (e.g., clonotype1) frequency Absolute number of cells assigned to this clonotype proportion Fraction of total analyzed cells represented by this clonotype cdr3s_aa Semicolon-delimited chain:sequence list (e.g., TRA:CAVR...;TRB:CASS...) cdr3s_nt Semicolon-delimited chain:sequence list with nucleotide sequences

docs.title: consensus_annotations.csv
docs.text:
Detailed annotation table for the consensus sequence of each clonotype.

  • Key Fields: clonotype_id, consensus_id, sample, length, chain, v_gene, d_gene, j_gene, c_gene, full_length, productive, cdr3, cdr3_nt, reads, umis.

docs.title: consensus.fasta
docs.text: FASTA file containing representative consensus sequences for all clonotypes.

docs.title: Analysis Metrics Summary
docs.text: Core Content: Structured evaluation of sequencing quality, cell recovery, V(D)J mapping, and assembly performance.

docs.title: metrics_summary.xls
docs.text:
A structured table of key quality metrics in tab-delimited text format (TSV).

  • Metric Categories: | Category | Contents | | :--- | :--- | | Basic Sequencing | Total reads, valid barcode fraction, valid UMI fraction, Q30 base quality | | Cell Calling | Estimated number of cells, fraction of reads in cells, mean reads per cell | | Gene Enrichment | Reads mapped to any V(D)J gene, chain-specific mapping rates | | Assembly Quality | Full-length contig fraction, productive contig fraction, CDR3 recovery | | Clonotype Analysis | Paired clonotype diversity, dominant clonotype frequencies |

  • Reading Instructions: Read with read.delim("metrics_summary.xls") in R or pd.read_csv("metrics_summary.xls", sep="\t") in Python. Detailed descriptions and benchmarks are provided in Web Report Interpretation.

docs.title: *_scVDJ_TR(IG)_report.html
docs.text:
Self-contained visual report in HTML format.

  • Core Purpose: Provides interactive charts for barcode ranking, receptor recombination, and clonotype abundance.
  • Convenient Sharing: Single offline file; opens in any desktop browser without an internet connection.

docs.title: Web Report Interpretation
docs.text:
Overview: The HTML report provides visual summaries and quality metrics for single-cell V(D)J sequencing, evaluating library quality, assembly efficiency, and immune repertoire diversity.

Quality Assessment Principles & Guide

  • Holistic Assessment: The HTML report provides an end-to-end overview of scVDJ analysis, covering cell calling, sequencing quality, V(D)J targeted gene mapping, productive chain assembly, and clonal expansion.
  • Baseline Context: Benchmarks reflect typical targeted enrichment protocols. Metrics depend on cell type (e.g., PBMC, tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes, sorted B/T cells), target cell purity, and sequencing depth.
  • Review Workflow: We recommend inspecting base sequencing quality and valid barcode fractions first, followed by V(D)J mapping rate and productive V-J pairing fractions, before analyzing clonotype expansion profiles.

docs.title: V(D)J Analysis Metrics
docs.text:
Core Function: Assesses cell recovery, UMI capture depth, and immune receptor assembly efficiency.

Quality Reference Benchmarks:

Metric Optimal Acceptable Suboptimal Mean reads per cell ≥ 10,000 5,000 – 10,000 < 5,000 Fraction of Reads in Cells ≥ 50% 20% – 50% < 20%

Detailed Metric Definitions & Interpretation:

Metric Calculation & Definition Interpretation & Troubleshooting Estimated number of cells Estimated number of high-confidence cell barcodes expressing target V(D)J transcripts. Evaluate against cell loading and target lymphocyte frequency. Low recovery indicates low cell purity, poor viability, or inefficient targeted PCR. Mean reads per cell Total input reads / Estimated number of cells. Evaluates library sequencing depth. Paired-end sequencing recommends ≥ 5,000–10,000 read pairs/cell to ensure complete full-length assembly. Fraction of Reads in Cells Percentage of valid barcode reads successfully assigned to real cells. Measures targeted signal against ambient mRNA. Recommended ≥ 50%; low values indicate cell damage or elevated cell-free RNA background. Median TRA/TRB or IGH/IGK/IGL UMIs per cell Median number of unique UMI molecules per cell assigned to the specific receptor locus. Reflects per-cell transcript abundance and cDNA capture efficiency. Number of cells with TRA/TRB or IGH/IGK/IGL contig Number of cells with at least one contig assembled for the specified chain. Basic detection threshold without requiring full-length or productive rearrangement. Cells with V-J spanning TRA/TRB or IGH/IGK/IGL contig Number of cells with contigs spanning from the V segment through the J segment. Verifies physical assembly continuity across the recombination junction. Cells with productive TRA/TRB or IGH/IGK/IGL contig Number of cells with an in-frame, full-length, stop-codon-free contig and complete CDR3. Measures functionally competent receptor recovery, providing the basis for clonotype definition. Paired clonotype diversity Inverse Simpson Index calculated from paired clonotype frequencies. A value of 1 indicates total dominance by a single clone; values approaching cell count indicate a diverse polyclonal repertoire.

docs.title: Sequencing Metrics
docs.text:
Core Function: Assesses primary sequencing quality, barcode validity, and UMI integrity.

Quality Reference Benchmarks:

Metric Optimal Acceptable Suboptimal Valid barcodes ≥ 80% 70% – 80% < 70% Valid UMIs ≥ 80% 70% – 80% < 70% Q30 Base Quality ≥ 85% 75% – 85% < 75%

Detailed Metric Definitions & Interpretation:

Metric Calculation & Definition Interpretation & Troubleshooting Valid barcodes Percentage of reads whose cell barcodes match the pre-defined whitelist (with error correction). Recommended ≥ 80%. Low fractions indicate sequencing degradation, adapter contamination, or primer issues. Valid UMIs Percentage of reads whose UMI sequence contains no N bases and is not a homopolymer. Ensures reliable molecular deduplication and accurate transcript quantification. Recommended ≥ 80%. Q30 Base Quality Percentage of bases in barcode, UMI, and RNA reads with quality score ≥ 30 (error rate < 0.1%). Primary sequencing fidelity metric ensuring robust contig assembly and accurate somatic hypermutation calling.

docs.title: Gene Enrichment Metrics
docs.text:
Core Function: Evaluates targeted V(D)J amplification specificity and capture efficiency.

Quality Reference Benchmarks:

Metric Optimal Acceptable Suboptimal Reads mapped to any V(D)J gene ≥ 50% 30% – 50% < 30%

Detailed Metric Definitions & Interpretation:

Metric Calculation & Definition Interpretation & Troubleshooting Reads mapped to any V(D)J gene Percentage of valid barcode reads aligning partially or fully to known germline V(D)J gene segments. Recommended ≥ 50%. Values < 30% suggest low lymphocyte purity, non-specific PCR amplification, or reference segment mismatches. Reads mapped to TRA/TRB/IGH/IGK/IGL Fraction of reads aligning to specific receptor chains (TRA, TRB, IGH, IGK, IGL). Confirms whether individual chain abundances align with biological expectations (e.g., balanced heavy/light chain capture).

docs.title: V(D)J Annotation Analysis
docs.text:
Core Function: Assesses productive receptor pairing and functional chain recovery.

Quality Reference Benchmarks:

Metric Optimal Acceptable Suboptimal Cells with productive V-J spanning pair ≥ 40% 20% – 40% < 20%

Detailed Metric Definitions & Interpretation:

Metric Calculation & Definition Interpretation & Troubleshooting Number of Cells with Productive V-J Spanning Pair Total cells harboring at least one productive receptor pair (TRA/TRB or IGH/light chain). Yield of cells eligible for functional paired TCR/BCR repertoire investigations. Cells with productive V-J spanning pair Percentage of estimated cells harboring a full productive receptor pair. Recommended ≥ 40%. Values < 20% suggest PCR amplification bias, unbalanced chain capture, or low viability. Cells with productive V-J spanning (IGK, IGH) pair Percentage of cells with functional IGK/IGH immunoglobulin pairing. BCR-specific metric measuring pairing efficiency for κ light chain B cells. Cells with productive V-J spanning (IGL, IGH) pair Percentage of cells with functional IGL/IGH immunoglobulin pairing. BCR-specific metric measuring pairing efficiency for λ light chain B cells. Cells with productive V-J spanning (TRA, TRB) pair Percentage of cells with functional TRA/TRB T cell receptor pairing. TCR-specific metric; high percentages confirm successful α/β heterodimer recovery.

docs.title: Interactive Visualization Charts
docs.text: The HTML report includes interactive visualizations for UMI barcode ranking and clonotype abundance analysis.

docs.title: 1. V(D)J Barcode Rank Plot
docs.text:
Chart Function: Displays cumulative productive UMI counts across cell barcodes ranked in descending order to assess target enrichment and separation from background noise.

How to Interpret:

  • Axes:
    • X-axis (Barcode Rank): Cell barcodes ranked by productive contig UMI count in descending order (log scale).
    • Y-axis (UMI Counts): Total UMI count per barcode (log scale).
  • Visual Elements:
    • Blue curve: Identified real cells.
    • Gray curve: Background ambient molecules and empty droplets.
    • Blue gradient zone: Transition boundary separating cells from background.
  • Quality Guidance: High-quality libraries display a sharp drop-off between real cells and noise. In BCR datasets, distinct peaks with exceptionally high UMI counts typically correspond to antibody-secreting plasma cells.

docs.title: 2. Clonotype Abundance & Diversity
docs.text:
Chart Function: Illustrates the relative frequency distribution and sequence features of dominant clonotypes to evaluate clonal expansion.

How to Interpret:

  • Top Bar Chart (Top 10 Clonotypes): Displays the percentage of analyzed cells represented by the 10 most frequent clonotypes. High concentration indicates significant clonal expansion (e.g., in immune responses or tumor infiltrates).
  • Bottom Table (Detailed Clonotype Table): Lists key molecular features for the top 10 clonotypes, including Clonotype ID, CDR3 amino acid and nucleotide sequences per chain, cell count (Frequency), and relative percentage (Proportion).

docs.title: C6 Multiplexed Analysis Parameters
docs.text:
C6 multiplexed single-cell RNA analysis is executed via the dnbc4tools multi run command using a sectioned CSV configuration file that maps shared pooled libraries to Sample Barcodes.

See the Chinese–English Glossary for terminology.

docs.title: Execution Command
docs.text:
dnbc4tools multi run \
  --name c6_demo \
  --csv sample.config.csv \
  --outdir ./results \
  --threads 40

docs.title: Basic Options
docs.text: Option Required Description --name Yes Unique identifier for the run. Results are written to <outdir>/<name>/ --csv Yes Path to the sectioned CSV configuration file --outdir No Path to the output directory; defaults to the current directory --threads No Number of CPU threads to use [default: all available cores]

docs.title: CSV File Structure
docs.text: A standard C6 configuration file contains three essential sections: [rna] (global RNA and experiment-level settings), [libraries] (paths to input sequencing data), and [samples] (mapping of sample names to Sample Barcodes).

docs.title: Minimal Configuration Example
docs.text:
[rna]
genomeDir,/database/scRNA/Human
chemistry,scRNAC6
darkreaction,auto

[libraries]
fastqs,feature_types
/rawdata/c6_pooled_run,rna

[samples]
sample_id,probe_barcode_ids
S1,BC01
S2,BC02;BC03

Optional BAM output setting: This example uses the default [rna] no_bam,false, generating per-sample BAMs, unassigned BAM, and oligo BAM with their applicable indexes. To save disk space, add no_bam,true to [rna]; BAM files and their indexes will then be omitted.

docs.title: [libraries] Specification
docs.text:
The [libraries] section declares the directories containing input sequencing data and their corresponding modality types.

Column Required Rules & Description fastqs Yes Path to the directory containing paired FASTQ files. For C6 RNA libraries, this directory must contain cDNA/ and oligo/ subdirectories housing the respective FASTQ files. feature_types Yes Modality type; fixed to rna for C6 RNA.

Tip: Sequencing Consistency & Batch Handling All FASTQ inputs in a single run must originate from the same library batch with identical sequencing modes and dark reaction settings; data from different libraries cannot be mixed. If different sequencing batches of the same library batch exhibit differing dark reaction cycles or read lengths, use the FASTQ trimming tool fqsubC4 to trim reads to match the standard library structure (see Library Structure).

docs.title: [samples] Specification
docs.text:
The [samples] section declares the unique identity of each biological sample and its assigned Sample Barcodes.

Column Required Rules & Description sample_id Yes Unique identifier for the sample. Must begin with an alphanumeric character and contain only letters, numbers, ., _, and -. Reserved words such as unassigned or non_multiplexed are prohibited. probe_barcode_ids Yes Assigned Sample Barcode identifier (e.g., built-in BC01) or custom barcode DNA sequence. If a sample uses multiple barcodes, delimit them with semicolons ; or pipes \| (e.g., BC02;BC03). The same barcode must not be assigned to multiple samples. expectcells No Per-sample expected cell count override (positive integer). If omitted, falls back to the [rna] default. Does not accept auto. forcecells No Per-sample forced cell count override (positive integer). Takes precedence over expectcells. minumi No Per-sample minimum UMI threshold override. Droplets below this count are excluded from called cells.

docs.title: Configuration with Per-Sample Parameter Overrides:
docs.text:
[samples]
sample_id,probe_barcode_ids,expectcells,forcecells,minumi
Sample_A,BC01,3000,,800
Sample_B,BC02;BC03,5000,,1000

docs.title: [rna] Experiment-Level Settings
docs.text: Parameter Default Description genomeDir Required Path to the STAR reference genome index directory chemistry scRNAC6 C6 chemistry name, fixed to scRNAC6 (omitted or set to auto normalizes to this name) darkreaction auto Dark cycle detection. auto automatically identifies dark reaction cycles across cDNA and Oligo reads high_occupancy_filter true When true, applies cross-sample high-occupancy droplet filtering across the pooled experiment to remove multiplet artifacts sample_failure_policy skip Sub-sample failure policy: skip logs errors and continues processing remaining samples; fail terminates the run upon any sample failure no_bam false When true, skips all BAM generation (sample BAMs, unassigned BAM, and oligo BAM) to conserve disk space and execution time

docs.title: Multi-Omics Analysis Parameters
docs.text:
dnbc4tools multi run executes unified multi-omics analysis (RNA, ATAC, and V(D)J) from a sectioned CSV configuration file.

Note For high-throughput single-cell RNA analysis based on Sample Barcode multiplexing, please refer to the dedicated C6 Parameters Guide.

docs.title: Run command
docs.text:
dnbc4tools multi run \
  --name demo \
  --csv multi.config.csv \
  --outdir ./results \
  --threads 20
Option Required Meaning --name Yes Run name; results are written to <outdir>/<name>/ --csv Yes Sectioned CSV configuration --outdir No Analysis root, default current directory --threads No Number of CPU threads to use [default: all available cores]

docs.title: Complete CLI Help
docs.text:
$ dnbc4tools multi run --help
dnbc4tools 3.2

Process an integrated multi-omics sample.
Coordinate RNA, ATAC, and V(D)J workflows within a single run.
Support C6 probe-barcoded RNA sample demultiplexing via [samples].
Generate a unified multi-omics report.

Usage: dnbc4tools multi run [OPTIONS]

options:
  --help           show this help message and exit

Basic Settings:
  --name <STR>     Unique identifier for the sample.
  --csv <FILE>     CSV file containing pipeline configuration settings. Add [samples] for C6 RNA sample
                   demultiplexing; RNA chemistry is fixed to scRNAC6 in this mode.
  --outdir <DIR>   Output directory path for analysis results.
  --threads <INT>  Number of CPU threads to use [default: all available cores].

rna multi and atac multi only generate per-sample scripts. multi run executes analysis.

docs.title: CSV configuration rules
docs.text:
Modality sections use key,value rows. [libraries] is a table with headers.

Section Purpose [rna] RNA reference, chemistry and cell calling [atac] ATAC reference, peak calling and filters [vdj-t] / [vdj-b] TCR / BCR reference and assembly [libraries] Required mapping of FASTQ directories to modalities

Use true/false for booleans. Quote comma-containing values, for example darkreaction,"R1,R1R2". Global [rna] expectcells and [atac] jaccard_cutoff accept auto. Absolute input paths are recommended.

RNA input roots contain cDNA/ and oligo/; ATAC and VDJ directories contain their paired FASTQs directly. See FASTQ naming rules.

Tip: Sequencing Consistency & Batch Handling Multi accepts separate RNA, ATAC, TCR, and BCR libraries in the same run. Within each modality entry, pooled FASTQs must belong to the corresponding library with compatible read structures and dark-cycle settings. Do not pool unrelated libraries into the same modality input; configure each modality independently. If different sequencing batches of the same library batch exhibit differing dark reaction cycles or read lengths, use the FASTQ trimming tool fqsubC4 to trim reads to match the standard library structure (see Library Structure).

docs.title: Ordinary multi-omics configuration
docs.text:
This minimal 5′ RNA + TCR configuration can be saved as multi.config.csv and run with the command above.

[rna]
genomeDir,/database/scRNA/Human
end5,true
no_bam,true

[vdj-t]
ref,human

[libraries]
fastqs,feature_types
/rawdata/rna,rna
/rawdata/tcr,vdj-t

For BCR, replace [vdj-t] / vdj-t with [vdj-b] / vdj-b. Add an [atac] section and library row for ATAC. Remove the VDJ section and input row for RNA alone.

VDJ uses RNA cell information by default; set beadstrans for another cell table. Ordinary RNA + VDJ requires end5,true.

Note: C6 Multiplexed Configuration

The configuration rules and [samples] syntax for C6 multiplexed RNA experiments have been moved to their own dedicated chapter. Please refer to C6 Parameters.

docs.title: Modality parameter mapping
docs.text:
Section Common settings Full reference [rna] genomeDir, chemistry, darkreaction, expectcells, forcecells, minumi, consistent_cells, calling_method, no_introns, end5, no_bam, star_parameters, sample_read_pairs RNA [atac] genomeDir, darkreaction, forcecells, frags_cutoff, tss_cutoff, jaccard_cutoff, merge_cutoff, need_bam, sample_read_pairs ATAC [vdj-t] / [vdj-b] ref, beadstrans, darkreaction, customize, keep_all_cells, r2_only, enrichment_primers, sample_read_pairs VDJ

Ordinary RNA requires explicit chemistry and dark cycles together. Repeat customize as required for libraries; keep one definition for other scalar options.

docs.title: Parameter Overview
docs.text:
Find commands, configuration specifications, and default parameter settings by module. Each module documentation page provides complete parameter quick references, detailed options, and full CLI help.

Module Primary Commands Use Case Parameter Reference scRNA rna run, rna mkref, rna multi Single-cell RNA (3' / 5') profiling, reference building, and batch script generation RNA Parameters scATAC atac run, atac mkref, atac multi Chromatin accessibility analysis, Chromap index & reference building, batch processing ATAC Parameters scVDJ vdj run Full-length TCR/BCR immune repertoire assembly and clonotype profiling VDJ Parameters Multi-omics multi run (with sectioned CSV) Simultaneous multi-modal analysis (RNA + ATAC + VDJ) with unified orchestration and combined reporting Multi Parameters C6 Multiplexed multi run (with [samples]) Sample Barcode demultiplexing, per-sample cell calling, and independent matrix generation C6 Parameters GTF Tools tools mkgtf GTF annotation filtering, gene type filtering, and format validation Tools

docs.title: Entry Point Recommendations
docs.text:
• Individual Sample Analysis: For an independent library, run the corresponding module command directly (e.g., rna run, atac run, vdj run).
  • Batch Script Generation: rna multi and atac multi generate independent shell scripts for each sample based on a tab-separated list; verify scripts before launching.
  • Multi-Omics and Multiplexing: Use multi run exclusively. Configure via a CSV file: declare [rna], [atac], [vdj-*] sections for multi-modal assays, and add [samples] for C6 probe demultiplexing.

docs.title: Key Configuration Principles
docs.text:
• Default Values: Omitted options adopt recommended pipeline defaults. Note that not all options accept the explicit literal string auto.
  • Parameter Types: CLI boolean switches are flags that take no values (e.g., --no_bam, --end5), whereas in Multi CSV files, boolean values must be explicitly written as true or false.
  • Precedence & Overrides: In multi-sample and multi-omics runs, when sample-level overrides conflict with global settings, the inheritance rules defined in each module's parameter documentation apply.

docs.title: scATAC Parameters
docs.text: DNBelab C Series HT scATAC Parameter Configuration Guide

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
This document describes the parameters, default behaviors, and usage patterns for dnbc4tools atac subcommands, including single-sample analysis (run), reference database construction (mkref), and batch script generation (multi).

Tip: Parameter specifications are based on current command-line help outputs. Examples can be used directly as templates.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
dnbc4tools atac run \
  --name sample1 \
  --fastqs /data/atac \
  --genomeDir /reference/atac \
  --threads 20

docs.title: Full Command-Line Help
docs.text:
$ dnbc4tools atac run --help
dnbc4tools 3.2

Process a single-cell ATAC-seq sample.

Usage: dnbc4tools atac run [OPTIONS]

options:
  --help                     show this help message and exit

Input Files:
  Choose one input method: either `--fastqs` (directory input) or individual FASTQ files (`--fastq1` and
  `--fastq2`).

  --fastqs <DIR>             Input directory path containing paired-end FASTQ files. Read 1 and Read 2 files are
  detected from the directory (e.g., `./fastq_dir`).
  --fastq1 <FILE>            Read 1 FASTQ file path(s) for the ATAC library. Wildcards and comma-separated lists are
  supported (e.g., `sample1_L01_R1.fastq.gz,sample1_L02_R1.fastq.gz`).
  --fastq2 <FILE>            Read 2 FASTQ file path(s) for the ATAC library. Must match the order provided to
  `--fastq1` (e.g., `sample1_L01_R2.fastq.gz,sample1_L02_R2.fastq.gz`).

Basic Settings:
  --name <STR>               Unique identifier for the sample. Used for naming output files and reports (e.g.,
  `sample1`).
  --genomeDir <DIR>          Reference genome directory path. Must contain required index and annotation resources
  (e.g., `./genome_index`).
  --outdir <DIR>             Output directory path for results and reports [default: current directory] (e.g.,
  `./output`).
  --threads <INT>            Number of CPU threads for parallel processing [default: all available cores].

Library Settings:
  --darkreaction <STR>       Dark cycle setting for ATAC library. Supported values: `R1R2`, `R1`, `R2`, `unset` (e.g.,
  `R1R2`).
  --customize <STR>          Custom read structure string. Format: `<type>,<read>:<start>-<end>` joined by `;`. (e.g.,
  `"cb,R1:7-16;cb,R1:23-32;R1,R1:66-115;R2,R2:20-69"`).

Filtering Settings:
  --forcecells <INT>         Force pipeline to use exactly this number of cells (e.g., `5000`).
  --frags_cutoff <INT>       Additional minimum total unique fragments for called cells [default: 0, disabled]. Cell
  calling and other configured QC filters still apply.
  --tss_cutoff <FLOAT>       Minimum TSS proportion threshold to retain a cell [default: 0.0] (e.g., `0.2`).
  --jaccard_cutoff <FLOAT>   Jaccard similarity threshold in [0,1] for bead merging (e.g., `0.02`).
  --merge_cutoff <INT>       Minimum unique fragments per bead for initial bead-merge candidates [default: 500].
  Lowering it admits weaker evidence and can change merging and the filtered peak-calling
  input.

Analysis Settings:
  --need_bam                 Enable generation of BAM files containing aligned reads.
  --sample_read_pairs <INT>  Subsample the specified number of read pairs from input FASTQ file(s) (e.g., `1000000`).

docs.title: Required & Basic Settings
docs.text: Option Type Default Description --name String Required Unique sample identifier; used as output file prefix and report title (e.g., sample_001) --genomeDir Directory Required Reference genome directory path containing index and annotation resources built by atac mkref --outdir Directory ./ Root output directory for analysis results and HTML reports --threads Integer All cores Number of CPU threads allocated for parallel processing

docs.title: Input Files Options
docs.text:
Choose one input mode: directory-based (--fastqs) or explicit files (--fastq1 and --fastq2).

Option Type Default Description --fastqs Directory None Directory containing paired-end FASTQ files (files reside directly in this directory; paired files detected automatically) --fastq1 File path None Read 1 FASTQ file list (supports wildcards * or comma-separated paths) --fastq2 File path None Read 2 FASTQ file list (order must strictly match --fastq1)

Tip: Sequencing Consistency & Batch Handling All FASTQ inputs in a single run must originate from the same library batch with identical sequencing modes and dark reaction settings; data from different libraries cannot be mixed. If different sequencing batches of the same library batch exhibit differing dark reaction cycles or read lengths, use the FASTQ trimming tool fqsubC4 to trim reads to match the standard library structure (see Library Structure).

docs.title: Cell Calling & Bead Merging Settings
docs.text: Option Type Default Description --forcecells Integer None Forces the pipeline to retain exactly this number of cells (highest priority, overrides automatic calling). Barcodes are ranked in descending order of unique fragments, and the top N barcodes are selected --frags_cutoff Integer 0 (disabled) Additional minimum total unique fragments for called cells; 0 disables this extra filter while still running cell calling --tss_cutoff Float 0.0 (disabled) Minimum TSS proportion threshold to retain a cell; 0 disables this filter (e.g., 0.2) --jaccard_cutoff Float | auto auto Jaccard similarity threshold for bead merging (auto estimated via OTSU algorithm, clamped at 0.02 if estimated below 0.02; or manual 0–1 float value) --merge_cutoff Integer 500 Minimum unique fragments per bead for initial bead-merge candidates

docs.title: Library Chemistry & Read Structure
docs.text: Option Type Default Description --darkreaction Choice auto Dark cycle settings: auto, R1R2, R1, R2, unset --customize String None Custom read structure string overriding darkreaction (wrapped in quotes, delimited by semicolons)

docs.title: Analysis Settings & Tuning
docs.text: Option Type Default Description --need_bam Flag Disabled Enables generation of aligned BAM files (increases runtime and disk usage by 30%–50%). Note: Due to slight discrepancies in how Chromap produces BED versus BAM outputs, enabling --need_bam may introduce minor differences in downstream analysis results --sample_read_pairs Integer None Subsample a specified number of read pairs for rapid benchmarking

docs.title: 1. FASTQ Directory Structure & Input Rules
docs.text:
Unlike the RNA workflow (which requires cDNA/ and oligo/ subfolders), the ATAC --fastqs option points to a flat directory containing paired-end files directly:

fastq_directory/
├── sample_ATAC_L01_R1.fastq.gz
├── sample_ATAC_L01_R2.fastq.gz
├── sample_ATAC_L02_R1.fastq.gz
└── sample_ATAC_L02_R2.fastq.gz
  • Naming detection: Supports standard read patterns _R1_, _R1, _1, _read1 paired with _R2_, _R2, _2, _read2; file extensions support .fastq.gz, .fq.gz, .fastq, .fq.
  • Individual inputs: If not using --fastqs, supply paired files via --fastq1 and --fastq2 with comma-separated file lists.

docs.title: 2. Bead Merging & Multi-stage Quality Control
docs.text:
Single-cell ATAC-seq exhibits droplet bead co-encapsulation. The pipeline applies a two-stage merging and filtering strategy:

  • --merge_cutoff: Minimum unique fragments per bead required to participate in Jaccard similarity calculation (default: 500). This parameter only controls bead merging; beads with fewer than 500 fragments or beads without overlapping partners are retained intact as singleton cells and advance to downstream steps without being discarded. In low-depth libraries, this can be lowered (e.g. 200) to allow more beads to be evaluated for merging.
  • --jaccard_cutoff: Jaccard similarity cutoff measuring genomic accessibility overlap between beads. Defaults to auto (OTSU bimodal distribution estimation with a safety floor of 0.02 to prevent over-merging), or a float between 0–1. Beads with $\ge 500$ fragments that do not meet this cutoff are likewise preserved as singletons.
  • --forcecells: Forces retention of a specified number of authentic cells when automatic calling does not meet expectations.
