Cell calling evaluates the complete candidate pool (both merged multi-bead cells and all singleton beads), sorts candidates by unique fragments in descending order, and directly selects the top N cells.
  • --frags_cutoff & --tss_cutoff: Downstream supplementary QC filters. Setting them to 0 leaves filtering to the cell calling algorithm. If damaged nuclei debris remains in the report, activate manual cutoffs (e.g., --frags_cutoff 1000 --tss_cutoff 0.1).
  • --need_bam & Alignment Differences Note: Chromap's direct BED export differs slightly from its SAM/BAM generation and subsequent fragment extraction pipeline in terms of fragment shifting (Tn5 shift) and deduplication boundaries. Consequently, enabling --need_bam may produce minor variations in downstream metrics (such as fragment counts and cell statistics), which is expected behavior.

docs.title: 3. Dark Reaction & Custom Read Structure
docs.text:
Library Structure Reference: For complete ATAC library adapter architecture, extension sequences, and dark reaction schematics, see Library Structure.

  • --darkreaction: Select based on MGI sequencer chemistry:
  • auto: Automatically detected from base compositions
  • R1R2: Dark cycles on both Read 1 and Read 2
  • R1: Dark cycles only on Read 1
  • R2: Dark cycles only on Read 2
  • unset: No dark reactions (standard sequencing mode)
  • --customize: Defines exact 1-based intervals for barcodes and reads (overrides darkreaction): 
    # Structure: CB1(7-16bp), CB2(23-32bp), R1(66-115bp), R2(20-69bp)
--customize "cb,R1:7-16;cb,R1:23-32;R1,R1:66-115;R2,R2:20-69"

docs.title: Reference Database Construction (mkref)
docs.text: dnbc4tools atac mkref builds Chromap genome indices, chromosome tables, and TSS annotation BED files.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
dnbc4tools atac mkref \
  --fasta genome.fa --ingtf genes.gtf \
  --species human --genomeDir /reference/atac

docs.title: Full Command-Line Help
docs.text:
$ dnbc4tools atac mkref --help
dnbc4tools 3.2

Build an ATAC reference database.

Usage: dnbc4tools atac mkref [OPTIONS]

options:
  --help               show this help message and exit

Input Files:
  Input genome FASTA files and gene-annotation GTF files. For mixed-species analysis, separate multiple files with
  commas.

  --fasta <FILE>       Reference-genome FASTA file path(s). Separate multiple files with commas (e.g., `genome.fa`).
  --ingtf <FILE>       Gene-annotation GTF file path(s). Separate multiple files with commas (e.g., `anno.gtf`).

Basic Settings:
  --genomeDir <DIR>    Output directory path for generated reference files [default: current directory] (e.g.,
                       `./ref`).

Advanced Settings:
  --tag <STR>          Feature type used to generate the BED file [default: transcript] (e.g., `exon`).
  --chrM <STR>         Mitochondrial chromosome name [default: auto-detect common names]. For mixed-species

docs.title: 1. TSS Extraction & Mixed-Species Reference
docs.text:
• TSS BED Generation: The tool automatically extracts Transcription Start Sites (TSS) from GTF based on --tag, used for single-cell ATAC TSS enrichment and proportion calculations.
  • Mixed-Species Reference:
  • Provide matching comma-separated arguments: 
    dnbc4tools atac mkref \
  --fasta human.fa,mouse.fa \
  --ingtf human.gtf,mouse.gtf \
  --species human,mouse \
  --genomeDir /ref/human_and_mouse

docs.title: 2. Directory Layout & ref.json Metadata
docs.text:
genomeDir/
├── fasta/
│   ├── genome.fa          # Unified FASTA sequence
│   ├── genome.chrom.sizes # Chromosome lengths
│   └── genome.index       # Chromap index
├── genes/
│   ├── genes.gtf          # Standardized GTF annotation

Dual-Species ref.json Example:

  "chrmt": "human_chrM,mouse_chrM",
  "chloroplast": null,
  "genome": "/database/scATAC/human_and_mouse/fasta/genome.fa",
  "genomeDir": "/database/scATAC/human_and_mouse",

}

docs.title: Multi-Sample Workflow (multi)
docs.text: dnbc4tools atac multi generates standalone executable shell scripts for each sample defined in a tab-separated list file. It does not launch analyses automatically.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: dnbc4tools atac multi --list samples.tsv --genomeDir /reference/atac --threads 20

docs.title: Full Command-Line Help
docs.text:
$ dnbc4tools atac multi --help
dnbc4tools 3.2

Process multiple ATAC-seq samples.

Usage: dnbc4tools atac multi [OPTIONS]

options:
  --help             show this help message and exit

Input Files:
  --list <FILE>      Tab-separated sample list: sample name <TAB> FASTQ R1;R2. Multiple FASTQ files within one
                     end are comma-separated. Generates one shell script per sample in the current working directory;
                     run the generated scripts to start analysis.

Basic Settings:
  --genomeDir <DIR>  Reference genome directory path containing required reference files.
  --outdir <DIR>     Analysis output directory written into each generated script [default: current directory] (e.g.,
                     `./output`). Scripts are written to the current working directory.
  --threads <INT>    Number of CPU threads written into each generated analysis script. If omitted, each analysis
                     detects available cores when it runs.

docs.title: Parameter Reference Tables
docs.text: Option Type Default Description --list File path Required Tab-separated sample list file --genomeDir Directory Required Reference genome directory path --outdir Directory ./ Output root directory written into each script (scripts are generated in current working directory) --threads Integer Auto-detect Thread count configured inside each generated script

docs.title: 1. --list File Specification
docs.text:
The sample list must be a tab-separated (\t) text file with 2 columns: 1. Sample Name (sample_name) 2. ATAC FASTQ Paths (paired R1 and R2 separated by semicolon ;, multiple lane files comma-separated ,)

Sample1 /data/S1_L01_R1.fq.gz,/data/S1_L02_R1.fq.gz;/data/S1_L01_R2.fq.gz,/data/S1_L02_R2.fq.gz
Sample2 /data/S2_L01_R1.fq.gz;/data/S2_L01_R2.fq.gz

docs.title: 2. Execution & Cluster Dispatch
docs.text:
• Running dnbc4tools atac multi creates per-sample shell scripts (e.g., Sample1.sh, Sample2.sh) in the current directory.
  • Each script contains the complete parameterized dnbc4tools atac run command.
  • Users can run scripts directly via bash Sample1.sh or submit them to batch workload managers (e.g., Slurm, SGE).

docs.title: scRNA Parameters
docs.text: DNBelab C Series HT scRNA Parameter Configuration Guide

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
This document explains the parameter definitions, default behaviors, and standard usage patterns for dnbc4tools rna subcommands, including single-sample analysis (run), reference database construction (mkref), and multi-sample script generation (multi).

Tip Parameter specifications are based on the latest command-line help messages. Examples can be used directly as operational templates.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
dnbc4tools rna run \
  --name sample1 \
  --fastqs /data/rna \
  --genomeDir /reference/rna \
  --threads 20

docs.title: Full Command-Line Help
docs.text:
$ dnbc4tools rna run --help
dnbc4tools 3.2

Process a single-cell RNA-seq sample.

Usage: dnbc4tools rna run [OPTIONS]

options:
  --help                     show this help message and exit

Input Files:
  Choose one input method: either `--fastqs` (directory input) or all four individual FASTQ files.

  --fastqs <DIR>             Directory containing cDNA and oligo FASTQ subfolders (e.g.,
                             `cDNA/sample_cdna_R1.fastq.gz`, `oligo/sample_oligo_R1.fastq.gz`). Paired-end files are
                             detected from the directory structure.
  --cDNAfastq1 <FILE>        cDNA Read1 FASTQ list. Supports wildcard and comma-separated inputs (e.g.,
                             `sample1_R1.fastq.gz,sample2_R1.fastq.gz`).
  --cDNAfastq2 <FILE>        cDNA Read2 FASTQ list. Order must match `--cDNAfastq1` (e.g.,
                             `sample1_R2.fastq.gz,sample2_R2.fastq.gz`).
  --oligofastq1 <FILE>       Oligo Read1 FASTQ list for barcode merging. Supports wildcard and comma-separated inputs.
  --oligofastq2 <FILE>       Oligo Read2 FASTQ list. Order must match `--oligofastq1` (e.g.,
                             `sample1_oligo_R2.fastq.gz`).

Basic Settings:
  --name <STR>               Unique identifier for the sample. Used for naming output files and reports (e.g.,
                             `sample1`).
  --genomeDir <DIR>          Reference genome directory path containing STAR index files (e.g., `./genome_index`).
  --outdir <DIR>             Output directory path for results and reports [default: current directory] (e.g.,
                             `./output`).
  --threads <INT>            Number of CPU threads for parallel processing [default: all available cores] (e.g.,
                             `16`).

Filtering Settings:
  --calling_method <STR>     Cell detection method [default: emptydrops]. Supported values: `barcoderanks`,
                             `emptydrops`.
  --expectcells <INT>        Expected number of cells to guide detection (e.g., `3000`).
  --forcecells <INT>         Force pipeline to use exactly this number of cells, overriding expected cell detection
                             (e.g., `5000`).
  --minumi <INT>             Minimum UMI count per cell to retain [default: 1000].
  --consistent_cells <FILE>  Headered CSV or CSV.gz for merge/cell-calling constraints. Supported schemas: `cell`;
                             `cell,barcode`; `cell,is_cell_barcode`; `cell,barcode,is_cell_barcode`. Other columns are
                             ignored.

Library Settings:
  --chemistry <STR>          Library chemistry version. Auto-detected when omitted [default: auto]. Options:
                             `scRNAv1HT`, `scRNAv2HT`, `scRNAv3HT`, `scRNA5Pv1`.
  --darkreaction <STR>       Dark cycle setting for cDNA and oligo libraries. Auto-detected when omitted [default:
                             auto]. Provide two comma-separated values in the form `<cDNA>,<oligo>`.
                             cDNA=`R1`/`unset`; oligo=`R1R2`/`R1`/`unset`.
  --customize <STR>          Custom read structure string. Format: `<type>,<read>:<start>-<end>` joined by `;`. cDNA
                             (e.g., `"cb,R1:7-16;cb,R1:23-32;umi,R1:38-47;R1,R2:1-100"`). Oligo (e.g.,
                             `"cb,R1:7-16;cb,R1:23-32;R1,R2:1-10;R1,R2:17-26;R1,R2:33-42"`). For RNA, provide
                             `--customize` twice when both cDNA and oligo are customized: first cDNA, then oligo.

Analysis Settings:
  --no_introns               Exclude intronic reads from the expression matrix to increase specificity.
  --end5                     Enable 5'-end scRNA-seq analysis for 5' gene-expression profiling.
  --no_bam                   Skip BAM file generation to save time and disk space.
  --sample_read_pairs <INT>  Subsample this number of cDNA read pairs for analysis (e.g., `1000000`).
  --star_parameters <STR>    Extra STAR filtering, alignment, seeding or scoring arguments. Wrap them in quotes (e.g.,
                             `"--outFilterMismatchNmax 10 --outFilterMultimapNmax 1"`). Unknown or ineffective options
                             are rejected.

docs.text: Option Type Default Description --name String Required Unique sample identifier; used as output file prefix and report title (e.g., sample_001) --genomeDir Directory Required Reference directory containing STAR index and annotations built via rna mkref, compatible with v2 references and Cell Ranger RNA reference databases --outdir Directory ./ Root output directory for analysis results and HTML reports --threads Integer All cores Number of CPU threads allocated for parallel processing

docs.title: Input Files Options
docs.text:
Choose one input mode: directory-based (--fastqs) or explicit files (--cDNAfastq1/2 and --oligofastq1/2).

Option Type Default Description --fastqs Directory None FASTQ directory containing cDNA/ and oligo/ subdirectories (auto-detects paired files) --cDNAfastq1 File path None cDNA Read 1 file list (supports comma-separated paths or wildcards *) --cDNAfastq2 File path None cDNA Read 2 file list (order must strictly match --cDNAfastq1) --oligofastq1 File path None Oligo Read 1 file list (supports comma-separated paths or wildcards *) --oligofastq2 File path None Oligo Read 2 file list (order must strictly match --oligofastq1)

Tip: Sequencing Consistency & Batch Handling All FASTQ inputs in a single run must originate from the same library batch with identical sequencing modes and dark reaction settings; data from different libraries cannot be mixed. If different sequencing batches of the same library batch exhibit differing dark reaction cycles or read lengths, use the FASTQ trimming tool fqsubC4 to trim reads to match the standard library structure (see Library Structure).

docs.title: Cell Calling & QC Settings
docs.text: Option Type Default Description --calling_method emptydrops | barcoderanks emptydrops Cell detection algorithm (emptydrops: expression test; barcoderanks: UMI inflection) --expectcells Integer | auto auto Expected number of recovered cells to guide algorithm thresholding --forcecells Integer None Forces the pipeline to retain exactly this number of cells (highest priority, overrides auto-calling). Truncates the top N candidate cells sorted in descending order of total valid UMI counts --minumi Integer 1000 Minimum UMI cutoff for evaluating candidate cells in EmptyDrops (only applies when --calling_method emptydrops). Droplets below this threshold do not enter the secondary ambient RNA profile likelihood test and cell rescue, and are treated directly as background. For low-coverage libraries or smaller cells with lower RNA content, lower this value (e.g., 500) to rescue low-UMI cells --consistent_cells CSV file None External cell whitelist or barcode merging constraint table (supports .csv / .csv.gz)

docs.title: Library Chemistry & Read Structure
docs.text: Option Type Default Description --chemistry Choice auto scRNA kit chemistry: scRNAv1HT, scRNAv2HT, scRNAv3HT, scRNA5Pv1 --darkreaction Choice / String auto Dark cycle settings formatted as <cDNA>,<oligo> (e.g., R1,R1R2, unset,unset) --customize String None Custom barcode/read structure definition; specify twice (first cDNA, then oligo)

docs.title: Analysis Settings & Tuning
docs.text: Option Type Default Description --no_introns Flag Disabled Exclude intronic reads and quantify expression strictly using exonic alignments --end5 Flag Disabled Enable 5'-end scRNA-seq mode (for 5' transcript capture kits) --no_bam Flag Disabled Skip BAM file generation to save disk space and runtime --sample_read_pairs Integer None Subsample a specified number of cDNA read pairs for rapid benchmarking --star_parameters String None Additional arguments passed to STAR aligner (must be wrapped in quotes)

docs.title: 1. FASTQ Directory Structure & Input Rules
docs.text:
When using --fastqs, the pipeline resolves paired-end files based on subdirectory naming:

fastq_directory/
├── cDNA/
│   ├── sample_cDNA_L01_R1.fastq.gz
│   └── sample_cDNA_L01_R2.fastq.gz
└── oligo/
    ├── sample_oligo_L01_R1.fastq.gz
    └── sample_oligo_L01_R2.fastq.gz
  • Naming detection: Supports standard read patterns _R1_, _R1, _1, _read1 paired with _R2_, _R2, _2, _read2; file extensions support .fastq.gz, .fq.gz, .fastq, .fq.
  • Individual inputs: If not using --fastqs, all four options --cDNAfastq1, --cDNAfastq2, --oligofastq1, and --oligofastq2 must be supplied. Multiple lanes are comma-separated and R1/R2 pairs must align sequentially.

docs.title: 2. Cell Calling Algorithms & Diagnosis Strategies
docs.text:
The pipeline offers two complementary cell identification methods:

Method Principle Strengths & Best Use Cases emptydrops (Default) Dirichlet-multinomial statistical test comparing non-empty droplets against ambient RNA profiles Accurately identifies low-RNA cells while controlling false positives; recommended for almost all tissue samples barcoderanks Empirical inflection thresholding on total UMI rank curves Fast and lightweight; suitable for high-contrast samples or rapid preliminary quality screening

UMI Rank Curve Diagnostics & Decisions:

  • Steep drop: Clear distinction between genuine cells and background droplets; default settings yield optimal results.
  • Gradual decline / No clear inflection: High ambient RNA contamination or damaged cells. Use conservative cell counts by setting --expectcells or increasing --minumi 1500.
  • --minumi Candidate Evaluation Cutoff: Only applies to the emptydrops method (default: 1000). It defines the lower UMI boundary for candidate droplets to be evaluated in the non-ambient likelihood test. Candidate droplets meeting this cutoff (and exceeding the ambient pool's maximum UMI) undergo Monte-Carlo simulation against the ambient RNA profile; droplets below this threshold are directly treated as ambient background and excluded from EmptyDrops testing and cell rescue. If shallow sequencing causes valid small cells to be missed, lower this parameter (e.g., --minumi 500).
  • Cell count mismatch:
  • Too low: Check if --minumi is overly stringent or if sequencing depth is low; try lowering to --minumi 500.
  • Too high: Background noise droplets included; use --forcecells <N> to lock the target cell count directly (the pipeline sorts candidate barcodes in descending order of total valid UMI counts and retains the top N cells).

docs.title: 3. External Cell Whitelist Constraints (--consistent_cells)
docs.text:
Injects prior cell information during barcode merging and cell identification (e.g., cross-omics barcode pairing or historical gold standards). Supports headered .csv or .csv.gz:

Header Schema Function cell Constrains final identified valid cell barcode list cell,barcode Enforces explicit bead-to-cell merging mapping; bypasses Oligo analysis and applies this mapping directly cell,is_cell_barcode Supplies candidate barcodes and explicitly flags whether each is a genuine cell cell,barcode,is_cell_barcode Simultaneously specifies cell-to-bead barcode mappings and sets explicit cell calling status per barcode via is_cell_barcode (1/0 or true/false; e.g., passing a QC singlecell.csv directly)

docs.title: 4. Chemistry & Dark Reaction Configuration (--chemistry & --darkreaction)
docs.text:
• Chemistry (--chemistry): Supports scRNAv1HT, scRNAv2HT, scRNAv3HT, scRNA5Pv1. Defaults to auto.
  • Dark Reaction (--darkreaction): Configures dark cycles for MGI sequencing platforms.
  • Automatic detection: --darkreaction auto
  • Manual format: <cDNA>,<oligo>:
    • cDNA options: R1 or unset
    • Oligo options: R1R2, R1, or unset
    • Common combinations: --darkreaction R1,R1R2, --darkreaction unset,unset
  • Rule: If --chemistry is specified manually, --darkreaction must also be explicitly set.

docs.title: 5. Custom Read Structure (--customize)
docs.text:
For non-standard, modified, or third-party library protocols, use --customize to define exact 1-based closed-interval intervals for barcodes, UMIs, and reads (cannot exceed sequencing read length).

Library Structure Reference: For complete library linker sequences, physical segment coordinates, and dark reaction schematics, see Library Structure.

docs.title: Syntax Rules & Requirements
docs.text:
• Syntax: "<type>,<read>:<start>-<end>", delimited by semicolons ;.
  • cb: Cell Barcode (composed of 2 or 3 segments);
  • umi: Unique Molecular Identifier;
  • R1 / R2: Usable read sequence interval.
  • Rule: Must be passed twice sequentially for scRNA: first for cDNA, second for oligo.

docs.title: Scenario Comparisons: How to Strip Fixed Linker Sequences
Example A: Non-Dark Reaction Mode (Full Sequencing, Stripping Fixed Linkers)
docs.text:
In standard sequencing mode or sequencing without dark reactions, reads contain invariant linker sequences. If invariant bases are incorporated into barcodes, demultiplexing will fail. Directly skipping linker intervals safely removes them:

  • cDNA Extraction Strategy:
  • Skip 1–6 bp (Linker 1), capture cb,R1:7-16 (CB1 10bp)
  • Skip 17–22 bp (Linker 2), capture cb,R1:23-32 (CB2 10bp)
  • Skip 33–37 bp (Linker 3), capture umi,R1:38-47 (UMI 10bp)
  • Read 2 maps to 1–100 bp transcript sequence: R1,R2:1-100
  • Argument: --customize "cb,R1:7-16;cb,R1:23-32;umi,R1:38-47;R1,R2:1-100"
  • Oligo Extraction Strategy:
  • Read 1 skips linkers: cb,R1:7-16;cb,R1:23-32
  • Read 2 extracts first UMI (1–10 bp), then skips fixed linkers to extract Tag 1 (17–26 bp) and Tag 2 (33–42 bp): R1,R2:1-10;R1,R2:17-26;R1,R2:33-42
  • Argument: --customize "cb,R1:7-16;cb,R1:23-32;R1,R2:1-10;R1,R2:17-26;R1,R2:33-42"

Operational command: 

dnbc4tools rna run \
  --name non_dark_demo --genomeDir /reference/rna \
  --cDNAfastq1 cdna_R1.fq.gz --cDNAfastq2 cdna_R2.fq.gz \
  --oligofastq1 oligo_R1.fq.gz --oligofastq2 oligo_R2.fq.gz \
  --customize "cb,R1:7-16;cb,R1:23-32;umi,R1:38-47;R1,R2:1-100" \
  --customize "cb,R1:7-16;cb,R1:23-32;R1,R2:1-10;R1,R2:17-26;R1,R2:33-42" \
  --threads 20

docs.title: Example B: Dark Reaction Mode (Hardware Skips Fixed Sequences)
docs.text:
The sequencer has already skipped invariant linkers; output reads contain exclusively informative bases starting from base 1:

  • cDNA Extraction: --customize "cb,R1:1-10;cb,R1:11-20;umi,R1:21-30;R1,R2:1-100"
  • Oligo Extraction: --customize "cb,R1:1-10;cb,R1:11-20;R1,R2:1-30"

Operational command: 

dnbc4tools rna run \
  --name dark_demo --genomeDir /reference/rna \
  --cDNAfastq1 cdna_R1.fq.gz --cDNAfastq2 cdna_R2.fq.gz \
  --oligofastq1 oligo_R1.fq.gz --oligofastq2 oligo_R2.fq.gz \
  --customize "cb,R1:1-10;cb,R1:11-20;umi,R1:21-30;R1,R2:1-100" \
  --customize "cb,R1:1-10;cb,R1:11-20;R1,R2:1-30" \
  --threads 20

docs.title: 6. STAR Alignment Parameters (--star_parameters)
docs.text:
Pass validated STAR alignment, filtering, or scoring parameters via --star_parameters:

--star_parameters "--outFilterMismatchNmax 10 --outFilterMultimapNmax 1"

Note: Only STAR alignment options are accepted; pipeline-managed arguments (input/output paths, thread counts, genome index) and unknown options are rejected during preflight validation. If disk space or speed is a priority and downstream BAM inspection is not required, use --no_bam to skip BAM output entirely.

docs.title: Reference Database Construction (mkref)
docs.text: dnbc4tools rna mkref builds a STAR index database from reference FASTA and GTF annotation files.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
dnbc4tools rna mkref \
  --fasta genome.fa --ingtf genes.gtf \
  --species human --genomeDir /reference/rna --threads 20

docs.title: Full Command-Line Help
docs.text:
$ dnbc4tools rna mkref --help
dnbc4tools 3.2

Build an RNA reference database.

Usage: dnbc4tools rna mkref [OPTIONS]

options:
  --help              show this help message and exit

Input Files:
  Input genome FASTA files and gene-annotation GTF files. For mixed-species analysis, separate multiple files with
  commas.

  --fasta <FILE>      Reference-genome FASTA file path(s). Separate multiple files with commas (e.g.,
                      `genome1.fa,genome2.fa`).
  --ingtf <FILE>      Gene-annotation GTF file path(s). Separate multiple files with commas (e.g.,
                      `anno1.gtf,anno2.gtf`).

Basic Settings:
  --genomeDir <DIR>   Output directory path for generated reference files [default: current directory] (e.g.,
                      `./ref`).
  --species <STR>     Species identifier(s) [default: undefined]. For mixed-species references, provide
                      comma-separated names in the same order as --fasta and --ingtf (e.g., `human,mouse`).
  --threads <INT>     Number of CPU threads for parallel processing [default: all available cores] (e.g., `16`).

Advanced Settings:
  --chrM <STR>        Mitochondrial chromosome name [default: auto-detect common names]. For mixed-species references,
                      provide comma-separated names in --species order (e.g., `MT,chrM`).
  --limitram <INT>    RAM limit for STAR index generation, in GiB (e.g., `64`). Omit to use STAR's default. Index
                      sparsity can affect mapping memory use and speed.
  --extra-args <STR>  Additional validated STAR genomeGenerate parameters (e.g., `"--sjdbOverhang 100
                      --genomeSAsparseD 2"`). Preflight rejects alignment-only, unknown and mkref-managed parameters.
  --noindex           Skip the STAR index-generation step.

docs.title: Required & Basic Settings
docs.text: Option Type Default Description --fasta File path Required Reference genome FASTA file(s) (comma-separated for mixed species, e.g., human.fa,mouse.fa) --ingtf File path Required Gene annotation GTF file(s) (comma-separated for mixed species, e.g., human.gtf,mouse.gtf) --genomeDir Directory ./ Output directory path for generated reference database files --species String undefined Species identifier(s), comma-separated for mixed species (e.g., human,mouse) --threads Integer All cores Number of CPU threads for STAR indexing and annotation processing

docs.title: Advanced Settings
docs.text: Option Type Default Description --chrM String Auto-detect Mitochondrial chromosome name(s) in species order (e.g., MT,chrM) --limitram Integer (GiB) STAR default Maximum RAM limit during STAR genome index generation (in GiB); restricts memory usage during alignment, where lower memory allocation incurs higher processing time --extra-args String None Validated additional parameters passed to STAR genomeGenerate --noindex Flag Disabled Generates metadata and preprocessed annotations without building STAR index

docs.title: 1. GTF Annotation Requirements & Dual-Species Reference
docs.text:
• GTF Format Rules:
  • Must adhere to standard GTF format (GFF/GFF3 not supported).
  • Must include gene or transcript features as well as exon rows.
  • Attributes must include gene_id or gene_name, and transcript_id or transcript_name.
  • Chromosome identifiers must strictly match FASTA headers.
  • Mixed-Species Reference:
  • --fasta, --ingtf, and --species accept comma-separated inputs with matching order: 
    dnbc4tools rna mkref \
  --fasta human.fa,mouse.fa \
  --ingtf human.gtf,mouse.gtf \
  --species human,mouse
  • Gene names and chromosomes are automatically prefixed with the species name (e.g., human_GAPDH, mouse_Actb) for clean cross-species separation.

docs.title: 2. Directory Layout & ref.json Metadata
docs.text:
A successfully built reference directory generates a standardized layout under --genomeDir (subdivided into <species>/, named species1_and_species2 for dual-species references):

  • Database Compatibility: In addition to references built via rna mkref in the current version, dnbc4tools rna run is fully compatible with legacy v2 reference databases as well as standard Cell Ranger RNA reference directories (you can directly pass directories containing STAR index and annotations to --genomeDir).
genomeDir/
└── <species>/
    ├── fasta/
    │   └── genome.fa          # Unified processed FASTA sequence
    ├── genes/
    │   └── genes.gtf          # Standardized gene annotation
    ├── star/
    │   ├── SA                 # STAR genome index
    │   ├── SAindex            # STAR index parameters
    │   ├── chrLength.txt      # Chromosome lengths
    │   ├── chrName.txt        # Chromosome names
    │   ├── mtgene.list        # Mitochondrial gene list for QC
    │   └── genomeParameters.txt
    └── ref.json               # Reference configuration and provenance

Single-Species ref.json Example:

{
  "chrmt": "chrM",
  "genome": "/database/scRNA/Homo_sapiens/fasta/genome.fa",
  "genomeDir": "/database/scRNA/Homo_sapiens/star",
  "gtf": "/database/scRNA/Homo_sapiens/genes/genes.gtf",
  "input_fasta_files": [
    "genome.fa"
  ],
  "input_gtf_files": [
    "genes.gtf"
  ],
  "mtgenes": "/database/scRNA/Homo_sapiens/star/mtgene.list",
  "species": "Homo_sapiens",
  "version": "3.2"
}

Dual-Species ref.json Example:

{
  "chrmt": "human_chrM,mouse_chrM",
  "genome": "/database/scRNA/human_and_mouse/fasta/genome.fa",
  "genomeDir": "/database/scRNA/human_and_mouse/star",
  "gtf": "/database/scRNA/human_and_mouse/genes/genes.gtf",
  "input_fasta_files": [
    "human.fa",
    "mouse.fa"
  ],
  "input_gtf_files": [
    "human.gtf",
    "mouse.gtf"
  ],
  "mtgenes": "/database/scRNA/human_and_mouse/star/mtgene.list",
  "species": "human_and_mouse",
  "version": "3.2"
}

docs.title: Multi-Sample Workflow (multi)
docs.text: dnbc4tools rna multi generates standalone executable shell scripts for each sample defined in a tab-separated list file. It does not launch analyses automatically.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: dnbc4tools rna multi --list samples.tsv --genomeDir /reference/rna --threads 20

docs.title: Full Command-Line Help
docs.text:
$ dnbc4tools rna multi --help
dnbc4tools 3.2

Process multiple RNA-seq samples.

Usage: dnbc4tools rna multi [OPTIONS]

options:
  --help             show this help message and exit

Input Files:
  --list <FILE>      Tab-separated sample list: sample name <TAB> cDNA R1;R2 <TAB> oligo R1;R2. Multiple FASTQ files
                     within one end are comma-separated. Generates one shell script per sample in the current working
                     directory; run the generated scripts to start analysis.

Basic Settings:
  --genomeDir <DIR>  Reference genome directory path containing required reference files.
  --outdir <DIR>     Analysis output directory written into each generated script [default: current directory] (e.g.,
                     `./output`). Scripts are written to the current working directory.
  --threads <INT>    Number of CPU threads written into each generated analysis script. If omitted, each analysis
                     detects available cores when it runs.

Analysis Settings:
  --end5             Enable 5'-end single-cell transcriptome analysis.
  --no_bam           Skip BAM file generation for every sample in the generated scripts.

docs.title: Parameter Reference Tables
docs.text: Option Type Default Description --list File path Required Tab-separated sample list file --genomeDir Directory Required Reference genome directory path --outdir Directory ./ Output root directory written into each sample script (scripts are generated in current working directory) --threads Integer Auto-detect Thread count configured inside each generated script --end5 Flag Disabled Enables 5'-end scRNA analysis mode in generated scripts --no_bam Flag Disabled Skips BAM generation in all generated scripts

docs.title: 1. --list File Specification
docs.text:
The sample list must be a tab-separated (\t) text file with 3 columns: 1. Sample Name (sample_name) 2. cDNA FASTQ Paths (paired R1 and R2 separated by semicolon ;, multiple lane files comma-separated ,) 3. Oligo FASTQ Paths (paired R1 and R2 separated by semicolon ;, multiple lane files comma-separated ,)

SampleA /data/A_cDNA_R1.fq.gz;/data/A_cDNA_R2.fq.gz /data/A_oligo_R1.fq.gz;/data/A_oligo_R2.fq.gz
SampleB /data/B_cDNA_L1_R1.fq.gz,/data/B_cDNA_L2_R1.fq.gz;/data/B_cDNA_L1_R2.fq.gz,/data/B_cDNA_L2_R2.fq.gz /data/B_oligo_R1.fq.gz;/data/B_oligo_R2.fq.gz

docs.title: 2. Execution & Cluster Dispatch
docs.text:
• Running dnbc4tools rna multi creates per-sample shell scripts (e.g., SampleA.sh, SampleB.sh) in the current directory.
  • Each script contains the complete parameterized dnbc4tools rna run command.
  • Users can execute scripts directly via bash SampleA.sh or submit them to batch workload managers (e.g., Slurm, SGE) for cluster execution.

docs.title: scVDJ Parameters
docs.text: DNBelab C Series HT scVDJ Parameter Configuration Guide

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
This document explains the parameter definitions, default behaviors, and standard usage patterns for dnbc4tools vdj, covering single-cell TCR / BCR immune repertoire full-length assembly and clonotype identification.

Tip: Parameter specifications are based on current command-line help outputs. Examples can be used directly as operational templates.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
dnbc4tools vdj run \
  --name sample1 --fastqs /data/tcr \
  --ref human --chain TR \
  --beadstrans /results/rna/outs/singlecell.csv \
  --threads 20

docs.title: Full Command-Line Help
docs.text:
$ dnbc4tools vdj run --help
dnbc4tools 3.2

Process a single-cell V(D)J sample.

Usage: dnbc4tools vdj run [OPTIONS]

options:
  --help                       show this help message and exit

Input Files:
  Choose one input method: either `--fastqs` (directory input) or individual FASTQ files (`--fastq1` and
  `--fastq2`).

  --fastqs <DIR>               Input directory path containing paired-end FASTQ files (e.g., `./fastq_dir`).
  --fastq1 <FILE>              Read 1 FASTQ file path(s). Wildcards and comma-separated lists are supported (e.g.,
                               `sample1_L01_R1.fastq.gz,sample1_L02_R1.fastq.gz`).
  --fastq2 <FILE>              Read 2 FASTQ file path(s). Must match the order provided to `--fastq1` (e.g.,
                               `sample1_L01_R2.fastq.gz,sample1_L02_R2.fastq.gz`).

Basic Settings:
  --name <STR>                 Unique identifier for the sample. Used for naming output files and reports (e.g.,
                               `sample1`).
  --ref <STR>                  Reference database: `human`/`mouse`, or a custom reference directory path containing
                               `reference.json` (e.g., `human` or `./custom_vdj_ref`).
  --chain <STR>                VDJ receptor type: `IG` (BCR) or `TR` (TCR) (e.g., `TR`).
  --outdir <DIR>               Output directory path for results and reports [default: current directory] (e.g.,
                               `./output`).
  --threads <INT>              Number of CPU threads for parallel processing [default: all available cores].
  --beadstrans <FILE>          RNA-analysis `singlecell.csv` file path for cell filtering and bead merging info (e.g.,
                               `./singlecell.csv`).

Library Settings:
  --darkreaction <STR>         Dark cycle setting for VDJ library. Supported values: `R1`, `unset` (e.g., `R1`).
  --customize <STR>            Custom read structure string. Format: `<type>,<read>:<start>-<end>` joined by `;`.
                               (e.g., `"cb,R1:7-16;cb,R1:23-32;umi,R1:38-47;R1,R1:61-150;R2,R2:1-150"`).
  --enrichment_primers <FILE>  Custom inner enrichment primers file path (one primer sequence per line) (e.g.,
                               `./inner_primers.txt`).

Analysis Settings:
  --keep_all_cells             Retain all cells in analysis without RNA-based filtering.
  --r2_only                    Use only Read 2 sequences for VDJ assembly.
  --sample_read_pairs <INT>    Subsample the specified number of read pairs from input FASTQ file(s) (e.g.,
                               `1000000`).

docs.title: Required & Basic Settings
docs.text: Option Type Default Description --name String Required Unique sample identifier; used as output prefix and report title (e.g., sample_VDJ_001) --ref String / Path Required VDJ reference: built-in human or mouse, or a custom directory path containing reference.json --chain Choice Required Immune receptor type: TR (T-cell Receptor) or IG (B-cell Immunoglobulin) --beadstrans File path None Optional RNA cell table for bead mapping and cell filtering; omitting it automatically enables keep_all_cells --outdir Directory ./ Root output directory for analysis results and HTML reports --threads Integer All cores Number of CPU threads allocated for parallel processing

docs.title: Input Files Options
docs.text:
Choose one input mode: directory-based (--fastqs) or explicit files (--fastq1 and --fastq2).

Option Type Default Description --fastqs Directory None Directory containing paired-end FASTQ files (files reside directly in this directory; paired files auto-detected) --fastq1 File path None Read 1 FASTQ file list (supports wildcards * or comma-separated paths) --fastq2 File path None Read 2 FASTQ file list (order must strictly match --fastq1)

Tip: Sequencing Consistency & Batch Handling All FASTQ inputs in a single run must originate from the same library batch with identical sequencing modes and dark reaction settings; data from different libraries cannot be mixed. If different sequencing batches of the same library batch exhibit differing dark reaction cycles or read lengths, use the FASTQ trimming tool fqsubC4 to trim reads to match the standard library structure (see Library Structure).

docs.title: Library Chemistry & Read Structure
docs.text: Option Type Default Description --darkreaction Choice auto Dark cycle setting: auto, R1, unset (Note: VDJ does not support R1R2) --customize String None Custom barcode, UMI, and read structure string overriding dark reaction settings --enrichment_primers File path None Path to custom inner enrichment primers file (one primer per line)

docs.title: Analysis Settings & Tuning
docs.text: Option Type Default Description --keep_all_cells Flag Disabled Retain all assembled barcodes without RNA-based cell filtering (auto-enabled when omitting --beadstrans) --r2_only Flag Disabled Use only Read 2 sequences for VDJ assembly (for libraries where Read 1 carries only barcode/UMI) --sample_read_pairs Integer None Subsample a specified number of read pairs for rapid benchmarking

docs.title: 1. FASTQ Directory Structure & Input Rules
docs.text:
The VDJ --fastqs option points to a flat directory containing paired-end files directly:

VDJ_fastq_dir/
├── sample_VDJ_L01_R1.fastq.gz
├── sample_VDJ_L01_R2.fastq.gz
├── sample_VDJ_L02_R1.fastq.gz
└── sample_VDJ_L02_R2.fastq.gz
  • Naming detection: Supports standard read patterns _R1_, _R1, _1, _read1 paired with _R2_, _R2, _2, _read2; file extensions support .fastq.gz, .fq.gz, .fastq, .fq.
  • Individual inputs: If not using --fastqs, supply paired files via --fastq1 and --fastq2 with comma-separated file lists.

docs.title: 2. Cross-Omics Cell Linkage via --beadstrans
docs.text:
--beadstrans is a pivotal parameter for multi-omics integration, linking V(D)J clonotypic assemblies directly to 5' scRNA expression profiles:

  • Input source: Provide the outs/singlecell.csv file generated from the corresponding 5' scRNA analysis (supports .csv.gz from C6 multi-sample pipelines).
  • Core Mechanism: The pipeline performs comprehensive de novo assembly across all candidate VDJ reads. Subsequently, during the cell filtering and barcode translation stage, the pipeline applies the authentic cell whitelist from singlecell.csv to retain genuine cell contigs and translate bead barcodes into unified Cell IDs, outputting filtered_contig_annotations.csv matched with 5' scRNA.
  • Behavior when omitted: If --beadstrans is omitted, bead merging and cell filtering are skipped, and --keep_all_cells automatically engages to retain all assembled barcodes.
  • Recommendation: In paired 5' RNA + VDJ experiments, always provide --beadstrans to ensure clean clonotype-to-cell mapping and filter technical ambient noise.

docs.title: 3. Reference Databases (--ref) & Receptor Chains (--chain)
docs.text:
• Reference Database (--ref):
  • Built-in options: human or mouse (loads bundled V/D/J/C reference sequences).
  • Custom database: For other species, specify a custom directory path containing reference.json, V/D/J/C sequences, and primer configurations (compatible with Cell Ranger VDJ reference databases).
  • Receptor Type (--chain):
  • TR: T-cell Receptor (TRA, TRB, TRG, TRD chains).
  • IG: Immunoglobulin (IGH, IGK, IGL chains).

docs.title: 4. Dark Reaction & Custom Read Structure
docs.text:
Library Structure Reference: For complete VDJ library linker sequences, TSO regions, and dark reaction schematics, see Library Structure.

  • Dark Reaction (--darkreaction): VDJ libraries support only Read 1 dark cycles or unset:
  • auto: Automatically inferred
  • R1: Read 1 contains dark cycles
  • unset: No dark reactions
  • Note: R1R2 is invalid for VDJ.
  • Custom Read Structure (--customize): 
    # Standard VDJ structure example: Barcode 1 (1-10bp) + Barcode 2 (11-20bp) + UMI (21-30bp) in R1
--customize "cb,R1:1-10;cb,R1:11-20;umi,R1:21-30;R1,R1:31-120;R2,R2:1-150"

docs.title: 5. Custom Inner Enrichment Primers (--enrichment_primers)
docs.text:
For non-human/non-mouse custom species or modified library protocols, provide an inner enrichment primer file (plain text, one primer sequence per line):

GTCCTCGGTGGCCTCCACGTG
AGCACCTGGGGCCTCGGCCAC
CCTGGACTCCTGGGCCCCAG

docs.title: Tools Parameters
docs.text:
DNBelab C Series HT Auxiliary Tools Parameter Reference

The public subcommand of dnbc4tools tools is mkgtf. The following bam2fastq, chromsplit, and fqsubC4 are standalone auxiliary tools located in the software misc directory, not subcommands of dnbc4tools tools.

docs.title: GTF Processing (mkgtf)
docs.text:
Core Function

GTF annotation processing tool supporting gene type statistics, rule-based filtering, format validation, and automated repair for single-cell transcriptomic reference pipelines.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: dnbc4tools tools mkgtf --ingtf genes.gtf --output genes.filtered.gtf

docs.title: Full Command-Line Help
docs.text:
$ dnbc4tools tools mkgtf --help
dnbc4tools 3.2

Filter and process GTF annotation files.

Usage: dnbc4tools tools mkgtf [OPTIONS]

options:
  --help           show this help message and exit

Basic Settings:
  --action <STR>   Operation type: 'mkgtf' (filter by gene types), 'stats' (count statistics), 'check' (validate
                   format) [default: mkgtf] (e.g., `stats`).
  --ingtf <FILE>   Path to input GTF annotation file (required) (e.g., `genes.gtf`).
  --output <FILE>  Path to output file (required unless --action stats). If omitted for "stats", statistics are
                   printed to stdout.

Analysis Settings:
  --include <STR>  Comma-separated list of gene types to include. Supports wildcards (e.g., 'IG_*' will match
                   'IG_V_gene', 'IG_C_gene'). [default: protein_coding,lncRNA,lincRNA,antisense,IG_*,TR_*].
  --type <STR>     Attribute name for gene type classification (e.g., gene_biotype, gene_type).
  --feature <STR>  Feature type to process from GTF. Use 'transcript' if no 'gene' entries exist [default: gene].

Usage Examples:
  Statistics:   dnbc4tools tools mkgtf --action stats --ingtf genes.gtf
  Filtering:    dnbc4tools tools mkgtf --ingtf genes.gtf --output filtered.gtf --include 'protein_coding,lncRNA'
  Validation:   dnbc4tools tools mkgtf --action check --ingtf genes.gtf --output corrected.gtf

docs.title: Parameter Reference Tables
docs.text: Option Type Default Description --ingtf File path Required Path to the input standard GTF annotation file (GFF/GFF3 not supported) --output File path Conditional Path to output file (required for mkgtf and check; prints to stdout for stats) --action Choice mkgtf Operation mode: mkgtf (filter by type), stats (count distribution), check (validate & fix) --include String Default set Comma-separated gene biotypes to retain (supports wildcards *, e.g., IG_*) --type String auto Attribute key in GTF defining gene type classification (e.g., gene_biotype, gene_type) --feature String gene Target feature level in GTF (usually gene; fallback to transcript if absent)

docs.title: 1. Filtering Mode (--action mkgtf)
docs.text:
Extracts trusted biotypes from full annotations containing pseudogenes or non-coding fragments, reducing non-unique mapping:

dnbc4tools tools mkgtf \
  --action mkgtf \
  --ingtf Homo_sapiens.GRCh38.108.gtf \
  --output Homo_sapiens.filtered.gtf \
  --include "protein_coding,lncRNA,IG_*,TR_*"
  • Wildcard Matching: Pattern IG_* matches IG_V_gene, IG_C_gene, IG_J_gene, etc.
  • Default Inclusion Set: protein_coding,lncRNA,lincRNA,antisense,IG_*,TR_*.

docs.title: 2. Summary Mode (--action stats)
docs.text:
Tallies gene counts across all biotypes to evaluate source annotation structure and determine correct attribute tags:

dnbc4tools tools mkgtf --action stats --ingtf genes.gtf

docs.title: 3. Validation & Repair Mode (--action check)
docs.text:
Validates GTF integrity and automatically reconstructs missing parent features (e.g., inferring missing gene rows from existing transcript entries):

dnbc4tools tools mkgtf --action check --ingtf raw_genes.gtf --output corrected.gtf

docs.title: BAM to FASTQ (bam2fastq)
docs.text:
Conversion Utility (Located in Software misc Directory)

Converts C4 cDNA and C4/C6 oligo BAM files back into FASTQ format. Features coordinate/name-sorted input handling, automatic single/paired-end detection, C4 vs. C6 double-UMI layout recognition, multi-threaded parallel compression, and genomic locus extraction.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
$ bam2fastq -h
BAM to FASTQ Converter for cDNA and oligo data

Usage: bam2fastq [OPTIONS] <BAM> <OUTPUT>

Arguments:
  <BAM>     Path to the input BAM file
  <OUTPUT>  Directory where FASTQ files will be written

Options:
      --library-type <LIBRARY_TYPE>  BAM library format; auto checks c4_oligo program metadata and oligo tags [default: auto] [possible values: auto, cDNA, oligo]
      --oligo-layout <OLIGO_LAYOUT>  Oligo layout (default: auto): c4 barcode only or c6 barcode plus R1 UMI [default: auto] [possible values: auto, c4, c6]
  -t, --threads <THREADS>            Number of CPU threads for parallel processing (default: all available cores) [default: 8]
  -r, --locus <REGION>               Process a zero-based, half-open genomic region (format: chr1:1000-2000)
      --bx-list <BX_LIST>            BX list; requires a BX-sorted BAM and .bam.bxi index
  -n, --reads-per-fastq <READS>      Maximum number of reads per FASTQ file. All reads go to a single file if not specified.
      --max-memory <MEMORY>          Working-memory target in MB for caches, queues and output buffers; not a hard RSS limit.
      --traceback                    Show detailed error traceback
      --relaxed[=<RELAXED>]          Relaxed mode: skip unpaired reads instead of erroring [default: true] [possible values: true, false]
      --auto-detect[=<AUTO_DETECT>]  Automatically detect paired-end status from BAM flags [default: true] [possible values: true, false]
      --no-compress                  Disable gzip compression for output FASTQ files
  -h, --help                         Print help
  -V, --version                      Print version

docs.title: Parameter Reference Tables
docs.text: Argument / Option Type Default Description <BAM> File path Required (Positional) Path to input BAM (coordinate-sorted or name-sorted cDNA BAM, or c4_oligo BAM) <OUTPUT> Directory path Required (Positional) Directory where output FASTQ files will be written --library-type Choice (auto, cDNA, oligo) auto BAM library format; auto checks c4_oligo program metadata and oligo tags --oligo-layout Choice (auto, c4, c6) auto Oligo layout: c4 barcode only or c6 barcode plus R1 UMI (auto detects automatically) -t, --threads Integer All available cores (default: 8) Number of CPU threads for parallel processing -r, --locus String None Process a zero-based, half-open genomic region (format: chr1:1000-2000; requires .bai index) --bx-list File path None Filter cDNA by a barcode whitelist (requires BX-sorted BAM and .bam.bxi index) -n, --reads-per-fastq Integer None (single file) Maximum number of reads per FASTQ file; all reads go to a single file if not specified --max-memory Integer (MB) Half available RAM Working-memory target in MB for caches, queues, and output buffers; not a hard RSS ceiling --traceback Flag Disabled Show detailed error traceback and context --relaxed Boolean (true, false) true Relaxed mode: skip unpaired reads instead of erroring --auto-detect Boolean (true, false) true Automatically detect paired-end status from BAM flags --no-compress Flag Disabled Disable gzip compression for output FASTQ files (outputs uncompressed .fastq) -h, --help Flag - Print help message and exit -V, --version Flag - Print version and exit

docs.title: Practical Examples
docs.text:
# Basic conversion (auto-detects paired-end/single-end and library type, uses all available cores)
bam2fastq sample.bam ./output/

# Custom thread budget
bam2fastq -t 20 sample.bam ./output/

# Extract specific genomic region (requires .bai index)
bam2fastq -t 8 -r chr1:1000000-2000000 sample.bam ./output_chr1/

# Disable compression for fastest write speed
bam2fastq -t 8 --no-compress sample.bam ./output/

# Chunk output into 50M reads per file
bam2fastq -t 20 -n 50000000 sample.bam ./output/

# Convert Oligo BAM (auto-detects C4 single-UMI vs C6 double-UMI layout)
bam2fastq -t 20 oligo.records.bam ./output_oligo/

docs.title: Chromosome Splitting (chromsplit)
docs.text:
Core Function

Splits large scaffold/chromosome sequences at N-stretches or intergenic regions based on optional GTF annotations to prevent fragment length from exceeding tool limits (e.g., $2^{29}-1$ bp).

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
$ chromsplit --help
Split large genome sequences into smaller fragments at N-stretches or intergenic regions

Usage: chromsplit [OPTIONS] --fasta <FA> --prefix <PREFIX>

Options:
  --fasta <FA>               Input genome sequence file in FASTA format
  --gtf <GTF>                Optional GTF/GFF annotation file for the genome
  --prefix <PREFIX>          Prefix for output files (.fa and .cutsite.tsv will be appended)
  --min_length <MIN_LENGTH>  Minimum length of output scaffold fragments [default: 300000000]
  --max_length <MAX_LENGTH>  Maximum length of output scaffold fragments [default: 500000000]
  --cut_site <CUT_SITE>      Optional cut site file containing predefined split positions
  --help                     Print help
  --version                  Print version

docs.title: Parameter Reference Tables
docs.text: Option Type Default Description --fasta File path Required Input genome FASTA sequence file --prefix String Required Prefix for output files (generates <prefix>.fa and <prefix>.cutsite.tsv) --gtf File path None Optional GTF annotation to guide splitting across intergenic intervals --min_length Integer (bp) 300000000 Minimum fragment length in base pairs --max_length Integer (bp) 500000000 Maximum fragment length in base pairs --cut_site File path None File containing custom pre-defined coordinate break points

docs.title: Practical Examples
docs.text:
# Split genome using GTF to protect gene structure
chromsplit --fasta large_genome.fasta --gtf genes.gtf --prefix genome_split

# Custom fragment bounds (200Mb to 400Mb)
chromsplit --fasta large_genome.fasta --prefix custom_split --min_length 200000000 --max_length 400000000

docs.title: FASTQ Substring Slicing (fqsubC4)
docs.text:
Core Function

High-performance FASTQ substring slicer. Extracts exact 1-based base coordinate intervals to unify barcode architectures across historical sequencing batches.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
$ fqsubC4 --help
Extracts regions from FASTQ sequences

Usage: fqsubC4 [OPTIONS] --input <FILE> --output <FILE> --regions <REGIONS>

Options:
  --input <FILE>       Path to input FASTQ file (supports both uncompressed and gzipped formats)
  --output <FILE>      Path to output FASTQ file (automatically compressed if ending in .gz)
  --regions <REGIONS>  Comma-separated regions in format start:end (e.g., 7:16,23:32,38:47)
  --threads <THREADS>  Number of threads to use for parallel processing [default: 8]
  --help               Print help
  --version            Print version

docs.title: Parameter Reference Tables
docs.text: Option Type Default Description --input File path Required Input FASTQ file (supports .fq, .fastq, .fq.gz, .fastq.gz) --output File path Required Output FASTQ path (automatically compressed if ending in .gz) --regions String Required Comma-separated 1-based intervals in start:end format --threads Integer 8 Number of CPU threads for parallel I/O and processing

docs.title: Practical Examples
docs.text:
# Extract two barcode intervals from Read 1 and output compressed FASTQ
fqsubC4 \
  --input sample_raw_R1.fq.gz \
  --output extracted_R1.fq.gz \
  --regions "7:16,23:32" \
  --threads 8

docs.title: DNBelab C Series HT C6 Analysis Pipeline
docs.text: Multiplexed Single-Cell RNA Analysis & Sample Deconvolution Guide

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
C6 is a high-throughput multiplexed single-cell RNA-seq solution based on Sample Barcode multiplexing. Multiple biological samples are labeled with distinct Sample Barcodes during library construction and pooled for sequencing. In the bioinformatics stage, dnbc4tools automatically demultiplexes samples, aggregates beads, independently calls cells per sample, and generates full expression quantifications and interactive quality reports.

Workflow: Data Input → Barcode Demultiplexing → Alignment → Bead Aggregation → Per-Sample Cell Calling → Unified & Per-Sample Deliverables

Usage Note: $dnbc4tools represents the executable path and should be replaced with your actual installation path. The C6 workflow is orchestrated via the multi run command to automate sample demultiplexing and per-sample deliverables.

docs.title: Core Steps
docs.text:
The C6 pooled multiplexing workflow encompasses 5 essential stages from shared raw libraries to per-sample outputs:

Step Stage Core Mechanism Key Inputs & Deliverables 01 Input Preparation & Validation Shared dual libraries; automated dark cycle detection; sectioned CSV validation Shared FASTQs, Config CSV ➔ Validated Parameters 02 Sample Barcode Demultiplexing Extracts barcodes from Oligo reads with whitelist error correction Oligo Reads ➔ Droplet Assignment, Unassigned Tracking 03 Alignment & Bead Aggregation STAR alignment & annotation; similarity-based bead pooling; global high-occupancy filtering cDNA Reads ➔ Alignment BAM, Bead-to-Cell Merging 04 Independent Cell Calling Completely isolated per-sample EmptyDrops calling; adaptive noise safeguards Assigned Droplets ➔ Per-Sample Authentic Cells 05 Archiving & Output Per-sample matrices/reports/BAMs; pooled combined matrix & batch summary report per_sample_outs/ Deliverables + Combined Report

docs.title: Step 1: Input Preparation & Configuration
docs.text:
• Sequencing Libraries: A shared pooled pair of cDNA and Oligo FASTQ libraries.
  • Pipeline Configuration: A sectioned CSV file (e.g., sample.config.csv) declaring sample identifiers and their corresponding Sample Barcodes in the [samples] section.
  • Dark Reaction Auto-Detection: Version 3.2 automatically detects dark reaction cycles (Dark Cycles) in cDNA and Oligo reads without manual intervention.

Key Pillars Shared Paired Libraries Dark Cycle Detection Sectioned CSV Mapping

docs.title: Step 2: Sample Barcode Identification & Demultiplexing
docs.text:
• Barcode Matching: Extracts Sample Barcodes from Oligo reads and matches them against the built-in whitelist with error-correction.
  • Flexible Mapping: Assigns beads and droplets to their respective biological samples; supports single barcodes (e.g., BC01) or multi-barcode assignments per sample (e.g., BC02;BC03).
  • Unassigned Tracking: Reads that cannot be confidently matched to a known barcode are tracked under the Unassigned category, for reviewing unassigned read counts.

Key Pillars Whitelist Error-Correction Multi-Barcode Pooling Unassigned Tracking

docs.title: Step 3: Transcript Alignment & Bead Aggregation
docs.text:
• High-Quality Alignment: Aligns cDNA reads against the reference genome using an optimized STAR workflow with functional region annotation.
  • Cross-Sample Bead Aggregation: Uses a robust bead similarity scoring algorithm to merge beads originating from the same physical droplet while retaining Sample Barcode suffixes.
  • Experiment-Wide High-Occupancy Filtering: high_occupancy_filter=true is enabled by default to remove multiplexed droplet artifacts across the entire experiment.

Key Pillars STAR Alignment Bead Aggregation High-Occupancy Filtering

docs.title: Step 4: Independent Cell Calling per Sample
docs.text:
• Isolated Calling: Droplets assigned to each sample undergo independent cell calling (EmptyDrops), so that the called-cell set is determined separately for each sample.
  • Adaptive Bounds Protection: 3.2 introduces upper and lower bounds on the automatically estimated cell count.
  • Intra-Cell UMI Conflict Resolution: Resolves ambiguous UMIs mapped to multiple genes within the same cell using read counts; UMIs without a unique gene assignment are excluded from expression counts.

Key Pillars Per-Sample Calling EmptyDrops Safeguard UMI De-noising

docs.title: Step 5: Result Archiving & Output
docs.text:
• Per-Sample Deliverables: Each sample receives its own subdirectory under per_sample_outs/<sample>/ with raw/filtered expression matrices (MEX, H5, and H5AD formats), dimensionality reduction, clustering (PCA, UMAP, marker genes), and an interactive HTML report.
  • Per-Sample BAM Output: When BAM generation is enabled, alignments are partitioned into sample-specific BAM files (<sample>_alignments.bam), alongside unassigned alignments and a shared oligo BAM.
  • Root Combined Matrices: A unified matrix containing all called cells across all samples is provided in the root directory (MEX, H5, H5AD) with raw counts for downstream batch correction (e.g., Harmony).
  • Batch Multi-Sample Report: A root <run>_multi_report.html summarizes cell counts, sequencing saturation, library QC, and cross-sample comparison charts.

Key Pillars Per-Sample MEX/H5/H5AD Per-Sample BAM Global Pooled Matrix Two-Tier HTML Reports

docs.title: Input Configuration
docs.text:
C6 analysis uses a sectioned CSV configuration file (commonly named sample.config.csv), consisting of three core sections:

Section Purpose Key Parameters [rna] Global transcriptome and run settings genomeDir, chemistry,scRNAC6, darkreaction,auto, no_bam [libraries] Shared sequencing library path declaration fastqs (pointing to the directory containing cDNA/ and oligo/), feature_types,rna [samples] Sample and Sample Barcode mapping table sample_id, probe_barcode_ids, expectcells (optional)

docs.title: Minimal Configuration Example
docs.text:
[rna]
genomeDir,/database/scRNA/Homo_sapiens
chemistry,scRNAC6
darkreaction,auto

[libraries]
fastqs,feature_types
/rawdata/c6_pooled_run,rna

[samples]
sample_id,probe_barcode_ids
Sample_1,BC01
Sample_2,BC02;BC03

Optional BAM output setting: This example uses the default [rna] no_bam,false, generating per-sample BAMs, unassigned BAM, and oligo BAM with their applicable indexes. To save disk space, add no_bam,true to [rna]; BAM files and their indexes will then be omitted.

Tip: If multiple barcodes are assigned to the same sample, separate them with semicolons ; (e.g., BC02;BC03). For complete configuration specifications, refer to C6 Parameters.

docs.title: Execution Command
docs.text:
$dnbc4tools multi run \
  --name c6_demo \
  --csv sample.config.csv \
  --outdir ./results \
  --threads 16

docs.title: Pre-Run Checklist
docs.text:
C6 Pre-Run Verification Checklist

  • Chemistry Type Declaration: Ensure chemistry,scRNAC6 is configured in the [rna] section of the CSV.
  • Shared Data Paths: Ensure fastqs in [libraries] points to a valid path containing paired cDNA/ and oligo/ subdirectories and FASTQ files.
  • Sample Barcode Mapping: Verify sample_id values in [samples] are unique, and probe_barcode_ids correspond to experimental barcodes (e.g. BC01 or BC02;BC03).
  • STAR Reference Index: Verify genomeDir points to a complete and valid STAR reference directory.

docs.title: DNBelab C Series HT Multi-omics Analysis Pipeline
docs.text: Single-Cell Multi-omics Integrated Analysis Guide

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The Multi-omics workflow unifies orchestration and generates combined reports; ATAC is analyzed independently and summarized, while RNA and VDJ support cell association analysis. A single configuration file coordinates all sub-pipelines and generates combined reports for cross-omics inspection.

Workflow: Configuration → Module Dispatch → Parallel Analysis → Status Aggregation → Combined Report

Usage Note: $dnbc4tools represents the executable path and should be replaced with your actual installation path. The backslash \ is used to split commands across multiple lines for readability; commands can also be executed on a single line.

Key Features:

Feature Description Unified Orchestration One entry command dispatches multiple omics modules (RNA / ATAC / VDJ) Status Tracking Module-level status management (success / failed / skipped / reused) Combined Report Generates combined HTML report supporting cross-omics browsing and comparison Flexible Configuration Supports arbitrary module combinations (single / dual / all modules)

docs.title: Configuration File Structure
docs.text:
multi run uses a CSV configuration file to define module parameters and input data. Typical sections include:

Section Purpose Key Parameters [rna] RNA analysis module configuration genomeDir, expectcells, no_bam... [atac] ATAC analysis module configuration genomeDir, frags_cutoff, need_bam... [vdj-t] T-cell VDJ analysis configuration ref, beadstrans... [vdj-b] B-cell VDJ analysis configuration ref, beadstrans... [libraries] Input data mapping (required) fastqs, feature_types

Detailed Configuration: Please refer to the Multi Parameter Documentation for complete CSV configuration specifications and parameter mappings.

[libraries] Input Directory Guidelines:

  • rna: fastqs points to the RNA FASTQ root directory, which must contain cDNA/ and oligo/ subdirectories.
  • atac: fastqs points to the FASTQ directory for the ATAC library, with paired R1/R2 files placed directly under it.
  • vdj-t / vdj-b: fastqs points to the TCR or BCR FASTQ library directory. TCR and BCR data must be configured separately.
  • File Pairing: The pipeline automatically pairs files based on _R1/_R2 or _R1_/_R2_ naming patterns.

docs.title: Configuration Examples
docs.text:
Scenario 1: RNA + VDJ (TCR / BCR) Joint Analysis (Recommended)

[rna]
genomeDir,/database/scRNA/Homo_sapiens
end5,true
no_bam,true

[vdj-t]
ref,human

[libraries]
fastqs,feature_types
/rawdata/multi_sample/rna,rna
/rawdata/multi_sample/tcr,vdj-t

Scenario 2: Full Multi-Omics (RNA + ATAC + VDJ) Analysis

[rna]
genomeDir,/database/scRNA/Homo_sapiens
end5,true
no_bam,true

[atac]
genomeDir,/database/scATAC/Homo_sapiens

[vdj-t]
ref,human

[vdj-b]
ref,human

[libraries]
fastqs,feature_types
/rawdata/multi_sample/rna,rna
/rawdata/multi_sample/atac,atac
/rawdata/multi_sample/tcr,vdj-t
/rawdata/multi_sample/bcr,vdj-b

docs.title: Running Command
docs.text:
$dnbc4tools multi run \
  --csv sample.csv \
  --name demo \
  --outdir /data/result \
  --threads 20

Parameter Description:

Parameter Required Description --csv Yes Path to CSV configuration file --name Yes Sample name for output directory naming --outdir No Output directory, defaults to current directory ./ --threads No Number of CPU threads, uses software default if not specified

docs.title: Pre-Run Checklist
docs.text:
Multi-Omics Pre-Run Verification Checklist

  • Core Flags: Both --csv configuration file path and --name sample identifier are supplied, and --outdir is writable.
  • Enabled Sections: The CSV file contains at least one active omics section (e.g. [rna], [vdj-t], [atac]).
  • Data Path Mapping: Input paths in [libraries] physically exist and accurately correspond to feature_types (rna/atac/vdj-t/vdj-b).
  • Reference Readiness: Database paths (e.g. genomeDir, ref) for all active modules are valid and version-compatible.

docs.title: Execution Flow
docs.text: Stage Stage Name Core Responsibility Deliverable 01 Config Parsing & QC Parses CSV sections, verifies library paths, and detects dark reactions Validated configuration 02 Task Queue Building Constructs the execution flow based on enabled modules and checks reuse flags Scheduled task queue 03 Sub-Pipeline Runs Sequentially executes core alignments, bead merging, and cell calling (RNA/VDJ/ATAC) Module output folders 04 Status Aggregation Captures exit codes, runtimes, and skip/reuse status across all modules run_manifest.json 05 Combined Reporting Integrates cross-omics barcode translation (e.g. RNA-VDJ) into an interactive report <sample>_multi_report.html

docs.title: Execution Highlights
docs.text:
Core Principles

  • Multi handles "orchestration and aggregation"; module algorithms remain in each single-omics sub-pipeline.
  • A module failure will not invalidate other completed modules but will be reflected in the final status summary.

docs.title: Output Directory Structure
docs.text:
After completion, results are organized under <outdir>/<name>/:

<outdir>/<name>/
├── outs/                                    # Organized output results
│   ├── <sample>_multi_report.html           # Multi-omics combined report
│   ├── rna/                                 # RNA results (if enabled)
│   ├── atac/                                # ATAC results (if enabled)
│   ├── vdj-t/                               # VDJ-T results (if enabled)
│   └── vdj-b/                               # VDJ-B results (if enabled)
├── logs/                                    # Logs and runtime status
│   ├── run_manifest.json                    # Module runtime status summary
│   └── *.log                                # Module runtime logs
├── RNA_ANALYSIS_WORKFLOW_PROCESSING/        # Module workflow directories (if enabled)
├── ATAC_ANALYSIS_WORKFLOW_PROCESSING/
├── VDJ-T_ANALYSIS_WORKFLOW_PROCESSING/
└── VDJ-B_ANALYSIS_WORKFLOW_PROCESSING/

docs.title: Key Output Files
docs.text:
File/Directory Description outs/<sample>_multi_report.html Multi-omics combined report displaying core QC and analysis charts from all modules outs/rna/ RNA module standard outputs (matrix, statistics, module report, etc.) outs/atac/ ATAC module standard outputs (fragment files, peaks, module report, etc.) outs/vdj-t/ / outs/vdj-b/ VDJ module standard outputs (clonotypes, annotations, module report, etc.) logs/run_manifest.json Module runtime status summary including return codes, runtime, and reuse status

Detailed Output Description: Please refer to the Multi Output Documentation for detailed interpretation of the combined report.

docs.title: Pipeline Overview
docs.text:
Choose a workflow based on your assay and sequencing design.

Module Core Steps Guide RNA cDNA/oligo QC → Alignment & UMI counting → Cell calling → Clustering & report RNA pipeline ATAC Fragment processing → Bead merging → Peak calling & matrix → Cell QC & clustering ATAC pipeline V(D)J QC → De novo assembly → Annotation & filtering → Clonotypes & report VDJ pipeline Multi-omics CSV configuration → Modality dispatch → Result archiving → Combined report Multi pipeline C6 Multiplexed Shared library → Sample Barcode demultiplexing → Per-sample cell calling & analysis C6 pipeline

docs.title: Workflow Selection
docs.text:
• Independent Single-Omics: Run the respective pipeline directly (scRNA, scATAC, or scVDJ). VDJ accepts an optional RNA singlecell.csv for bead mapping and cell filtering; omitting --beadstrans automatically enables keep_all_cells.
  • Multi-omics (Multi): When RNA, ATAC, or VDJ data are generated for the same batch, use a single CSV file to orchestrate modules and generate combined reports.
  • C6 Multiplexed RNA: For pooled libraries with Sample Barcodes, configure the [samples] section to automate demultiplexing and per-sample deliverables.

docs.title: DNBelab C Series HT scATAC Analysis Pipeline
docs.text: Single-Cell ATAC Sequencing Data Analysis Guide

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
This document provides a detailed guide for analyzing single-cell ATAC sequencing data using dnbc4tools.

Workflow: Raw Data → Quality Control → Alignment → Bead Merging → Peak Calling → Cell Identification → Dimensionality Reduction & Clustering → Analysis Report

Usage Note: $dnbc4tools represents the executable path and must be replaced with the actual installation path. The backslash \ is used to split a command across multiple lines for readability.

docs.title: File Preparation
docs.text:
The analysis requires FASTQ files:

File Type Description ATAC Library Sequencing data containing cell barcodes and chromatin accessibility information

Note: Ensure that the FASTQ files are of good quality and record their paths for subsequent analysis.

docs.title: Reference Database Input Files
docs.text:
File Type Format Description Genome File FASTA Contains the complete genome sequence of a species, including chromosomes, mitochondria, and other genetic information, typically the primary assembly. This file provides the foundation for genome analysis and alignment. Annotation File GTF Contains detailed information about genes, transcripts, exons, and other functional regions in the genome. This file identifies the location, type, and related attributes of genes.

Recommended Data Source: It is recommended to use files from the Ensembl database. Ensembl's GTF files contain optional tags that facilitate filtering with dnbc4tools tools mkgtf.

GTF File Requirements:

  • Must contain annotations of type gene or transcript as well as exon.
  • Attributes must include gene_id or gene_name and transcript_id or transcript_name.
  • The GFF file format is not supported.
  • The genome file and annotation file must be from corresponding versions.

docs.title: GTF File Processing (Optional)
docs.text: For details on GTF file filtering, please refer to the scRNA analysis pipeline.

docs.title: Reference Database Construction
docs.text: Before running the dnbc4tools atac run analysis, a reference database must be built. This step uses the annotation file (GTF) and reference genome (FASTA) to create Chromap alignment indexes and genomic region files for read alignment and statistical analysis.

docs.title: Single-Species Reference Construction (e.g., Mouse)
docs.text:
# Build single-species reference database
$dnbc4tools atac mkref \
  --fasta genome.fa \
  --ingtf genes.gtf \
  --species Mus_musculus \
  --genomeDir /database/scATAC/Mus_musculus

docs.title: Dual-Species Mixed Reference Construction (Human + Mouse)
docs.text:
Applicable for human-mouse mixed-cell validation experiments:

# Build dual-species mixed reference database (Human + Mouse; --prefix is unsupported for mixed species)
# Prepare FASTA and filtered GTF files for both species, separating multiple inputs with commas
$dnbc4tools atac mkref \
  --fasta GRCh38.primary_assembly.genome.fa,GRCm38.primary_assembly.genome.fa \
  --ingtf hg38.filtered.gtf,mm10.filtered.gtf \
  --species hg38,mm10 \
  --genomeDir /database/scATAC/hg38_mm10

Dual-Species Notes:

  • --fasta: Provide genome FASTA file paths for both species, separated by a comma ,.
  • --ingtf: Provide filtered GTF annotation paths for both species, separated by a comma , (order must strictly match --fasta).
  • --species: Declare concise identifiers for each species (e.g. hg38,mm10).
  • Important Restriction: When constructing a dual-species reference, the --prefix argument is not supported (due to differing chromosome naming rules between species).

Output Directory:

Upon successful execution, a reference database directory will be created at the specified location with the following structure:

/database/scATAC/Mus_musculus
├── fasta
│   ├── genome.fa
│   ├── genome.fa.fai
│   ├── genome.index
│   └── genome.index.log
├── genes
│   └── genes.gtf
├── ref.json
└── regions
    ├── chrom.sizes
    ├── promoter.bed
    └── tss.bed

ref.json Example:

The ref.json file records the main information of the database:

{
    "species": "Mus_musculus",
    "input_fasta_files": [
        "genome.fa"
    ],
    "input_gtf_files": [
        "genes.gtf"
    ],
    "genome": "fasta/genome.fa",
    "index": "fasta/genome.index",
    "gtf": "genes/genes.gtf",
    "chrmt": "chrM",
    "chloroplast": "None",
    "chromeSize": "regions/chrom.sizes",
    "tss": "regions/tss.bed",
    "promoter": "regions/promoter.bed",
    "version": "3.2",
    "blacklist": "None",
    "genomesize": "mm"
}

Note: Building the reference database can be time-consuming, depending on the genome size and computational resources. The main analysis pipeline is compatible with older database versions.

Runtime Log Example:

The following information will be printed during runtime:

...done

 2025-11-12 16:13:32 Writing genome FASTA file into reference folder...
...done

 2025-11-12 16:13:33 Indexing genome FASTA file...
...done

 2025-11-12 16:13:34 Writing genes GTF file into reference folder...
...done

 2025-11-12 16:13:38 Extracting TSS and promoter regions from GTF file...
...done

 2025-11-12 16:13:42 Generating Chromap genome index...
...done

 2025-11-12 16:14:07 Writing reference JSON file...
...done
Analysis Complete

docs.title: Main Pipeline
docs.text:
The main pipeline can be used in two ways:

  • Single-sample analysis: Run dnbc4tools atac run directly for a complete analysis of one ATAC library.
  • Multi-sample batch processing: Use dnbc4tools atac multi to generate one run script per sample, which is useful for preparing batch jobs.

docs.title: Single-Sample Analysis
docs.text:
The ATAC main analysis pipeline processes single-cell ATAC library data from a single sample. The core workflow includes:

  1. Data Processing: Perform quality control and alignment to generate the fragments file for all beads.
  2. Peak Calling: Run peak calling on aggregated data to identify open chromatin regions.
  3. Cell Identification: Identify valid cells using fragment information within peak regions.
  4. Advanced Analysis: Perform cell filtering, dimensionality reduction, and clustering.
  5. Report Generation: Integrate outputs from all steps and generate the HTML report plus other result files.

Two input methods are supported:

Method 1: Directory Input (Recommended)

$dnbc4tools atac run \
  --name sample \
  --fastqs /data \
  --genomeDir /opt/database/Mus_musculus \
  --threads 10

Directory structure example: 

/data/
├── sample_R1.fastq.gz
└── sample_R2.fastq.gz

Directory requirements:

  • The --fastqs path should point to the FASTQ directory for the current ATAC library.
  • R1/R2 FASTQ pairs should be placed directly under this directory.
  • Automatic detection relies on R1/R2 markers in file names. The recommended naming patterns are _R1/_R2 or _R1_/_R2_.
  • Do not mix data from different samples or different libraries in the same input directory.

Method 2: Explicit Individual FASTQ Inputs

$dnbc4tools atac run \
  --name sample \
  --fastq1 /data/sample_R1.fastq.gz \
  --fastq2 /data/sample_R2.fastq.gz \
  --genomeDir /opt/database/Mus_musculus \
  --threads 10

docs.title: Multi-Sample Batch Processing (Optional)
docs.text:
To simplify the analysis of multiple samples, you can use a configuration file to generate a shell script for each sample.

$dnbc4tools atac multi \
  --list sample.tsv \
  --genomeDir /opt/database/Mus_musculus \
  --threads 10

The sample.tsv file is tab-separated (\t) and contains two columns:

Column Content Description 1 Sample Name Unique sample identifier (e.g., sample1) 2 Library Sequencing Data Paired FASTQs, R1;R2 format, multiple files per read separated by commas ,

Note: Multiple FASTQ files within one end should be separated by commas (,), and R1/R2 files by semicolons (;).

sample1 /data/sample1_R1.fq.gz;/data/sample1_R2.fq.gz
sample2 /data/sample2_R1.fq.gz;/data/sample2_R2.fq.gz
sample3 /data/sample3_1_R1.fq.gz,/data/sample3_2_R1.fq.gz;/data/sample3_1_R2.fq.gz,/data/sample3_2_R2.fq.gz

After execution, a shell script is generated for each sample:

sample1.sh
sample2.sh
sample3.sh

Example content of sample1.sh:

$cat sample1.sh
/opt/software/dnbc4tools3.2/dnbc4tools atac run --name sample1 --fastq1 /data/sample1_R1.fq.gz --fastq2 /data/sample1_R2.fq.gz --genomeDir /opt/database/Mus_musculus --threads 10

You can then execute these scripts to run the main analysis.
